t: ― 2nd visit (August 2023) ―
I went to eat here in August 2023 😊　This is about a year after the previous time 😁

I actually wanted to go to an Okinawa soba shop I'd never eaten at, and I was driving from the north toward the south looking for one, but in the end the time for an errand was approaching, so I decided to go into this one, which was plain tasty when I ate it last time lol
Kenpa no Subaya (near Naha Shintoshin Park)

It was lunchtime and bustling with local customers and tourists, and I didn't have much time, so for a moment I thought, "Will this take quite a while? Should I leave?", but thinking "I might just make it?", I ordered the "Nankotsu Suba (regular size)" at the meal ticket machine.
After that, I secured a counter seat along the wall.

When I ate here last time I didn't really notice (my powers of observation are way too lacking (^_^;)), but I realized the walls are plastered with tons of autographs from celebrities and famous people from Okinawa Prefecture (^_^;)
The autographs posted at the wall-side counter where I happened to sit
Looking at the autographs one by one, what suddenly caught my eye, although the autograph is from a while back, was none other than Norika Fujiwara's autograph 😊

*I only noticed while writing this blog now, but the autograph posted below Norika Fujiwara's was from Yoko Gushiken, the former world boxing champion I respect, a star of the people of Okinawa Prefecture known by the nickname "Kanmuri Washi (Crested Serpent Eagle)" (^_^;)
Norika Fujiwara's autograph (sorry, I only noticed while writing the blog, so I didn't take a photo of Yoko Gushiken's autograph posted below it and can't show it lol)

Several people had ordered before me, so I'd braced myself that it would take a fair amount of time, but in about the time it took to gaze at the autographs on the wall for a bit, the "Nankotsu Suba (regular size)" I ordered came out.
This sense of speed, where you order quickly and it comes out quickly, is great ✌　My rating went up 😁
This is about other shops, but in the past I've experienced Okinawa soba shops that took quite a long time after ordering, even though they were popular shops, so I got a very good impression 😊
Nankotsu Suba (regular size)　¥850
As expected, this clear broth of "Kenpa no Subaya" is distinctive and nice 😊

Like last time, this clear broth and the thin noodles feel so "Kenpa no Subaya", nice. First, a sip of the standard broth; as always, there's no doubt it's a delicious broth with the bonito stock coming through 😊
The noodles are plain tasty too. After savoring the plain bonito-stock broth, I added Kenpa's kōrēgūsu (chili-infused awamori) that was on the table to change up the flavor.

This is plain tasty too 😋　Next, the soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) topping. They're tender and plain tasty in flavor, but not super melt-in-your-mouth, and there were sinewy soft-bone ribs in there too, so they had chewiness, and the sinewy meat got stuck between my teeth, so I needed a toothpick's help too (^_^;)

Rating (10/15): Plain tasty 😊　As expected, with the recent rise in prices, it seems the price has gone up compared to a year ago. The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) felt a bit sinewy, and I needed a toothpick to get the meat stuck in my teeth lol　I think it's plain tasty, so how about it when you come to Naha Shintoshin for sightseeing and such?
― 1st visit (May 2022) ―
I went to eat here in May 2022 😊

On the official website it says: [The concept of our soba making is "harmony". To bring out a harmonious flavor, we repeated failure over and over again, yet without giving up and without compromise, we finally arrived at the unshakable golden ratio of pork, bonito and salt.

The golden (kugani) broth, finished over 2 days, has depth within its clarity; with the faintly fragrant bonito flavor and an exquisite level of salt, it is a bowl of soul made by summoning every ounce of our strength.]
They're really particular about the broth 😊
Kenpa no Subaya (near Naha Shintoshin Park)
I ordered the "Seared Nankotsu Green Onion Suba".
Menu
Seared Nankotsu Green Onion Suba　¥800

The clear, transparent broth that you don't see much at other shops has the gentle taste of bonito stock. After drinking about half the broth, I enjoy changing up the flavor with homemade chili oil 😊　The flavor change is a nice accent lol　The noodles are also ramen-like, a thin noodle type, plain tasty.
Rating (9/15): Plain tasty 😊　How about it when you come to Shintoshin for sightseeing and such?

森の家.name: Mori no Ie
森の家.desc: A shop tucked quietly away in the forest of Izumi. Look for the arched gate guarded by shisa and the handmade mailbox. The everything-on-top "Mix Soba" is a big-volume bowl with pig's feet (tebichi), pork spare ribs (soki), braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) and a boiled egg. Great for a drive in cherry blossom season, too.
t: *This article was created with AI (ChatGPT 5.1 Thinking) and partly added to by me 😆

I ate here in February 2025 😄　As you drive up the winding road toward the mountains of Izumi in Motobu Town, the surroundings are nothing but forest, to the point where you get a little nervous wondering, "Is there really a shop up ahead…?" 🌿　Along the way the Taiwan cherry blossoms happened to be in bloom, deep pink puffs floating up here and there, a view that made me want to stop the car and just gaze at it 🌸　Appearing quietly in the middle of that forest is the Okinawa soba shop I visited this time, "Mori no Ie".
Mori no Ie (it's seriously in the middle of the forest 😆)
Mori no Ie (it's seriously in the middle of the forest 😆)
Mori no Ie (it's seriously in the middle of the forest 😆)
Cherry blossoms along the road near the shop lol
Cherry blossoms along the road near the shop lol

Walking toward the shop, the first thing that catches your eye is an arched gate guarded by shisa. The stone paving underfoot has a swirling pattern, and it somehow feels like you've wandered into a secret garden 🙂　The surroundings are full of trees and plants, truly a "house in the forest" just like the name. Next to the entrance sits a colorful mailbox with a very handmade feel, and it was so cute it got me excited 📮
Inside the shop
Inside the shop
Inside the shop
Inside the shop

Stepping inside, there's a glossy wooden floor lined with rattan chairs and wooden tables. Near the ceiling there's a display that makes use of branches just as they are, and in the center there's even a large aquarium. It's a strangely calming space, like a slightly retro coffee shop, a mountain hut and an art space all mixed together.
Menu
Menu

Opening the menu, in addition to the standards like soki soba, braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) soba and pork offal (nakami) soba, there were unusual ones like beef soba and even beef curry soba, which surprised me a bit. There's also a kids' soba, so it seems easy to come with the family. For drinks, they have coffee, tea, fruit juice, and Orion Beer properly on the lineup too 🍺　I hesitated over a lot of things, but this time I ordered the "Mix Soba", which was labeled a "Recommended Popular Menu Item". It's what you'd call an everything-on-top bowl.
Mix Soba (medium)　¥1,000

After waiting a little while, the Mix Soba arrived generously piled in a large bowl. Pig's feet (tebichi), pork spare ribs (soki), braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), a boiled egg, shiitake mushrooms, kelp, green onions… there was so much topping you could barely see the noodles, and the moment I saw it I let out an "Ohhh!" 😆　First, a sip of the broth. It seems to be a blended stock of bonito and pork bone, and the bonito broth really comes through. The shiitake stock is also strong, and it reminded me of the flavor at "Papa Subu" in Ginowan City.
Mix Soba (medium)　¥1,000
The noodles are medium-thick and straight. The texture is not too soft, but not rock-hard firm either, right down the middle.

The meats have plenty of presence, just as they look. The pig's feet (tebichi) were jiggly, and the fat was melt-in-your-mouth ✨　The seasoning on the pork spare ribs (soki) and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) was light across the board. A sinewy texture remains here and there.

The boiled egg topping might be a point unique to this place, too. Rather than a seasoned egg, it's an old-fashioned, firmly hard-boiled egg, with a half plopped right on top, a style you don't see much at other shops, so it felt a little fresh 🥚

The direction of the flavor is, if anything, on the ordinary side. It's well balanced and easy to eat, but I didn't really feel a strong personality or impact like "you can only eat this here!", that's my impression 🤔　But in exchange, the pairing with the location is outstanding. Outside the window, green spreads out everywhere, and when you step outside after eating, time flows leisurely, with only the sound of birds and the wind to be heard.

Rating (9/15): It's ordinary. I think it's the perfect shop for people who want to step a little away from the busy areas in the heart of the tourist spots and slurp Okinawa soba at a relaxed pace in the forest. Dropping by on a drive in cherry blossom season, or deliberately going on a rainy day to soak in this moist atmosphere: enjoying it together with the scenery may be the tastiest way to enjoy "Mori no Ie" 🚗🌳

花村そば.name: Hanamura Soba
花村そば.desc: A shop in Seragaki, Onna Village, along National Route 58. The signature dish is the ¥800 Hanamura Soba with a blended broth of pork bone, chicken, bonito and kelp. Next door is the attached pottery studio "Unna-yaki", where you can enjoy picking out souvenirs like yachimun pottery and shisa. A shop overflowing with Okinawan vibes, where customers on their way back from diving also stop by.
t: *This article was also made with the help of AI (Claude 3.5 Sonnet), and I added to and updated part of it myself lol
I ate here in June 2024 😄

This time I'm introducing "Hanamura Soba" in Seragaki, Onna Village. At this spot with a superb view surrounded by blue sky and sea, I had an encounter with Okinawa soba that soothed both body and soul. 🌴
Hanamura Soba (along National Route 58; the sea spreads out on the opposite side)
Hanamura Soba (along National Route 58; the sea spreads out on the opposite side)

The first thing that jumps out at you is the "Hanamura Soba" sign standing out against the blue sky. Combined with the tropical palm trees, for tourists, it seems the Okinawan mood will already be at its peak right here 🌺

Entering the shop, there's a calm atmosphere where you can feel the warmth of wood. Looking at the menu, I just couldn't help ordering the "Hanamura Soba", which shares its name with the shop and seems to be the signature dish. 🤤
Hanamura Soba (inside the shop)
Menu
Menu (maybe because there are lots of inbound tourists, there's English on it too)
Menu (maybe because there are lots of inbound tourists, there's English on it too)
And now, the long-awaited "Hanamura Soba" makes its appearance! 🎉
Hanamura Soba　¥800

First, let's taste the broth. The stock, combining pork bone, chicken, bonito, kelp and more, has a gentle pork bone flavor coming through. Though it's a complex flavor, it's a gentle taste that somehow feels nostalgic. It wraps you in an indescribable sense of happiness. 😌
Hanamura Soba　¥800

Next, let's taste the noodles. The medium-thick straight noodles are just moderately soft. It's a texture typical of Okinawa soba, and they go perfectly with the broth. The glossiness of the noodles lifted with chopsticks is enough to make you swoon. 😍

And pay attention to the toppings too. Both the braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) and pork spare ribs (soki) are simmered until tender. The savory flavor of the meat fills your whole mouth. With fish cake (kamaboko) and chopped green onions added, the colors are vivid too. 🥩🥕
To be honest, you might say the taste is "very, very ordinary". But the great location in the tourist area of Onna Village multiplies the appeal of "Hanamura Soba" many times over.

Looking around the shop, it's bustling with tourists. Interestingly, there were also customers still wearing wetsuits, apparently on their way back from diving, enjoying Okinawa soba at the outdoor tables. The ocean side of the national highway is the sea, and because there's planting along the road, you can't see the sea directly from the shop, but the very Okinawan scene made me smile without thinking. 🏊‍♂️😄
Actually, "Hanamura Soba" has one more attraction. Next to the shop, there's an attached workshop dealing in traditional Okinawan crafts. 🏺
The pottery room next to the shop

Even though it's a soba shop, very Okinawan items like shisa and ceramics are lined up crammed into every corner. After enjoying your Okinawa soba to the fullest, I also recommend taking your time to enjoy choosing souvenirs. 🛍️

Rating (9/15): So, how was the Okinawa soba at "Hanamura Soba"? It's a lovely shop where you can enjoy a superb location and Okinawan culture. 😊　Overall, the taste is ordinary, but the great location and the attached workshop are a big draw. 🌊🏺　When you visit on a trip, please do stop by! Nearby there's "Nakamura Soba", which I recommend and have introduced, but if that one is crowded, how about this one instead? I think you can leisurely soak up the Okinawan mood 😄

I lulu cafe.name: I lulu cafe
I lulu cafe.desc: A Thai food cafe along National Route 58. Its specialty is the "Thai-style Okinawa soba", with a pho-like chicken broth topped with shibui (winter melon), chicken thigh and cilantro. You can also change up the flavor with lemon juice, fish sauce and chili. A stylish shop that also sells clothes in the next room.
t: I went to eat here in November 2023 😊　It was during the "13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (2023.10.1–2024.2.29)", so I wanted to eat at a participating shop, but unluckily both of the two shops I went to were temporarily closed, so although it's not a stamp rally shop, I decided to eat at this shop that I'd been curious about for a while.
"I' LULU CAFE" along National Route 58

I'd seen this shop every time I drove along Route 58, but what concerned me was the parking. I'd thought you could park a few cars in front of the shop entrance, but looking carefully this time, it seemed difficult.
So while I was thinking "What should I do?", I noticed something that looked like a parking lot a little way off.
Shared parking lot with a ramen shop and others (a few meters south of I' LULU CAFE)
There were signs for several shops on the sign at the entrance, and looking carefully, on a small ocher-based sign was the name "I' LULUCAFE" too 🤗

However, the time I went this time was right at lunchtime, and with space for about 5 cars, and it being a parking lot shared by several shops, it was completely full. (The ramen shop next door seems to be popular too.)
But after waiting a little, a space opened up, and I somehow managed to park.
I entered the shop and ordered the "Thai-style Okinawa soba". While waiting, I checked out the menu 😊
Menu
Menu
Menu (hardcore Thai food lol　I want to eat khao man gai and gapao rice lol)
Menu (there's the Thai-style Okinawa soba)
Menu (tropical-looking drinks)
Menu
After looking through the menu and glancing around the shop, I saw an entrance leading to the next room.
When I went in, it seemed they also sell clothes, perhaps an original brand. It had a stylish feel 🤗
When I went into the room next to I' LULU CAFE, they were also selling clothes from an original brand?
After a while, the "Thai-style Okinawa soba" came 😁
Thai-style Okinawa soba　¥900

There were various condiments next to the soba. The staff explained that they're lemon juice, sugar, chili and fish sauce, and to add them to taste. Thai cooking condiments, this is a new kind of Okinawa soba not found at other shops lol
First I wanted to taste the broth as is, so I took a sip without adding anything.
"?" It's completely different from the Okinawa soba broths I've had so far. A flavor I'd never tasted before.

I learned about this shop when I saw it featured in the newspaper, and when I checked the newspaper article I'd snapped a photo of, it said that rather than the standard bonito and pork stock used in the usual Okinawa soba broth, it seems to be the broth used in a dish called pho, a chicken stock. A new broth, different from the Okinawa soba I've had until now.
Thai-style Okinawa soba　¥900

Next I had the noodles. They're thick, straight, on-the-soft-side noodles. The topping is shibui (winter melon), soft and well soaked in flavor. Since shibui was also a topping at "Okinawa Soba Papaya to Subui" in Uruma City, which I introduced before, it reminded me of that.

The meat is chicken thigh rather than pork, and tender. There was cilantro in it too, and it was probably my first time eating it (;^ω^); I think it's an ingredient people either love or hate, but I didn't notice any particularly strong taste or aroma and ate it just fine lol　I have a dumb tongue lol

Partway through, I added the Thai condiments (lemon juice, fish sauce, chili) and enjoyed changing up the flavor. Maybe I added too little lemon juice and fish sauce, since I didn't feel much change. But the chili, maybe I put in too much, because from partway through I was eating with sweat pouring out (;^ω^)　Spicy.
Rating (9/15): A new kind of Okinawa soba. The Okinawa soba I know has turned into Thai food 😊　How about everyone trying this Okinawa soba at least once?

OKINAWA SOBA HITOTSU.name: OKINAWA SOBA HITOTSU
OKINAWA SOBA HITOTSU.desc: A stylish shop like a bar with exposed concrete. The signature is the Special Hitotsu Soba, with a blended broth of chicken, pork and bonito, topped with sea lettuce (āsa) and yushi-dofu (soft Okinawan tofu).
t: I ate here in October 2023. This shop was a participant in the "13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (2023.10.1–2024.2.29)", and I went as my 7th of 34 shops 😊
OKINAWA　SOBA　HITOTSU　Without the "Okinawa soba" banner flags, the stylish exterior doesn't look like an Okinawa soba shop at all 😊
There were other customers, so I couldn't take photos inside, but the exposed-concrete building had a stylish feel, somehow like a bar 😁
For my order, I decided on the "Special Hitotsu Soba" introduced in the stamp rally booklet 😊
Menu 1
Menu 2
Special Hitotsu Soba (medium) ¥900

The "Special Hitotsu Soba" came lol　First, the broth of course lol　After tasting the broth a few times with my spoon, I thought that within the blended stock of chicken, pork, bonito and so on, the pork bone was subtly winning out a little?

However, when I researched the shop after finishing eating, they had an Instagram, and on that Instagram it was described as "○Bonito broth on the other side of ○○ the chicken and pork soup○✨A soak-into-you style Okinawa soba✨" (;^ω^)

Maybe it's my dumb tongue, but I didn't feel the bonito was particularly strong. However, since the "Special Hitotsu Soba" has "yushi-dofu (soft Okinawan tofu)" as a topping, I also thought maybe its liquid combines with the broth so you get this kind of taste (;^ω^)　Sorry, I'm just guessing lol
Next I had the noodles 🙏 The noodles are a thin straight type, with a soft feel.
Special Hitotsu Soba (medium) ¥900

When I ate the sea lettuce (āsa) topping ("āsa" is what Okinawans call the seaweed "hitoegusa". It clings to rocks in the shallows along Okinawa's coast, and it's apparently in season and delicious from February to May. It's rich in dietary fiber, minerals and calcium, and especially packed with beta-carotene, so it seems to be effective for anti-aging and cancer prevention too. It apparently has about 8 times the calcium of milk and about 2 times the folic acid of spinach (according to info from Nakamura Soba)) tangled with the thin straight noodles, I could taste the aroma and flavor of the āsa 🤗
The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) were jiggly and tender, well soaked in flavor and delicious 😁
Rating (9/15): Plain tasty. The inside of the shop has a stylish atmosphere like a bar.
*The shop has no parking lot, so you'll have to park at a coin parking lot nearby.

nomaclo（ノマクロ）.name: nomaclo (Nomakuro)
nomaclo（ノマクロ）.desc: An Okinawa soba shop like a select shop, with gentle white walls and wooden textures. The everything-on-top Nomakuro Soba with a creamy, cloudy white pork bone broth comes with freshly fried tempura. You can also enjoy hand-drip coffee and oden.
t: *This article was created with AI (ChatGPT 5 Thinking) and partly added to by me 😆
I ate here in January 2025 😄🌺 I went to "Nomaclo (Nomakuro)" in Onaga, Nishihara Town.
Nomaclo (Nomakuro)
Nomaclo (Nomakuro)
The banner flag is simple and stylish too 😆

First of all, the thread-like logo on the noren (shop curtain) is cute, and it suits the exterior with its gentle white walls and wooden textures perfectly. It's an Okinawa soba shop, but beyond the glass door there's also the atmosphere of a select shop, and it feels like everything is pulled together in the world of "Nomaclo = Nomakuro".
Menu
Menu
Menu
Menu
Menu
Menu
Menu

When I sat down, the table guide said "Water is self-service" and "Please return your dishes to the return counter", a pleasant smartness like a cafe. There were also the business hours and an Instagram QR code, giving off a modern feel. Looking over the menu, besides Okinawa soba there were coffee, non-alcoholic drinks, craft beer, and the words "takeout available". On top of that there's "Nomakuro Oden" and "tebichi (pig's feet)" too, which got me a little excited. This time I ordered the "Nomakuro Soba (everything on top)", which shares the shop's name.
Nomakuro Soba (greedy all-toppings-on-top) ¥1,000

The bowl that arrived on a round tray first of all looks great in photos with its polka-dot pattern. The broth is a cloudy white pork bone stock type. Taking a sip, it's creamy. The savoriness of the bones spreads gently. It's on the rich track that reminds me of "Tsukikuruchi" in Uruma City, with depth too, and I felt it was carefully simmered.
Nomakuro Soba (greedy all-toppings-on-top) ¥1,000

The noodles are medium-thick and loosely curly. Lifted with chopsticks they shine glossily, and in your mouth they have a pleasant chewy spring that pushes back against your teeth. Thanks to the curls they coat themselves in broth, and when you slurp, the sweetness of the pork bone arrives softly at the same time. They're boiled on the slightly soft side, and combined with the creaminess of the broth, they create a "gentle sense of unity".

As the name says, the toppings are everything on top, and lively to look at too. The pig's feet (tebichi) are melt-in-your-mouth, and the jiggly bounce of the collagen is fun. The fat is well rendered, so you can eat it easily without feeling heavy. The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) are prepared lightly too, the gelatinous parts around the bone falling apart, and the more you chew the more the flavor seeps out. And what made me even happier was the white of the yushi-dofu (soft Okinawan tofu). Its silky softness that crumbles fluffily pairs perfectly with the milkiness of the broth, pulling the whole impression together into something much milder. The kelp and green onions add aromatic accents, and I also liked how the aftertaste doesn't get dull.

And on a small side plate, there was a little bit of freshly fried tempura. Two kinds, okra and chikuwa, with a thin batter that's light and crispy when you bite into it. Delicious 😋 Drinking a sip of broth, biting the tempura, then going back to the soba refreshes the flavor. The contrast in temperature is fun too, and it makes you feel like you got a little bonus. The contrast between the round tray and the small black plate looks great too 📷

The shop is new and clean, and the color scheme of the bright wood-grain tables with black spoons and dishes is stylish. Along the walls, carefully selected goods are lined up, with cups, fabric items and plants casually arranged, and I felt it would go over well with groups of women or on a date. There's a hand-drip coffee menu too, so it's nice that you can enjoy a cup after your meal.
Including the sense for presentation and tableware, the added value of the tempura, and the comfort of the shop, my satisfaction with the total experience is solidly high.
Rating (9/15): Next time it might be nice to also get the oden set or coffee and take my time. So, the taste lands at a calm "fairly tasty", but how about trying this shop at least once 🙂

yu-i FACTORY（ユーイファクトリー）.name: yu-i FACTORY (Yui Factory)
yu-i FACTORY（ユーイファクトリー）.desc: An ultra-rare shop open only once a month. The "Okinawa 82 (Habu) Soba", with a broth of bonito, pork, chicken and kelp plus habu snake stock, topped with simmered habu, can only be tasted here. Next door there's also a habu leather goods shop (*as of July 2025 it appears to be suspended; please check).
t: *This article was also made with the help of AI (Claude 4 Sonnet), and I added to and updated part of it myself lol
*As of July 2025, it's difficult for this shop to procure habu for the soba, and it seems they aren't doing their once-a-month opening, so I recommend checking in advance whether they're open 😆
I ate here in December 2024 😄

This time I'm introducing a shop where you can have an especially rare experience, even among my Okinawa soba tours 😄 I learned about it in the newspaper: "yu-i FACTORY" in Arakawa, Haebaru Town. This shop is an ultra-rare Okinawa soba shop that's open only once a month, an Okinawa soba shop that uses that "habu" snake as a topping 😄
yu-i FACTORY

The moment I saw the exterior, it was such a unique building that I thought, "What kind of facility is this?" 😅 It has a stylish construction that looks like a renovated container house, and at first glance it's a modern atmosphere you'd never take for an Okinawa soba shop.
Inside the shop
Menu
How to eat 82 (habu) soba
Limited-edition jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice) with habu stock (^0^;)
Inside the shop (habu liquor? 😄)
Inside the shop

When you enter the shop, there's "habu soba" 😆 The ultimate oddball soba you can only taste in Okinawa. As someone who goes around eating Okinawa soba, this is something I absolutely have to take on 👍

What I ordered this time was the "Okinawa 82 Soba (Habu Soba) Set" for ¥1,300. I also ordered the limited-quantity ¥300 "Jushi with Habu Stock" along with it. A combination of Okinawan representatives ✖️3 — Okinawa soba, jushi and habu — there can't be a more Okinawan menu than this 😂
82 Soba (Habu Soba) Set　¥1,300

First, as usual, I taste the broth. It's quite a unique broth said to combine bonito, pork, chicken, kelp, and habu stock. Taking a sip… honestly, none of the stocks stood out, and if I hadn't been told it was habu I wouldn't have known 😅 But maybe that actually makes it easier to drink.
82 Soba (Habu Soba) Set　¥1,300
Next I have the noodles. They're a medium-thick straight type, with a soft-ish texture. My impression is that they're plain tasty Okinawa soba noodles 😊

And then the simmered habu, which you could call the star this time! When I timidly picked it up with my chopsticks, it had a ton of small bones and less meat than I expected 😅 There was no smell or quirkiness at all, and surprisingly it had a light flavor. But eating it while picking out the small bones was a bit of a struggle 💦
The rafute was simmered until tender, but it felt like a little sinewy texture remained. Even so, it was a reassuring flavor as a standard Okinawa soba topping 😄
82 Jushi　¥300 (limited quantity)

And I also taste the limited-quantity "Jushi with Habu Stock". This one was lightly seasoned too, and finished so that you wouldn't know it had habu stock in it unless you were told. But the unique lingering aftertaste left in my mouth after eating (earthy?) may perhaps be a characteristic of habu 🤔
The shop's introduction panel
The shop's introduction panel
The shop's introduction panel
The shop's introduction panel

Finishing my meal and looking around, a habu leather goods shop was also open in the prefab building next door 😆 The wallets combining indigo dye and habu leather were really cool, and appealing as a very Okinawan souvenir too ✨
Next to the 82 soba shop there's also a shop dealing in habu leather goods
Next to the 82 soba shop there's also a shop dealing in habu leather goods
Next to the 82 soba shop there's also a shop dealing in habu leather goods (later, I couldn't forget how cool the indigo-dyed habu leather wallet was and ended up buying one (^0^;))
Next to the 82 soba shop there's also a shop dealing in habu leather goods
Being open only once a month is a rare business style. Okinawa soba using habu, an ingredient unique to Okinawa, was a precious experience you absolutely can't have anywhere else 😊

To be honest, judging by taste alone it felt like ordinary Okinawa soba, but considering this rarity and the value of the experience, I think it's a shop worth trying at least once. It's definitely worth visiting by aiming for the once-a-month opening 👍

Rating (8.5/15): The taste itself is ordinary, but it's a shop where you can have a precious experience available only here, even within Okinawa, using the unusual ingredient habu. Including the rarity of opening only once a month, I think it's worth trying at least once if you love Okinawa soba 😄 However, while eating it didn't seem to have any quirkiness, after finishing there was something — not the gamy smell like after eating goat soba, but earthy? — a feeling different from usual, so be careful (^0^;)

なかま食堂.name: Nakama Shokudo
なかま食堂.desc: A local diner along Route 58 in Nakama, Onna Village. Its signature is the soki soba (¥1,200), served with a huge spare rib on a separate plate that looks like part of a BBQ set. The round, udon-like straight noodles and the pork-bone-forward blended broth are distinctive too, making for a very photogenic bowl.
t: This article was created with AI (Chat GPT 4o) and partly supplemented by me 😁

I ate here in November 2024 😄 This time I visited “Nakama Shokudo” in Nakama, Onna Village. It is a nostalgic-feeling local diner, easy to spot by its orange noren (shop curtain) and the banners fluttering in the wind.
Nakama Shokudo
And waiting here was an Okinawa soba that sticks in your memory for its sheer visual impact.
Menu
Menu
My order that day was the “soki soba (¥1,200).” The moment I saw the tray being brought over, I couldn’t help but say “Wow!” 😅
Soki soba　¥1,200

Served on a separate plate from the soba was, believe it or not, a gigantic spare rib. It’s the size of something from a BBQ set, and it hardly looks like a “soki” at all. It grabs you with its impact before you’ve even taken a bite.

Now, let me start with the broth. It looks clear, but when I took a sip it had a mysteriously unusual flavor. I think it’s probably based on a blended broth, but the pork-bone flavor came through rather strongly. Even so, I felt it had a character a bit different from the broth of typical Okinawa soba.
Soki soba　¥1,200

And then the noodles. These surprised me a little. They weren’t the kind of noodles you often see in Okinawa soba — they were round, straight noodles! They look just like udon. The texture is on the soft side. It’s quite a rare type for Okinawa soba, and for a moment you almost get the illusion of “Wait, am I eating udon today?” (lol) But it has a strange charm that makes you think “this works too.”

The star of the show, the spare rib, is simply packed with volume without any complaint 💥 It’s seasoned well with a sweet sauce and simmered until falling apart. It’s so tender the meat slips right off the bone, the flavor soaks in thoroughly, and the meat alone is satisfying enough.
Inside the shop
There’s vinegar among the condiments 😆

The shop has a homey atmosphere, and it’s easy to see why there are so many tourists. Looking at the menu, there are plenty of soba set meals and side dishes too, so it seems like an easy diner to use for a daytime drink or with the family.

The taste is more “just plain tasty” than “superb!” Still, I’d like you to experience the combination of this spare rib’s looks with the distinctive noodles and broth at least once. It was a photogenic bowl that I think would go over well with tourists 📷
Rating (9/15): It’s just plain tasty. If you want to experience a “giant spare rib,” I definitely recommend the soki soba at Nakama Shokudo 🍜✨

畑すば.name: Haru Suba
畑すば.desc: A lone-house-in-the-middle-of-nowhere Okinawa soba shop in Yamada, Onna Village, down a forest road leading from Route 58 toward the Yamada Castle ruins (the name is read “Haru Suba”). A homey place with a pork-bone-forward broth, medium-thick straight noodles, and sweetly seasoned bone-in pork ribs that leave an impression.
t: I ate here in April 2024 😁
Haru Suba (On Route 58 in Yamada, Onna Village, there is a sign like the one in the photo on what looks like a narrow forest road, and if you enter from that road you end up here 😁)
Haru Suba
Haru Suba (It’s a shop with real character 😁)

Whenever I drove along Route 58, I always wondered about this shop, because there is a sign on what looks like a forest road leading to the “Yamada Castle ruins” in Onna Village (I’ve never been there (^0^;)), so this time I went to check it out 😆
Once you enter the forest road, it is relatively close.
Menu
The menu is small. It’s a homey kind of place 😄 I decided to order the “soki soba.”
Soki soba　¥800
I took a sip of the broth 😁 It has a pork-bone-forward broth. It’s ordinary 😆
Soki soba　¥800
Next, the noodles. They are medium-thick, straight, and on the soft side. The bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki) were also tender, and the sweet seasoning left an impression.

Rating (9/15): It’s ordinary. Although it’s close to the highway, it is where the road goes up into the hills, so it’s a lone-house-in-the-middle-of-nowhere kind of shop 😁 It’s in Onna Village, a tourist destination, so why not drop by once when you come to Onna Village?

そば処 一本松.name: Soba-dokoro Ipponmatsu
そば処 一本松.desc: A local diner tucked away in a residential area of Toyama, Urasoe City. By far the most popular dish is the “Stamina Soba,” a three-way platter of braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), and bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki). Its clear broth of pork bone, kelp, and bonito with a soft waft of garlic is a distinctive feature.
t: * This article was created based on AI (Chat GPT 5 Thinking) and partly supplemented by me 😁

This time I ate here in January 2025 😆 After circling around the residential area of Toyama, Urasoe City, I finally found “Soba-dokoro Ipponmatsu.” With its pure white exterior wall and the stately carved wooden sign, it looked so tasteful that I couldn’t help taking a photo 📸
Soba-dokoro Ipponmatsu

Next to it is a bright red vending machine, and potted plants at its feet add a little seasonal color. The atmosphere of a local diner is already drifting out from the entrance. Since it’s a bit off the main road, it’s easy to get lost on a first visit, but seeing the neighborhood people entering one after another the moment it opened, I thought “this is surely a winner” and my expectations rose steadily 😊
Inside the shop
Inside, the wooden tables and chairs are neatly polished, and along the wall are self-service water and tea, pickled red ginger, and condiments.
Menu

Opening the menu, there are rows of photos on yellow paper. The shop’s top recommendation, the “Stamina Soba” at ¥1,100, is prominently featured, and the “Ipponmatsu Soba,” which bears the shop’s name, is ¥750 for small and ¥850 for large, kids’ soba is ¥400, and yushi-dofu soba and yushi-dofu soup are ¥800 each. Rice is ¥100, jushi is ¥200, iced coffee is ¥200, and a medium bottle of beer is ¥550, so the prices are balanced in a way that is friendly to both tourists and locals 💴 Of course this time I ordered the by-far most popular No. 1, the “Stamina Soba.”
Stamina soba　¥1,100

The moment the black bowl arrived on a wooden tray, along with the steam came the soft scent of garlic layered over a blended broth of pork bone, kelp, and bonito flakes. First a sip... the broth feels clear in the mouth, and the outline of the bonito steps smoothly to the front 🐟
Stamina soba　¥1,100
The noodles are medium-thick with a gentle wave, boiled on the soft side so they slide down easily 🍜

The toppings are a stamina trio worthy of the name. The star, the meat, comes as a three-kind platter, occupying half the bowl with hefty, chunky presence. The braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) is well seasoned with a rather strong sinewy texture. The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) are melt-in-your-mouth and light, so soft that even the bouncy collagen becomes one with the meat, and I was impressed by how cleanly the fat breaks. The bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki) have the fat trimmed for an elegant finish, though they too have a strong sinewy bounce 🥢 Partway through I sprinkled on the free fuchiba (mugwort) 🌿

My overall impression is “a satisfying soba that stays close to everyday life.” Locals gather right from opening time, and it’s nice that the shop’s secluded location deep in the residential area keeps a calm atmosphere 🏡
Rating (9/15): However, in terms of the flavor of Okinawa soba, it ends up settling at “just plain tasty” after all 😌 Why not try this shop at least once? 😆

我如古そば.name: Ganeko Soba
我如古そば.desc: A traditional diner in Gusukuma, Urasoe City. Its signature is the Ganeko soba, with a gentle, translucent pork-bone broth and thick, wavy noodles. There is also a free fried chicken service on Saturdays and a free jushi service on the 14th of every month. A popular local spot with a full lineup of set meals.
t: * This article was created by AI (Claude Opus 4.5) with some additions and updates by me 😆 I ate here in February 2025 😄

This time I visited “Ganeko Soba” in Gusukuma, Urasoe City! Looking at the exterior, the words “Ganeko Soba” on the wooden sign are striking. A pink noren hangs at the entrance, giving off the feel of an old-fashioned Okinawa soba shop 🏠
Ganeko Soba

Inside, the two-tone orange and blue walls stand out, and it has a nostalgic diner style. A few table seats are lined up, and handwritten menu items like “tebichi nitsuke (braised pig’s feet),” “nakami soba,” and “tebichi soba” are posted on the walls ✨
Inside the shop
Menu
Menu
Menu

Looking at the menu, it’s not just Okinawa soba but a full lineup of set meals too. There is “braised pig’s feet set meal” ¥1,200, “soki soup” ¥1,200, “nakami soup” ¥890, “liver and vegetable set” ¥930, “ginger pork set” ¥950, “vegetable champuru” ¥850, “katsudon” ¥880, “champon” ¥880, and more — an abundant lineup typical of an Okinawan diner 🍽️

The Okinawa soba menu also offers plenty of variety: “soba set meal” ¥930, “Okinawa soba” ¥700, “sanmai-niku soba” ¥750, “soki soba” ¥800, “tebichi soba” ¥980, “nakami soba” ¥890, “mugwort soba” ¥800, “squid-ink soba” ¥800, and so on. Kids’ soba at ¥400 is also a nice point for families 👨‍👩‍👧

And I found a bargain campaign too! Every Saturday is “Fried Chicken Day,” with 2 pieces of fried chicken free with a soba order 🎉 Also, the 14th of every month is “Jushi Day,” with one bowl of jushi free with a soba order. You can apparently swap it for white rice if you like. Today happened to be the 14th, so I got the jushi as a free service! Lucky 😆
This time I ordered the “Ganeko Soba” (¥820), which shares its name with the shop. After a short wait, it was brought out together with the jushi 🍜
Ganeko soba　¥820 (* jushi free on the 14th)

In the bowl is a translucent pork-bone broth with thick, slightly wavy noodles. The toppings are two slices of braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki), fish cake (kamaboko), and green onions. It looks satisfying just by appearance 😋
First, a sip of the broth. It has the gentle flavor of pork-bone stock. It has no off-notes and is a comforting taste. The saltiness is just right, and it’s an easy-drinking broth.
Ganeko soba　¥820
Next, the noodles. They are thick, wavy noodles with a soft texture. A simple flavor typical of Okinawa soba 🍜

The braised pork belly and bone-in pork ribs toppings are both lightly seasoned. The braised pork belly has a decent balance of fat and lean, but has a bit of a sinewy texture. The bone-in pork ribs are the same: the seasoning is gentle, but there were parts where the sinew remained.
I also had the complimentary jushi. This too is lightly seasoned, like a simple Okinawan seasoned rice. Eating it together with the soba fills you right up 🍚

Looking around the shop, many local customers were coming in and it was lively. Many were ordering set meals, and I felt this is a shop beloved by the locals. It’s very ordinary Okinawa soba, but that “ordinary” is exactly what’s good about it 😊

Rating (9/15): It was a very ordinary, tasty Okinawa soba. It has no special distinguishing character, but it’s a reassuring bowl that makes you understand why the locals love it. With such a full set-meal lineup, you’ll want to try things other than Okinawa soba too. If you come to Urasoe City, why not drop by? 😊

鉢巻.name: Hachimaki
鉢巻.desc: A unique shop in the Koza streetscape with two faces: a soba shop by day and "Bar Samurai" by night (* it may have closed as of 2026). Look for the red gate and the words NEW YORK RESTAURANT. A gentle, light pork-bone soup and rare thin, wavy noodles.
t: * As of July 2026 it may have closed, so please be aware.
On this Okinawa soba journey, I'll introduce "Hachimaki" in Chuo, Okinawa City. I went to eat here in May 2025 😄

I visited "Hachimaki," in the streetscape of Koza in Chuo, Okinawa City. The exterior is quite unique: a gate like a red torii with the words "NEW YORK RESTAURANT," and red paper lanterns and decorations reading "Sakaba (tavern)" hanging from it, giving off a rather mysterious atmosphere 😊
Hachimaki (a unique exterior with a red gate as its landmark)

No wonder, since this shop actually also operates as a bar by night, under the name "Samurai (Bar Samurai)." Looking at the banners, as the soba shop "Hachimaki" it's open 11:00 am to 3:00 pm and 5:00 pm to 10:00 pm, and as the night bar "Samurai" from 10:00 pm to 5:00 am, truly a shop with two faces, day and night 🍶
Two faces: the soba shop "Hachimaki" by day, and Bar "Samurai" by night
Okinawa soba made by Otō (Dad)  Large ¥950  Medium ¥850

Inside, it's built just like a bar, with corrugated metal walls, a tapestry of a samurai under the moon, and red, pink, and green paper lanterns hanging, creating a unique world. There's a sofa seating area too, so it feels less like a daytime Okinawa soba shop and more like visiting a nighttime establishment 😅 There was even a sign saying "Weekdays only: karaoke, all-you-can-sing ¥500," which clearly conveys that nights are the main business.
Counter seats inside (with a sign for weekday-only all-you-can-sing karaoke ¥500)
The tapestry of the samurai under the moon and the paper lanterns create a unique world
There's sofa seating too, giving a nighttime-bar atmosphere
A samurai suit of armor is displayed too. As expected of Bar "Samurai"

Honestly, my impression is that Okinawa soba shops that are open at night often have strongly seasoned flavors, probably with a finishing bowl in mind. So I thought this one would be that kind too, but in a good way my expectations were betrayed.

Now, let's look at the menu. Okinawa soba (medium) ¥850, (large) ¥950, tebichi (pig's feet) soba ¥1,000, sets with jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice), and even jushi taco rice. This time I went with the classic and ordered the "Okinawa soba (large)" 🍜
Menu at the shop front
Menu (you can choose between wavy noodles and flat noodles)
Drink menu (a wide selection of awamori and sours too. You can tell nights are the main business)

And what's interesting is that you can choose the noodles from "wavy noodles" and "flat noodles." Since I was there, I asked the staff member for a recommendation, and they pushed the wavy noodles, so I obediently chose the wavy noodles.
After a while, the Okinawa soba (large) appeared! Topped with braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), egg, fish cake (kamaboko), and green onions, it's a very standard-looking bowl 😄
Okinawa soba (large)  ¥950

First, the soup. Mm, this is pork-bone based, but only a faint pork-bone flavor, a very gentle taste. Since it's a shop that's also open at night, I had braced myself for a strong flavor, so this was a welcome surprise. It's light and goes down smoothly.

Next, the noodles. The wavy noodles I chose are actually quite rare. I don't remember seeing thin, wavy noodles much in Okinawa soba. And they're finished soft. Since the soup is gentle, these thin wavy noodles seem to cling to it nicely.
Rare thin, wavy noodles. Finished on the soft side

Looking at the braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) topping, the flavor has soaked in moderately, which is nice. However, some parts still had a bit of sinewy texture. The egg and fish cake are the usual reliable supporting players.

Overall, in contrast to its unique appearance as a nighttime bar, "Hachimaki"'s Okinawa soba was a gentle, light, and, in a good way, ordinary bowl. The novelty of thin, wavy noodles was a small discovery 😊
Rating (9/15): While sightseeing in Koza, why not stop by "Hachimaki (Samurai)" and enjoy its two faces: Okinawa soba by day and a bar by night? 👋

マルヨ製麺（沖縄市）.name: Maruyo Seimen (Okinawa City)
マルヨ製麺（沖縄市）.desc: A shop run directly by a noodle factory near Kensō (Okinawa Prefectural Comprehensive Sports Park). The chewy in-house fresh noodles made with Okinawa-grown wheat are high-level, and the top pick is the "Yokubari Soba," topped with a whole-rib bone-in pork rib (hon-soki), soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku).
t: I ate here in September 2023 😁
Maruyo Seimen

This shop is relatively close to Kensō (Okinawa Prefectural Comprehensive Sports Park), but when I googled it, it seems to have shops in various places (;^ω^) This time, as usual without any research, I happened to find this place and went in.
The menu in front of the entrance
Looking at the menu sign in front of the shop entrance, the "Yokubari Soba" is introduced as the "shop's top pick."

It's described as "a luxurious dish topped with a bone-in pork rib (hon-soki) using one whole pork rib, soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku)." So my order is decided: this "shop's top pick, Yokubari Soba" 😊

It was lunchtime, but probably because it was a weekday, the shop was empty. Entering from the entrance, there's a ticket machine (cash only) near the entrance, and I bought the recommended "Yokubari Soba (medium)" and ordered it from a staff member.
On the table was a laminated sheet explaining what seem to be this shop's selling points, the "fresh noodles" and the "broth."

The explanation says, "Fresh noodles: chewy texture, smooth slurping, made with Okinawa-grown wheat" and "Broth: light yet rich and savory, a luxurious broth of seafood, chicken, and pork, superb with the in-house fresh noodles." Just reading the explanation makes it sound delicious 😋
After a while, the "Yokubari Soba" came.
Yokubari Soba, medium  ¥900

First, the soup 🤗 According to the explanation it's a blended broth of seafood, chicken, and pork, and since "seafood" came first, I assumed on my own that the bonito base would be strong and took a sip.
But the taste was somehow different from what I imagined? I took another sip to check. Again, it didn't seem like a bonito base? If anything, it felt like a chicken and pork base.
It's a tasty soup, but personally I would have liked a stronger seafood feel (;^ω^) But it's still ordinarily tasty.
Next, the fresh noodles. They're medium-thick straight noodles, and as described, they have a chewy texture, moderate springiness, and are smooth. Delicious noodles 😊
Is that something made from Okinawa-grown wheat kneaded into the noodles? You can see something worked into them.
The noodles Maruyo Seimen is proud of. You can tell the smooth, chewy feel even from the photo.

Rating (9.5/15): It's ordinarily tasty. I thought the fresh noodles in particular are high-level. I thought they're similar to and as high-level as "Kinchichi Soba" that I ate in Onna Village and "Suke Soba" that I ate in Ginowan City the other day. The soup is delicious and goes with the noodles, but personally I thought a stronger seafood style would be better. The toppings are tender but lightly flavored, so personally I'd prefer them to be more flavor-soaked. Why not try the fresh noodles made with Okinawa-grown wheat at least once?

沖縄そば 咲樹.name: Okinawa Soba Saki
沖縄そば 咲樹.desc: A popular local shop in Ganeko, Ginowan City. Its signature is the hearty Saki Soba, with a rather pork-bone-forward blended broth, medium-thick wavy noodles, and toppings of braised pork belly, bone-in pork ribs, and pork. A solid flavor loved by construction workers too.
t: * This article was created with AI (Chat GPT 4o) and partly supplemented by me 😆

I ate here in November 2024 😄 This time I went to “Okinawa Soba Saki” in Ganeko, Ginowan City 🌺. There was some construction in front of the shop with scaffolding set up, but a large banner saying it was open was clearly hung, so I could walk in without hesitation! I like this kind of thing; it feels loved by the local people 😊.
Okinawa Soba Saki (scaffolding was set up, maybe for exterior wall painting work 😄)
Okinawa Soba Saki (scaffolding was set up, maybe for exterior wall painting work 😄)
Inside, signed shikishi boards were lined up, and I realized “this is a famous shop even locally” ✨.
Inside the shop (it was full of customers so I couldn't photograph it well 🙏)

Now, this time I ordered the “Saki Soba,” which is also the name of the shop! The menu had various kinds of Okinawa soba and I hesitated, but you do get curious about the item bearing the shop's name 😋.
Menu
Menu
Saki soba, large　¥950

The Saki Soba that came out, large size at ¥950. Topped with a big slab of braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki), and tender-looking pork, it's full of volume! Pickled red ginger, green onions, and shredded egg add color, and it already looks delicious just by sight… 🤤.

When I took a sip of the broth, the blended stock of bonito and pork bone let me taste both. But the pork bone feels rather strong. No wonder many local construction workers visit. The flavor is solid, so it may be just right for those who want to eat heartily 👍.
Saki soba, large　¥950
The noodles are medium-thick wavy noodles, boiled on the soft side. Personally I'd like a bit more firmness, but the broth clings to them easily, so it's not bad. They go down with a slurp.

The braised pork belly topping is well-seasoned and finished on the sweet side. But it was a bit sinewy and firm, I think. It may be good for people who like a chewy bite, but I prefer it a bit softer 😉. The bone-in pork ribs seemed seared, with a slight smoky aroma, and were delicious! These too are sweetly seasoned, but simmered tender and easy to eat.

The shop was bustling with local customers, and that kind of atmosphere is nice. There's an air where you can chat a little and take your time, and you can feel it's loved not only by tourists but by locals too 😊.

Rating (9/15): Overall my impression is “just plain tasty!” The flavor is on the strong side, so eating it with rice or jushi would probably raise the satisfaction further ✨. Why not try this shop at least once too? 😆

石くびり.name: Ishikubiri
石くびり.desc: On the Soba Kaido (soba road), with a nostalgic look like a Showa-era diner. A popular shop with celebrity autographs covering an entire wall. Its chewy noodles and chewy fish cake, among the best of any Okinawa soba shop, shine. Its taro (ta-imo) dishes are certified as "100-Year Food" by the Agency for Cultural Affairs.
t: *This article was created with AI (ChatGPT-4o), with some additions of my own lol
I went to eat here in September 2024😄

On my Okinawa soba rounds, I visited "Ishikubiri" in Aza Higashi, Motobu Town. Using an afternoon of hourly leave, I came to this shop with an atmosphere just like a Showa-era diner. Even the exterior is well-worn, with a somehow nostalgic feel. It's a shop you can tell at a glance is loved by locals😊
Ishikubiri (there are two entrances)
Ishikubiri (there are two entrances)

When you step inside, celebrity autographs and newspaper articles covering an entire wall jump out at you, and you can tell it's a popular shop rooted in the community. There's also tatami seating, and it's a relaxed space as if you were at home✨
Inside the shop
Celebrity autographs posted in the shop
Menu
Menu (it seems their taro (ta-imo) dishes are famous too)

The menu has not only "Ishikubiri soba" but also "vegetable soba," "beef and bean sprout soba," and even "eel," so there's plenty of variety. But here, of course, I tried ordering the "Ishikubiri soba" bearing the shop's name. The price is a reasonable ¥800 too, and my excitement grew while I waited.
Ishikubiri soba ¥800

And out came the "Ishikubiri soba"🍜. First, when I took a sip of the broth, the pork bone comes through firmly, and the saltiness felt strong too. However, since it's a bit on the salty side, people watching their salt might find it a little heavy.
Ishikubiri soba ¥800

The noodles are medium-thick with a chewy texture, and they have such springiness that it makes you think, maybe they're house-made? These noodles that grab the broth well are very satisfying and very delicious👍 What especially moved me was the "fish cake (kamaboko)" topping! This fish cake has without a doubt the No.1 chewiness of all the Okinawa soba shops I've eaten at, and it surprised me into thinking, "Was kamaboko always this delicious?" Fish cake, which I don't usually pay much attention to, has a star-level presence here🌟

The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) and bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki) are also well seasoned through, and the umami of the meat spreads out. However, some slightly sinewy parts remain, so people looking for tenderness might mind that.

Rating (9/15): Just plain tasty😄 I thought the noodles and fish cake in particular were high-level. I thought the deliciousness of the fish cake is hard to find elsewhere, so why not give it a try once? As expected of a shop on the Okinawa Soba Kaido😄

沖縄料理と島どうふ TO-PU.name: Okinawa Ryori to Shima-dofu TO-PU
沖縄料理と島どうふ TO-PU.desc: Near Churaumi Aquarium, marked by a handmade sign on National Route 449. The shop name "Tōpu" means tofu shop in the Motobu dialect. Its signature dishes are handmade tofu prepared twice a day and the "Okinawa soba everything-on-top set meal" with an appetizer of three kinds of tofu.
t: I went to eat here in May 2024😄
"TO-PU Okinawa Ryori to Shima-dofu" (the building has no conspicuous sign, so it was hard to tell what it was😁)
There's a handmade sign along National Route 449😄
I learned about this shop when it was featured in a local newspaper.
It was featured in a local newspaper
According to the newspaper, the shop name "Tōpu" means tofu shop in the Motobu dialect, and their biggest selling point is handmade tofu prepared twice a day😁
The signature dish was introduced as the "Okinawa soba everything-on-top set meal," so I decided to order it.
Menu (the Okinawa soba everything-on-top set meal is introduced first, so you can tell it's the recommendation)
Menu
Menu
Menu
Menu
Inside was crowded at lunchtime, so I ate at a table outside.
Outdoor table (inside was crowded, so I went outside, but the mosquitoes bothered me (^0^;))
Okinawa soba everything-on-top set meal ¥1,200

The appetizer is handmade tofu in three kinds. I got to taste bite-size "okara," "yushi-dofu," and "shima-dofu." The staff explained that they're already seasoned, so please eat them without adding anything. Just plain tasty😆
The broth is a combined bonito and pork bone broth, with the pork bone coming through. Just plain tasty.
Okinawa soba everything-on-top set meal ¥1,200
Next, the noodles. They're medium-thick and straight, with a cross-section like flat noodles, and soft.
The braised pork belly and soki toppings were a little dry, and some parts had a remaining sinewy texture.
The yushi-dofu (soft Okinawan tofu) on top of the Okinawa soba is handmade, and fluffy and soft😁
Rating (9/15): Just plain tasty😄 It's bustling with both local customers and tourists. It's close to Churaumi Aquarium, so why not stop by here too?

おきなわ長寿そば.name: Okinawa Choju Soba
おきなわ長寿そば.desc: A blue shipping-container shop on National Route 449 near the Shiokawa bus stop. Its specialty is "Choju single-noodle soba," where kishimen-like flat noodles form one continuous strand filling the whole bowl. Changing up the flavor with a chili-oil-crisp-style condiment is fun too.

I ate here in December 2024😄 I visited "Okinawa Choju Soba" in Sakimotobu, Motobu Town😊
Okinawa Choju Soba
Okinawa Choju Soba

This shop operates near the Shiokawa bus stop on National Route 449, and according to a newspaper article it's committed to making Okinawa soba with lots of local ingredients. The exterior is a vivid blue container type, with a presence you can spot right away even from a distance. The green parasols are a landmark, and the colorful, very Okinawan atmosphere is lovely🏝️

What I ordered from the menu this time was, of course, the famous "Choju single-noodle soba" (¥1,200)! The newspaper article said something like 4.5 meters, but looking at it in person, maybe it's not quite that long? But it's definitely not the length of a normal noodle~😅 This single noodle has a flat shape like kishimen, and it's amazing that it really is made as one strand!
Choju single-noodle soba ¥1,200
Choju single-noodle soba ¥1,200

When you lift it with your chopsticks, the way it just keeps going and going is hugely impactful. However, unlike regular Okinawa soba, honestly this flat shape makes it hard to slurp😆 The noodle texture is chewy.

The broth seems to be a combined broth with plenty of pork bone. The umami of the pork bone comes out well, and it's finished with richness🍲 The toppings are three kinds: pig's feet (tebichi), bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki), and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku). The tebichi is simmered until meltingly tender, full of collagen and delicious! The hon-soki has a sweetish seasoning and a bit of sinewy texture, but it's satisfying in its own way. The braised pork belly is also finished meltingly tender, with a nice balance of fat and lean. On the side there's fish cake, and interestingly, a condiment like chili oil crisp. Adding this partway through changes the taste of the broth so you can enjoy it two ways, which I think is a good idea🌶️
Condiments

The location is Sakimotobu, Motobu Town, near the Shiokawa bus stop on National Route 449. Since it's a mobile food vendor, the hours and location may change, so it might be better to check in advance. There's parking for a few cars in front of the shop, but it's along the road, so be careful. The eating area is open-air, covered by a green tent, with colorful picnic tables lined up, so you can enjoy your meal in a resort mood. It looks especially pleasant on sunny days☀️

The menu is wide-ranging too, from the standard Okinawa soba to soki soba, yushi-dofu soba, and more, reasonably priced at ¥800 for medium and ¥950 for large. There are set menus too; the jushi set is ¥1,000 medium and ¥1,150 large. There's also an unusual "ASIA yakisoba" for ¥1,000, which piqued my curiosity🍝 The drink menu is extensive too, so you can enjoy very Okinawan drinks like Okinawa green juice smoothies and mango smoothies. Acerola soda and shikuwasa soda are Motobu Town recommendations as well, and it's nice to be able to enjoy local flavors🥤

Rating (9/15): The single noodle at "Okinawa Choju Soba" definitely makes for an impactful experience! The taste was plainly tasty too, and it was a warm shop where you can feel love for the local area. I think the unusual single-noodle style is worth experiencing at least once😊 It's a slightly different way of eating from regular Okinawa soba, but that was all part of a fun experience. When you're heading toward Motobu, please do stop by!🌺

マルヨ製麺 塩屋店.name: Maruyo Seimen Shioya Branch

The "greedy soba" topped with bone-in pork ribs, soft-bone pork ribs, and braised pork belly is popular.

沖縄そば家 まる良.name: Okinawa Soba-ya Maruyoshi
沖縄そば家 まる良.desc: A shop in Kanna, Ginoza Village, that opened in summer 2024 (*closed in May 2025). Its distinctive feature was choosing between Chinen Seimenjo's wavy noodles and Sankakuya Seimenjo's Nago soba noodles, and its crunchy soft-bone pork ribs were unique too. I'm keeping the article as a record.
t: *This shop appears to have closed on May 7, 2025. What a shame.
This time I'm introducing "Okinawa Soba-ya Maruyoshi" in Kanna, Ginoza Village. I went to eat here in March 2025😄
Okinawa Soba-ya Maruyoshi
Okinawa Soba-ya Maruyoshi

Ginoza Village is an area a bit north of central Naha, and I stopped by as part of a drive up north. When you enter the parking lot, several banner flags are standing, and you can see at a glance that there's plenty of space. The building is relatively new, with a clean white exterior; above the glass door hangs a banner reading "Okinawa Soba-ya Maruyoshi," and there was an "Open" notice at the entrance too😄
The parking lot is big lol
Inside, the interior is bright and simple, with table seats lined up. Panels explaining the types of noodles are posted on the wall, and this shop's big feature is that "you can choose your noodles"🎉
Inside the shop (near the entrance)
Noodle description panel posted on the shop wall
Noodle description panel posted on the shop wall
Menu

Opening the menu, it's set up so you can choose from two kinds of noodles: one is Chinen Seimenjo's "Chinen soba (wavy noodles)" and the other is Sankakuya Seimenjo's "Nago soba (thin, straight noodles)." Chinen soba is satisfying, characterized by chewy springiness and wavy noodles that snap off with a pop, while Nago soba is a firm straight noodle widely used in northern Okinawa, with reliable deliciousness. I was curious about both, but this time I followed the staff's recommendation and chose Chinen Seimenjo's "wavy noodles."

Besides an orthodox lineup of soki soba, braised pork belly soba, pig's feet (tebichi) soba, soft-bone pork rib soba, and so on, I was also curious about an unusual one, the "vegetable soba" limited to 5 servings a day😁 The vegetable soba is a Maruyoshi-style dish topped with garlic-flavored stir-fried garlic chives, carrots, bean sprouts, cabbage, and pork, so I'd like to try it next time. This time I ordered the "Maruyoshi soba (medium)." You can also choose the noodle amount from small 150g, medium 200g, or large 250g, which is nice for people who want to eat heartily.
Looking at the Maruyoshi soba that was brought out after a while, it was a visibly hearty bowl, packed with toppings starting with the soft-bone pork ribs😋
Maruyoshi soba, medium (Chinen Seimenjo's wavy noodles) ¥900

First, the customary gulp of broth. It's bonito-broth-based, and I got the impression it's finished quite rich compared to other shops😊 But rather than a standout personality, my impression was of plainly tasty bonito broth.
Maruyoshi soba, medium (Chinen Seimenjo's wavy noodles) ¥900

Next, I try the wavy noodles I chose. Eating them, they were finished on the soft side overall. They had the popping texture typical of wavy noodles, but personally I felt they could have had a bit more springiness🍜

When I picked up the soft-bone pork ribs topping with my chopsticks, the cartilage part had a really crunchy texture, a type you rarely get at other shops😲 While many shops simmer their soft-bone ribs until meltingly tender, Maruyoshi's cartilage keeps a firm texture, and I thought it's rare for it to be this crunchy. It may divide opinions. On the other hand, the meat part has a bit of sinewy texture.

Rating (9/15): Overall, honestly, I'd say it's average~. It's a soba shop rooted in the community here in the Kanna area of Ginoza Village✨ It also has a bit of personality, with the fun of choosing your noodles and the crunchy soft-bone pork ribs, so why not stop by when you're on a drive up north?😊

"Kai Soba" on Pipeline Street
With no plan as usual, I was driving along Pipeline wondering, "Is there an Okinawa soba shop around?" when I suddenly found this place and went in lol

Menu

Menu: Kai Soba's commitments are explained

なりそば.name: Nari Soba
なりそば.desc: A self-service Okinawa soba shop operating unstaffed 24 hours a day. An automatic door that closes using plastic-bottle weights, a broth dispenser, and complimentary all-you-can-eat jushi or curry; its one-of-a-kind system feels fresh. A shop that runs on trust.
t: I ate here in October 2023. This shop was a participant in the "13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (2023.10.1–2024.2.29)," and I went as my 11th shop out of 34😊
Nari Soba: it's close to Tori Ojisan
The stamp rally booklet described it as "operating unstaffed 24h," so the system had me thinking "?", but once I went inside, I figured out a lot😊

It's quite novel lol What first made me laugh was the shop door (lol) After you open the sliding door, it closes automatically, and believe it or not, the power comes from the gravity of weights in plastic bottles lol The person who came up with it is amazing (lol)
They put water in plastic bottles so the shop's entrance door closes automatically under the weight lol Since it's open 24h, maybe it's to stop late-night drunks from leaving it open? Quite novel lol
You order by buying a ticket from the meal ticket machine with cash; I hope they switch to cashless soon.
Above the meal ticket machine there were instructions on how to make curry soba. Since it's unstaffed 24h, it's self-service lol Curry soba reminds me of Akainko in Nago😁
How the Okinawa soba is prepared. Like the Okinawa soba side dishes at bento shops, it's already prepared in disposable containers.
To the left is a machine for pouring Okinawa soba broth. It's my first self-service Okinawa soba shop, so it's novel and exciting lol

This time I ordered Okinawa soba for ¥600, and believe it or not, they said it comes with complimentary jushi (Okinawan-style seasoned rice) or curry rice for free. This is self-service too, so you're handed a container and can eat whichever dish you like, in whatever amount🙁
This rice cooker is labeled "Kinmai" (gold rice). That didn't tell me much (;^ω^)
When I opened the lid of the rice cooker, it was yellow rice.
This is the rice cooker with jushi, which is eaten in Okinawa at celebrations, grave visits, and other occasions
Jushi (Okinawan-style seasoned rice). It looks delicious, but this time I asked for curry rice as my freebie lol
Curry: a generous amount ready for 24h service😁
Okinawa soba ¥600. The curry in the photo is self-serve, so you can adjust the amount, and it's complimentary (free).
First, a gulp of the Okinawa soba broth. Is this broth strongly pork-bone-based? As expected, it's like the Okinawa soba side dishes sold at bento shops.
The noodles are a loosely wavy type, and the braised pork belly is soft too; just plain tasty. As in the earlier photo it's stored refrigerated, but with the hot broth it feels freshly made lol
Okinawa soba ¥600: it feels like the Okinawa soba side dish at a bento shop

Rating (9/15): Just plain tasty. I imagine there are security cameras, but operating unstaffed 24h is a system that works because of trust with customers lol It's my first Okinawa soba shop with a system like this, so why not give it a try once?

沖縄そば SOBA DAY.name: Okinawa Soba SOBA DAY
沖縄そば SOBA DAY.desc: A counter-only shop run by an owner who trained at my recommended shop "EIBUN." The shop name comes from "Okinawa Soba Day" on October 17. The signature is the double-meat soba, with chashu, braised pork belly, and fu (wheat gluten) on a broth with plenty of bonito.
t: This article was created with AI (ChatGPT-4o), with some additions of my own😁
This time I visited "Okinawa Soba SOBA DAY" in Daido, Naha. I ate here in October 2024😁 The shop's exterior is simple, and the mostly white sign catches the eye✨.
Okinawa Soba SOBA DAY
Okinawa Soba SOBA DAY

When you enter the shop, the ticket machine jumps out at you🎟. It seems to be a meal ticket system here, and the menu is extensive. What I chose this time was the "double-meat soba"! A luxurious bowl where you can enjoy both braised pork belly and chashu. When I bought my ticket and took a seat, the counter seats were full and it was bustling. It really is a popular shop😊.
Meal ticket machine set up near the entrance
This shop's name is "Okinawa Soba SOBA DAY," and indeed "Okinawa Soba Day" is October 17😄

Since I came to eat around Okinawa Soba Day, there was also a campaign pork dish called "Pineapple Pork." This time I went with the regular "double-meat soba," but it seems the usual broth had been upgraded to one made with "Pineapple Pork," so I was looking forward to it😆
Apparently every broth has been upgraded to "Pineapple Pork"😄
Double-meat soba ¥970

The "double-meat soba" was brought out after a wait of a few minutes. It's a very beautiful-looking bowl, with colorful toppings. Chashu, braised pork belly, and... fu (wheat gluten)? were on top. The fu was a little unexpected, with a distinctive fluffy texture. It has almost no taste of its own.
They said the broth uses Pineapple Pork, but the bonito broth really comes through in it🍜.
Double-meat soba ¥970
The noodles are medium-thin and straight, with a slightly firm texture. The overall balance is good, but if you ask whether there's any distinctive feature worth noting, it feels ordinary.

And as for the meat, both the braised pork belly and chashu are the type where a bit of sinewy texture remains. This may divide likes and dislikes😅. They're simmered thoroughly, but in terms of tenderness I'd say they're one step short.

The shop's atmosphere is casual, and it seemed bustling with local customers. It's a compact setup with only counter seats, and it's a nice point that it's easy to visit casually even on your own. Also, island chili peppers and vinegar are provided as condiments, so you can customize it to your liking, which is nice🌶️.
There's vinegar among the condiments too.

By the way, when I googled "SOBA DAY," it seems to be run by someone who previously trained at "EIBUN," which I introduce in "Recommended Okinawa soba shops I'd like you to try at least once." That raised my expectations, but my impression of the actual taste was just plain tasty. Of course, it's a reliable bowl.

Rating (9/15): Overall, it was plainly tasty Okinawa soba. I wanted one more surprise. It might be good to stop by once when visiting as a tourist, but whether you'd come back may depend on your taste? Next time I'd like to try a different dish🍴!

Chicken, Pork Bone & Seafood Okinawa Soba ¥800
