The interior has a calm, wood-grain atmosphere with counter and table seats, making it a comfortable space.
Meat soba ¥680

The "Meat Soba" arrived 😄 First, as always, let's taste the broth. Its distinctive feature is a very clear broth, different from the pork bone or bonito broth you often see at other shops. It's a gentle flavor that makes me think, "Maybe it's chicken-stock-based?" and it's decently tasty 😋
Meat soba ¥680

The noodles are medium-thick, straight fresh noodles. They have moderate firmness and are satisfying to eat. For toppings, in addition to the usual braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), there's also minced meat, a feature you won't find at other shops. However, the braised pork belly still had a bit of sinewy texture, which bothered me.

Rating (9/15): The broth has a clear, gentle flavor different from other shops, and you can feel the creativity in things like using two kinds of meat. However, overall my impression was that it's decently tasty. When you visit Naha, why not stop by once? 😊

まるち中城店.name: Maruchi Nakagusuku Branch
まるち中城店.desc: A hugely popular shop in an old Okinawan folk house in the farmland area of Nakagusuku Village. A customizable style where you choose from 3 kinds each of broth (light, rich, salt) and noodles (thin, flat, wavy). Its signature is the Maruchi Soba topped with pig's feet, braised pork belly, and soft-bone pork ribs.
t: I ate here in January 2024 😁 I've conquered the 13th stamp rally, so I'll keep going, aiming to clear every Okinawa soba shop on the main island 👍

This shop is in a rural spot you reach by driving through the farmland area on the sea side of National Route 329 in Nakagusuku Village, but when I arrived, relying on Google Maps, I was stunned (°°)!
There were tons of cars parked, and I could tell there were lots of customers. It may be rude to call it the countryside, but it's an amazingly popular shop.
Maruchi Nakagusuku Branch (it's an old Okinawan folk house, but I was surprised at how many tourists there were (^0^;))
Maruchi Nakagusuku Branch

Inside the old folk house, it was full of customers. However, there were tables set up outdoors too, and I was told that at an outdoor table you could order right away without waiting, so I decided to eat outside 😁 It was a little chilly though (^0^;)
The outdoor tables
Menu (it's the type where you can choose from 3 kinds each of broth and noodles)
Menu (an authentic lineup of Okinawa soba dishes 😁)
Menu (it's the type where you can choose from 3 kinds each of broth and noodles)

I decided to order the "Maruchi Soba," which shares the shop's name. Since you can choose the broth and noodles, I asked the staff for a recommendation. They said "light broth" and "thin noodles" are ordered a lot, so I ordered that.
Maruchi soba ¥880 (complimentary jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice) at lunchtime)
The Maruchi Soba arrived 😁 Tasting the broth, the description says it's a blended stock of chicken, pork, and bonito, but it's a somewhat pork-bone-based broth.
Maruchi soba ¥880

Next, the noodles. The straight, thin noodles feel soft. The toppings, pig's feet (tebichi), braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), and soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), give it plenty of volume. The soft-bone pork ribs and braised pork belly are a bit dry and have a sinewy texture.
Rating (9/15): It feels average, but there are lots of tourists and it's a popular shop. If you want to experience an old Okinawan folk house, why not give it a try at least once 😆

まるち南城市つきしろ店.name: Maruchi Nanjo Tsukishiro Branch
まるち南城市つきしろ店.desc: Maruchi's Tsukishiro branch, where you can choose from 3 broths (light/rich/salt) and 4 noodles. You can even choose superfood moringa noodles, and its signature is the Maruchi Soba with everything on top: braised pork belly, pig's feet, and soft-bone pork ribs. Complimentary jushi too.
t: *This article was created with AI (ChatGPT 4o) and partly edited by me lol

I ate here in July 2024 😁 This time I visited "Maruchi," an Okinawa soba specialty shop in Tsukishiro, Nanjo. I had the "Maruchi Soba," which shares the shop's name, so I'll give you my thoughts in full (?)!
Maruchi Nanjo Tsukishiro Branch (it's near the Costco opening in August 2024)
First, Maruchi's exterior. The red sign is the landmark. Inside the bright, clean shop, locals were enjoying their meals in a friendly, convivial atmosphere.
Menu
Menu
You can choose from 3 kinds of broth.
You can choose from 4 kinds of noodles.
Menu (there seems to be zaru soba too)
What I ordered from the menu this time was the "Maruchi Soba," which shares the shop's name. For the broth, on the staff's recommendation I chose "light," the most popular.
Maruchi soba (moringa noodles) ¥1,150 (jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice) is complimentary)
After a while, the "Maruchi Soba" arrived 😄
First, a sip of the broth. It's a blended stock of chicken, pork, and bonito, with the pork bone flavor standing out.
Maruchi soba (moringa noodles) ¥1,150

Next, the noodles. I tried choosing the moringa noodles. They're noodles made with a superfood vegetable called moringa, and apparently they're rich in nutrients important for human activity, such as vitamins, minerals, and amino acids. It feels like it makes things a little healthier (^0^;)

But to be honest, eating them, I couldn't really taste much difference from ordinary thin straight noodles. The texture wasn't anything special either; they were just ordinary soft noodles. Since I'd had high hopes, it was maybe a bit disappointing.

The toppings are a so-called "everything on top" combo: braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), pig's feet (tebichi), and soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki). They're all tender, but the braised pork belly still had a bit of sinew, and the texture bothered me in places.
Actually, I'd eaten "Maruchi Soba" before at the old-folk-house-style Nakagusuku branch, and I only realized afterward that it's the same chain as the "Maruchi" I visited this time.

Rating (9/15): It feels average. The Nakagusuku branch I visited before had lots of tourists, but this one seemed to have more local customers. The sinewy texture of the braised pork belly and the somewhat weak impact of the moringa noodles' flavor led me to this rating. It's near the Costco scheduled to open around August 24, 2024, so why not try a meal here at least once on your way back from Costco 😄

まるなが.name: Marunaga
まるなが.desc: A diner with plenty of set meals too, near the Okinawa City Fisheries Cooperative's Payao direct sales shop. The broth lets you taste both pork and bonito, and a distinctive touch is the diced "back fat" topping you won't see at other shops. A nostalgic, gentle bowl.
t: I ate here in October 2023. This shop was a participant in the "13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (Oct 1, 2023 to Feb 29, 2024)," and I went here as my 3rd of 34 shops 😊
"Marunaga" It's near the Okinawa City Fisheries Cooperative's Payao direct sales shop.
Menu posted at the entrance. Besides Okinawa soba, there are many dishes such as set meals.
Daily specials menu. These look delicious too 🤤

The menu posted at the entrance had all sorts of delicious-looking dishes, but of course I'd come to conquer the Okinawa soba stamp rally, so I ordered the "Marunaga Soba" featured in the stamp rally booklet. There were large, medium, and small sizes, and this time I chose "medium."
I ordered the "Marunaga Soba (Medium)" featured in the stamp rally booklet.

It's pay-first, and when I ordered the "Marunaga Soba (Medium)," the staff immediately asked, "Is this for the stamp rally?" (;^ω^) When I answered "Yes," they promptly asked for my booklet and said, "I'll stamp it." At Kukuru in Tomigusuku, the method was to stamp it at the end, saying "I'll stamp it on your way out," but here they stamped it right at the start. Each shop has its own way of doing things 😁
Got Marunaga's stamp! I've still got a long way to go to conquer it (;^ω^) I'll keep at it steadily.
Marunaga soba (medium) ¥780

First, a sip of the broth 😊 As described in the booklet, the pork- and bonito-based broth is finished so that you can taste both flavors rather than it leaning toward either one. It reminded me of the broth at "Awase Soba" lol
The noodles are medium-thick and straight. They're on the soft side.
Marunaga soba (medium) ¥780

The toppings are fish cake (kamaboko), rolled omelet, braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), and soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki); the meat is tender but has a bit of sinewy texture. There were also small dice-shaped pieces; they looked like "konnyaku?", but the ticket machine said "with back fat," so I think it's pork fat cut finely and added in. I've never seen this at other shops.

Rating (9/15): It's decently tasty. It feels like a nostalgic, old-fashioned, gentle Okinawa soba. Judging from the menu, I found it quite reasonably priced. This time I ordered the medium size, and it had a decent amount of volume, so I was satisfied.

まるの家.name: Maru no Ie
まるの家.desc: A homemade-noodle shop in the amusing location of the second floor of a pachislot parlor. Its pride is chewy, firm, medium-thick straight noodles, and you can change up the flavor with its special homemade kōrēgūsu. A wide-ranging menu with set meals and curry too.
t: *This article was created with AI (ChatGPT 4o) and partly edited by me 😆

I went to eat here in September 2024 😄 Today's soba tour took me to "Maru no Ie" in Chatan, Chatan Town. This shop is, believe it or not, located on the second floor of a pachislot parlor! ✨ A bit of an amusing location, right? Actually, this atmosphere reminded me of "Garyu Soba" in Nago, which I visited before.
Maru no Ie
*Garyu Soba in Nago, where I ate before
A big sign reading "Homemade Noodles" hangs at the shop's entrance, and you can feel their dedication to handmade noodles!
Menu panel set up at the outdoor entrance
Menu panel set up at the outdoor entrance
The shop is on the 2nd floor
The shop is on the 2nd floor
Maru no Ie entrance
Ticket machine set up at the entrance inside

Right away I ordered the "Soft-Bone Soba" at the ticket machine. Looking at the menu, besides Okinawa soba there was a wide selection of set meals, curry, and more, and it felt like you could eat just about anything, but today I decided to go with the classic Okinawa soba after all 😊.
Inside the shop
Inside the shop
Soft-bone soba ¥850

I sat down and looked at the soft-bone soba that was brought out; it looks substantial. The broth is clear, and it feels like both bonito and pork bone stocks are blended just right. It's a flavor where you can taste both bonito and pork bone.
Soft-bone soba ¥850

And then the long-awaited homemade noodles! These were quite delicious 🍜. They're medium-thick straight noodles with a chewy texture and firmness, and you can enjoy a solid bite with every mouthful. This texture is irresistible. They really live up to the "Homemade Noodles" sign!

The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) in the toppings were thoroughly simmered and tender, and I liked how they fell apart in my mouth. However, a bit of sinewy texture remained; the tenderness is perfect, but it's a little disappointing that there's a lot of sinew 😅.

On the table there was also Maru no Ie's special kōrēgūsu (chili-infused awamori), and adding it instantly gave the flavor a sharp, spicy kick! It's a nice touch that lets you enjoy the second half without getting bored.
Maru no Ie's special homemade kōrēgūsu
Maru no Ie's special homemade kōrēgūsu

Overall, it was a bowl where the deliciousness of the noodles left the strongest impression. The broth and soft-bone pork ribs aren't bad either, but if anything they fall within the ordinary range. The shop's atmosphere was calm too, and I could relax and enjoy my meal 🍴.
Rating (9.5/15): It's decently tasty. The homemade noodles score pretty high 😄 It's in Chatan Town, a tourist area, so why not try it once while sightseeing 😆
Next time I'd like to try other dishes too, but I fully enjoyed this soft-bone soba as well! See you on my next Okinawa soba tour! 👋🍜

まるひら食堂.name: Maruhira Shokudo
まるひら食堂.desc: A diner in a former community store in Uka, Kunigami Village, at the northernmost tip of Okinawa's main island. Featured in the newspaper as "the northernmost diner on Okinawa's west coast." Braised pork belly soba in a gentle pork bone broth, and the specialty "Genkotsu Set Meal" with its super-huge fried chicken.
t: The shop I'm introducing this time is "Maruhira Shokudo" in Uka, Kunigami Village, at the northernmost tip of Okinawa's main island. This shop is actually a place with history that has long been loved by locals as the former Uka Community Store 😁 I went to eat there in December 2024; it's been featured in the newspaper too and is known as "the northernmost diner on Okinawa's west coast."
Maruhira Shokudo
Menu set up outdoors
The entrance (watch out for habu snakes (^0^;))

Since it's in Kunigami Village at the very north of Okinawa's main island, it's not a place you can easily come to, but that's exactly what makes it feel special ✨ When you step inside, there's the atmosphere of an old-fashioned diner. Since it was lunchtime, surprisingly there were quite a lot of customers 😲 Maybe it's not just locals but lots of people visiting on sightseeing trips too.
Menu posted inside the shop

Looking at the menu posted on the wall, there's a wide selection of set meals besides Okinawa soba. I'm especially curious about the dish called "Genkotsu Set Meal" 😆 It apparently comes with super-huge fried chicken, and it seems to be a famous dish too. This time the goal was my Okinawa soba tour, so I decided to order the "Braised Pork Belly Soba, Medium" from the menu. At ¥750 the price is reasonable too, and though you can't tell from the menu, it's a nice plus that pickles come complimentary 😊
Menu
Braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) soba, medium ¥750

After ordering and waiting a while, the "Braised Pork Belly Soba" was brought out. It looks simple, but it feels like a proper Okinawa soba. First, as always, I'll taste the broth 😋 The pork-bone-based broth has a gentle, light flavor. The not-too-strong pork bone flavor is pleasant, and it's finished as a homey taste that somehow feels nostalgic. Maybe because of its northernmost location, it has a gentle seasoning that tourists can easily take to.

Next, the noodles. They're wavy noodles with a softish texture. The braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) topping is sliced thin like ramen chashu and is very tender. It's a different texture from thick braised pork belly, and it's tasty in its own way ✨ It's topped with plenty of finely shredded white leek too, and its crunchy texture is a nice accent.

The appeal of Maruhira Shokudo is, above all, the special feeling of it being "the northernmost tip of Okinawa's main island." Okinawa soba eaten after coming all the way to Kunigami Village, where an ordinary Okinawa soba tour rarely takes you, becomes an experience that stays in your memory even more than the taste 😊 Being a former community store, it has a warm atmosphere rooted in the community, with a charm different from Okinawa soba shops in urban areas. Eating Okinawa soba while time flows leisurely makes you forget the busyness of daily life.

Also, as the newspaper coverage shows, this shop is an important presence supporting the local food culture. It's a shop I'd definitely like you to drop by when you visit the northern region on a sightseeing trip 😄 The taste was decently good. It's not exceptionally outstanding in flavor, but I think the shop's big appeal is its northernmost location, its history as a former community store, and the warm atmosphere of a place that continues to be loved by the community ✨
It's been featured in the newspaper too, as "Local flavor at the northernmost tip"

Rating (9/15): When you come to sightsee in the northern region or enjoy the nature of Yanbaru, please be sure to try the Okinawa soba here at Maruhira Shokudo. You can have the special experience of "the northernmost Okinawa soba" that you can't usually taste 😊 Next time I'm also curious about the super-huge fried chicken of the "Genkotsu Set Meal," so if I get the chance I'd like to give it a try 😆

みよ家.name: Miyo-ya
みよ家.desc: A homemade-noodle shop near the Kadena Rotary on National Route 58 and the town hall. A rare shop where you can taste the additive-free, light bonito-broth Zensei Soba, and "Tojin Soba" (with a black soy-sauce-based broth), the roots of Okinawa soba, revived after 110 years. Hugely popular with local customers.
t: ― 2nd Visit (June 2024) ―
*This article was created with "ChatGPT 4o" and partly edited by me.

I went to eat here in June 2024 😄 Using the ¥500 discount voucher for Miyo-ya that I received at the Soba Jogu awards ceremony for the recent Okinawa soba stamp rally, I went to eat the "Tojin Soba" I'd been curious about for a while 😆
This "Tojin Soba" is said to be the roots of Okinawa soba, and it's a dish revived after 110 years.

Miyo-ya has an eye-catching storefront with colorful, very Okinawan decorations, and at the entrance hangs a sign reading "Homemade Noodles Okinawa Soba." As always, it was bustling with local customers.
Miyo-ya
You order easily inside the shop, receive a number tag, and wait at your seat. The wait wasn't that long, and the staff were kind and pleasant.
Number slip and order receipt 😄 (When I had ChatGPT read this photo, it recognized it as a "number tag" and wrote the article above. Amazing (^0^;))

Inside the shop, there's a poster explaining the history and features of "Tojin Soba" in detail. "Tojin Soba" can be called the origin of Okinawa soba, and this soba, revived after roughly 110 years, is characterized by its special soy-sauce-based broth.
Poster inside the shop explaining "Tojin Soba," the roots of Okinawa soba
Poster inside the shop explaining "Tojin Soba," the roots of Okinawa soba
Tojin soba ¥800

The "Tojin Soba" that was brought out is striking just from the look of its black broth. Taking a sip, I expected a strong soy sauce flavor, but it was a gentle taste with plenty of bonito flavor coming through. This is an irresistible point for lovers of Okinawa soba with bonito-based broth.
Tojin soba ¥800

Next, the noodles. The homemade fresh noodles have a chewy texture and go perfectly with the broth. This chewiness is something special you can't get with store-bought noodles, and they're satisfying to eat.

The toppings include green onions and tofu-sized chunks of pork, letting you enjoy a flavor a little different from regular Okinawa soba. The flavor of this meat combined with the broth gave the whole bowl a very good balance.

"Tojin Soba" is a dish worthy of the word "revival," with the broth, noodles, and toppings each in fine harmony. It was also a nice plus that I could enjoy it for effectively ¥300 using the ¥500 discount voucher. It wasn't just decently tasty; it was a bowl where I could feel history and tradition.

Rating (9/15): The broth looks black and striking, like it would taste strong, but it has the usual Okinawa soba bonito broth coming through and is decently tasty. How about Miyo-ya, where you can taste "Tojin Soba," the roots of Okinawa soba?
― 1st Visit (October 2023) ―
I ate here in October 2023. This shop was a participant in the "13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (Oct 1, 2023 to Feb 29, 2024)," and I went here as my 5th of 34 shops 😊
Miyo-ya. It's near the Kadena Rotary on National Route 58 and Kadena Town Hall
There's a parking lot next to Miyo-ya. The first 3 hours are free, which is nice
When I went inside, since it was lunchtime, it was bustling with local customers. There were quite a few elderly people too, so I thought it must be a shop popular in the community 😁
The "Zensei Soba" was featured in the stamp rally booklet, so I ordered the "Zensei Soba." The ticket machine is set up near the kitchen at the back of the shop, and you order with it.

When I asked, "Can I pay with my phone?" they said credit cards could be used, so I tried to pay by credit card, but whether it was a staff error or a machine malfunction, I don't know, the card payment wouldn't go through, and in the end I bought a ticket from the ticket machine with cash (;^ω^)
I continue to hope that cashless payment becomes possible at every Okinawa soba shop (;^ω^)
Zensei soba ¥1000
After a short wait, the Zensei Soba arrived. As always, a sip of the broth. It seems to be an additive-free broth, a light bonito stock. It's a gentle flavor with a subtle hint of bonito broth.

This broth is a light style reminiscent of the soba shops in the Shuri area of Naha that I ate at before. I thought it was tastier than the Shuri-area broth, but those who like rich, hearty broth might find it unsatisfying.
Zensei soba ¥1000
After the broth, I dig into the noodles 😊 You can choose between fresh noodles and boiled noodles, and I chose fresh. The medium-thick, slightly wavy noodles are chewy and delicious 🤗

Since it's "Zensei" (all-out), the toppings are rolled omelet, fish cake (kamaboko), braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki), and pig's feet (tebichi). The pig's feet are on the large side and wobbly.

Rating (9/15): The broth is on the light side, so those who like rich flavors may find it unsatisfying. It feels like a shop loved by local customers. My impression is that it takes a bit longer from ordering to serving than other shops. I also hope they get used to operating the credit card machine (;^ω^)

丸隆そば.name: Marutaka Soba
丸隆そば.desc: A shop in Okita, Nago City (across from Nago Commercial and Technical High School) that calls itself "the shop of the original soki soba". A light soup with a strong bonito broth, medium-thin noodles, and tender pork spare ribs. Comparing it with Gabusoka Shokudo's "head-family soki soba" is fun too.
t: It was featured on the "Nago City Soba Map", and I ate here in December 2020 😄
Marutaka Soba (across from Nago Commercial and Technical High School)
The soba map introduced it as "calling itself the original soki soba", so I ordered the "soki soba" 😏
"Marutaka Soba" is featured as shop 40 of 41 on the "Nago Soba Map" / Soki soba ¥630

A light soup with a strong bonito broth, medium-thin noodles, and tender pork spare ribs (soki) — delicious 😄 Gabusoka Shokudo also calls itself "head-family soki soba", so their claims kind of overlap, don't they? 😄

Rating (9/15): Simply tasty. Marutaka bills itself as "the shop of the original soki soba", while Gabusoka Shokudo bills itself as "head-family soki soba". Everyone, please try comparing them for yourselves 😄

亀そばしまや.name: Kame Soba Shimaya
亀そばしまや.desc: An independent Kame Soba shop with a striking red-tiled roof. The gentle Agu pork broth soup is the familiar Kame Soba flavor. The signature Honke Kame soba is topped with melt-in-your-mouth soft-bone pork ribs and braised pork belly, and there's an autograph from Yamakawa too.
t: *This article was created with AI (ChatGPT 4o), with some parts added by me 😆

I ate here in September 2024 😄 This shop in Uchidomari, Ginowan City, is an independent "Kame Soba" shop, so you can enjoy an atmosphere and flavor similar to the other Kame Soba affiliated shops. The exterior has a striking red-tiled roof, with a warm atmosphere that seems loved by tourists and locals alike.
Shimaya
Shimaya
Inside the shop
Celebrities have visited too (sorry, I don't know who they are (^0^;))
This is the autograph of pro baseball player Yamakawa 😆
Menu
Menu
Menu (there are also rice bowls and champuru dishes)
Kame Soba's soup is made with Agu broth 😄
I went inside and this time ordered the recommended "Honke Kame soba". It's the signature item, featured prominently on the menu too.
Honke Kame soba ¥890
The soba that was served looked simple, yet I could sense it was carefully made.

First, the soup: the broth made with Agu pork had a very gentle flavor. You can sense the richness of the meat, but it's not heavy, finished to be easy to drink. A comforting flavor that seems likely to appeal to a wide range of ages. It's the same flavor as the other Kame Soba shops 😄
Honke Kame soba ¥890

The noodles are thin and straight, finished on the soft side. The smooth, slippery feel going down is pleasant, and they clung well to the soup. Personally I'd be even happier with a bit more chewiness, but as it is, it's a classic flavor.

And the toppings are mainly soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku). Both are simmered until melt-in-your-mouth, and their tenderness, crumbling apart in your mouth, was appealing. The seasoning is just right too, with a perfectly balanced sweet-savory taste.

Overall, while not flashy, it was a bowl with a reliable flavor. What was especially memorable was the gentleness of the soup. I think it's something that a wide range of people, from Okinawa soba beginners to local regulars, can enjoy.
Rating (9/15): Simply tasty, and you can enjoy the same Kame Soba as at the other shops 😄

亀そば（北中店）.name: Kame Soba (Kitanaka Branch)
亀そば（北中店）.desc: The Kame Soba Kitanaka branch along Route 330. A surprisingly light Agu broth considering how it looks, medium-thin noodles, and tender braised pork belly and rafute. There are also locations in Nishihara Town, Roadside Station Kadena, and Minatomachi in Naha City.
t: I ate here in March 2019 😊
Kame Soba (Kitanaka Branch), along Route 330
Kame soba (medium) ¥600

I ordered the "Kame soba". From the color of the soup it looks like it would be strongly flavored, but the Agu broth is very light. Medium-thin noodles, and the braised pork belly and rafute are tender and delicious 😋

Rating (9/15): Simply tasty. It seems popular with locals, and at lunchtime it was full of customers. There are also Kame Soba shops in Nishihara Town, Roadside Station Kadena, and Minatomachi in Naha City, so how about trying it once?

二見そば.name: Futami Soba
二見そば.desc: A soba shop in a lone house standing along the mountains connecting the east and west of Nago City. Featured on the Nago Soba Map, it's particular about its chicken, pork, and bonito blended broth and homemade kōrēgūsu. The everything-on-top is loaded with toppings and superb. *There are reports it has been closed since around May 2024.
t: It was featured on the "Nago City Soba Map", and I tried it in September 2020 😀
*Please note that as of August 2024 there are reports that this shop is closed (since around May 2024?).
Futami Soba (driving along the mountains between Route 58 on Nago City's west coast and Route 329 on the east coast, it appears like a lone house in the middle of nowhere lol)
The interior is a renovated detached house, with a warm atmosphere like someone's home 😁
I ordered the "Futami soba everything-on-top" featured on the soba map.
"Futami Soba" is featured as shop 23 of 41 on the "Nago Soba Map"
Futami soba everything-on-top (¥850)

Loaded with toppings — pork spare ribs (soki), braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), kombu, and yushi-dofu — it's the best 😁 The medium-thin noodles go well with the soup made from painstakingly prepared chicken, pork, and bonito broth, and it's delicious.
The kōrēgūsu (chili-infused awamori) is homemade too, and you can tell that everything is made carefully with a great deal of time and effort.
Rating (12/15): Futami Soba is particular about making things in-house. This is also recommended, so please try it.
PS: I don't have a photo, but the actress Meisa Kuroki is apparently from around here, and she seems to like this soba shop too — I think there was her autograph in the shop.

今帰仁そば.name: Nakijin Soba
今帰仁そば.desc: A tile-roofed old-house soba shop near Nakijin Castle Ruins and Churaumi Aquarium. Agu pork and bonito blended broth with homemade noodles, and you can choose from four toppings. The three homemade condiments made with Yanbaru ingredients are fun too, and it's a photogenic spot.
t: I ate here in April 2025 😊 This time, on an Okinawa soba tour of the northern area of the main island, I went to "Nakijin Soba" in Shoshi, Nakijin Village 🌺 Nakijin Village is an area close to the World Heritage site Nakijin Castle Ruins and Churaumi Aquarium, and this shop is in a spot that's easy to drop by while sightseeing 😄
Nakijin Soba

Arriving at the shop, the first thing that jumped out at me was a very Okinawan tile-roofed old house. The noren (shop curtain) with "Nanokuni-mura Style House" and "Nakijin Soba" written in large letters, plus the yellow "Open" sign, really build up the atmosphere ✨ This is exactly what an Okinawan old-house soba shop looks like 😊 Just the exterior gets you excited 🎵
Nakijin Soba

Before you pass under the noren at the entrance, there's a rugged Ryukyu limestone wall, bougainvillea flowers, and trees like banyans planted, giving it a super Okinawan feel 🌴 It had become a photogenic spot that makes tourists want to take pictures 📸
Inside the shop

When you go inside, this too is a stylish design 😲 Stylish rattan chairs and tables are arranged, and it's an open space with natural light coming in through the sudare (bamboo blinds). It keeps the charm of an old house while feeling new 🌸
Inside the shop

Inside there's also a raised tatami area, which has an atmosphere like an old-fashioned Okinawan grandma's house 😊 Orion Beer posters and Nakijin Village watermelon posters are up, so you can feel the local vibe too 🍉
Menu

Looking at the menu, the signature "Nakijin soba" is ¥950. Homemade noodles with Agu pork and bonito broth, and it's set up so you can choose from four toppings 😄 You choose from "melt-in-your-mouth nankotsu soki", "seared salt-flavored sanmai-niku", "mix", and "yushi-dofu (limited quantity)", and this time I greedily ordered the mix (plus ¥50) 🍜 There's also kids' soba (¥750), a Nakijin soba set (¥1,350), jushi (¥300), homemade yushi-dofu (¥400), and more.
Condiments on the table

There are three kinds of condiments on the table — "nama-shichimi (spicy miso made with Yanbaru shikuwasa and island chili peppers)", "nimi togarashi (Yanbaru shikuwasa and island chili peppers)", and "kōrēgūsu" — all homemade condiments made with Yanbaru ingredients, which gets you excited 🌶️ They seem to sell them as souvenirs too, and you can sense their dedication ✨
Nakijin soba (mix) ¥1,000

After a short wait, the Nakijin soba (mix) was brought out 🍜 In a bowl that looks like Uruma ware, it looks very photogenic, with something white and creamy like yushi-dofu, julienned ginger, soft-bone pork ribs, seared braised pork belly, and green onion arranged in good balance 😊

The customary sip of soup. It's supposed to be an Agu pork and bonito blended broth, but hmm, honestly it's a light style where neither really comes through 🤔 Not in a bad way — it's a very gentle flavor with a refined finish — but personally I thought it'd be fine if the richness of the Agu pork or the bonito aroma hit a bit harder. Maybe they've finished it to have broad appeal for tourists 😅
Nakijin soba (mix) ¥1,000
Next I have the noodles 🍜 Homemade medium-thick, gently wavy noodles, and these are pretty good 😋 They have solid chewiness, and the noodles are simply tasty 👍

The braised pork belly and soft-bone pork ribs toppings are simmered until melt-in-your-mouth and tender, but my impression was that for the price of ¥1,000, they were a bit on the small side 😅 And some parts of the soft-bone pork ribs still had a bit of a sinewy texture, so I'd have been happier if they were just a little more fall-apart tender 🥩

Rating (9/15): The charming old-house exterior and the stylishly renovated interior are outstanding, and it seems like a shop that will be popular with tourists 😊 But as for the flavor, honestly, it's "ordinary" 🤔 With a light soup where neither the Agu pork nor the bonito comes through, and toppings on the small side for ¥1,000, I'd say it needs a little more in terms of value for money 🍜 For those who want to enjoy the atmosphere of an old house on the way back from sightseeing in Nakijin Village or from Churaumi Aquarium, I think it's worth stopping by 😄

伊差川食堂.name: Isagawa Shokudo
伊差川食堂.desc: A locally rooted, everyday diner in Isagawa, Nago City. A rich menu from set meals to soba, in a wall-photos-plus-ticket-machine style. The affordable pork-bone-based "meat and vegetable soba" has a flavor reminiscent of the Kame Soba chain in Nishihara.
t: I went to eat here in April 2024 😄
Isagawa Shokudo
It feels like a shop loved by the locals 😁
Menu posted on the wall
Menu posted on the wall
Menu posted on the wall
At this shop, there don't seem to be menus on the tables, so you choose from the menus posted on the wall or at the ticket machine 😄
From the menu I chose the "meat and vegetable soba".

Meat and vegetable soba ¥750

Rating (9/15): Simply tasty. I thought it was similar to the meat and vegetable soba at "Honke Kame Soba Wakasa branch" I ate before. The price was cheaper here. How about trying it once when you come to Nago City 😄

喫茶ジャーン.name: Kissa Jaan
喫茶ジャーン.desc: A retro café inside "Ishi no Yu Inomae-kan" along National Route 331. Here you can enjoy a new-style "Basil Soba": green homemade thin noodles kneaded with sweet basil, a bonito broth soup with lemongrass, and chicken smoked with cherry wood chips.
t: I went to eat here in January 2024 😊　It was during the "13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (Oct 1, 2023 – Feb 29, 2024)," and I had just one more shop to go to clear it, so I wanted to eat at a participating shop, but they were closed on holidays, so this time I decided to eat at this shop, which I learned about in the newspaper and which isn't part of the stamp rally.
"Kissa Jaan" entrance (it's along National Route 331)
"Kissa Jaan" (the building has the name of a (former?) stone sauna bath, so for a moment I thought I had the wrong place (^0^;))

The entrance had the name "Kissa Jaan" on it, so I went in thinking this was it, but the name of the building was "Ishi no Yu Inomae." Wondering "Huh?", I went inside and asked a staff member, "Is this where the Okinawa soba is?" and was told "Please come in" and shown to the back of the shop. I was glad I had it right 😄
Menu
At the top of the menu was the "Basil Soba" introduced in the newspaper. I ordered it 😄
Menu (this soba packed with herbs looks delicious too 😄)

Basil soba　¥800
While I was looking around the shop, the "Basil Soba" arrived 😄
First, I taste the soup 😋

As the menu describes, lemongrass seems to be added to the soup rich with bonito broth, and you can taste a faintly refreshing tartness. It's a new flavor you won't find at other shops. It works perfectly well—delicious 😋
Basil soba　¥800

嘉海食堂.name: Kakai Shokudo
嘉海食堂.desc: A popular diner along National Route 329 in Yaka, Kin Town. The Kakai Soba, limited to 10 servings a day, is topped with everything—pig's feet (tebichi), pork spare ribs (soki), braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), kelp, egg, and fish cake (kamaboko)—plus okara on the side, for a very generous portion. The "first in Japan" pig's feet (tebichi) vending machine in front of the shop is also famous.
t: I ate here in March 2023 ☺
Kakai Shokudo (along National Route 329)
Since it has the same name as the shop, and on top of that it's limited to 10 servings a day, I ordered the "Kakai Soba" 😁
Menu
The year's popular menu items are shown, which is a helpful reference for first-time customers.
Kakai soba　¥957

The soup has a strong pork bone base, and the noodles are a medium-thick straight type. The toppings are everything—pig's feet (tebichi), pork spare ribs (soki), braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), kelp, egg, and fish cake (kamaboko)—and it also comes with okara (soy pulp), for a very generous portion 😊

Rating (9/15): Solidly tasty. How about it when you're driving along the east coast of the northern region 😁　Also, I don't have a photo, but in front of the shop there's a vending machine selling "pig's feet (tebichi) (pig's trotters)" labeled "first in Japan." It might be an Instagrammable photo spot for sightseeing 😁

城木屋.name: Shirokiya
城木屋.desc: A restaurant along National Route 449. Soki soba with a gently flavored broth, soft noodles, pork spare ribs (soki), and flavor-soaked knotted kelp. It has a wide menu beyond soba and becomes an izakaya at night. A pro baseball favorite, lined with autographs from Nippon-Ham players.
t: It was introduced in the "Nago City Soba Map," and I ate here in December 2020 😄
Shirokiya (along National Route 449)
In the "Nago Soba Map," "Shirokiya" is featured as shop 37 of 41
I ordered the "Soki Soba" that was introduced in the map.
Soki soba　¥650
Knotted kelp that has soaked up the flavor, tender pork spare ribs (soki), smooth soft noodles, and a gently flavored broth—delicious 😄

Rating (9/15): I think it's solidly tasty. There are lots of menu items besides soba, and at night they also run as an izakaya. It seems lots of pro baseball players come here too, with plenty of autographs and uniforms inside. During camp season, players from the Hokkaido Nippon-Ham Fighters might be dropping by ☺

壱蘭.name: Ichiran
壱蘭.desc: A shop with a black noren (shop curtain) like a ramen shop. A light bonito-based soup with homemade fresh medium-thick wavy noodles. Its distinctive feature is changing up the flavor with "Shimanero," an original habanero-based seasoning. A rare Okinawa soba shop that's also open in the evening.
t: *This article was created with AI (Claude 3.5 Sonnet) and partly added to by me.
I ate here in September 2024 😄 This time I'm introducing "Ichiran" in Nishizaki, Itoman!

It's not a shop name that makes you think of "Uchinā soba," is it. It gives off a completely ramen-shop vibe 😄 Perhaps to match the shop name, the black noren (shop curtain) with gold lettering is striking.
Ichiran
Inside there are counter seats and table seats, with a cozy atmosphere. On the tables was a seasoning called "Shimanero" that I've never seen at other Okinawa soba shops, which made me curious 😲
Seasonings on the counter
Besides the usual kōrēgūsu (chili-infused awamori), there's Shimanero rather than habanero
Menu
Menu
Looking at the menu, there are spicy items, but this time I decided to stick to the basics and order the "Nankotsu Soba."
After waiting a few minutes, the "Nankotsu Soba" came served in a black bowl with beautiful kintsugi, and it looks great too! 😋
Nankotsu soba (medium)　¥800
First, the soup. It's a light soup based on bonito broth, with a gentle flavor.
Nankotsu soba (medium)　¥800
Next, the noodles. They're said to be homemade fresh noodles—medium-thick and wavy. They're chewy, but honestly my impression was that they're just average for homemade fresh noodles 🤔
As for the soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) topping, the cartilage parts are stewed until meltingly tender, but parts of the meat still had some sinewiness left.
I tried changing up the flavor with the "Shimanero" I was curious about. It's said to be a seasoning based on habanero; about three drops add a tingling heat and let you enjoy a different flavor 😆
The tourist sitting next to me kept saying "So good! So good!", but I couldn't help thinking there are many more delicious Okinawa soba shops out there 😅

Rating (9/15): It's solidly tasty Okinawa soba, but its distinctive feature is that you can enjoy changing up the flavor with the original seasoning "Shimanero." If you love super-spicy food, why not take on the super-spicy menu? 😊 This shop is also open in the evening, which is rare for an Okinawa soba shop.

Seats overlooking a garden and soft-bone pork rib soba with homemade thick noodles. Hugely popular with tourists, with a record-level wait. There's also the famous dessert "Ufuya Ball."

大衆食堂ミッキー.name: Taishu Shokudo Mickey
大衆食堂ミッキー.desc: A rare diner open only on Fridays and Saturdays. The wall covered in celebrity autographs is stunning, and the retro "Coffee Shop Mickey" sign has great charm too. Soki soba with rich pork bone flavor, plus a mysterious dish called "Okazu" 😂

My first of 2025 was "Taishu Shokudo Mickey" in Chuo, Okinawa City〜😊　This is a somewhat rare shop that's only open on Fridays and Saturdays. I happened to pass by and it was open, so in I went unplanned (lol). Chance encounters like this are part of the fun of the soba tour.

Taishu Shokudo Mickey

The exterior has an old-fashioned diner atmosphere, and the "Coffee Shop Mickey" lettering on the sign is retro and full of charm ☕️✨. Inside, an entire wall is lined with celebrity autographs. There are so many, it's stunning! It had the kind of atmosphere where you immediately realize entertainers and artists from both inside and outside the prefecture have stopped by. Mountains of autographs like this somehow get me excited.

Now, what I ordered from the menu this time was the "Soki Soba" (¥850). In the bowl brought to me were the vivid red of pickled red ginger, the green of green onions, and pork spare ribs (soki) with a bold presence. Just the look of it whets the appetite 😋.
Soki soba　¥850
First, a sip of the soup. The pork bone base is strong, and my impression was that the richness of the pork comes to the front.
Soki soba　¥850

The noodles are medium-thick, loosely wavy noodles, finished on the soft side. People who love firm noodles might find them a bit lacking, but they had a reassuring flavor just like you'd expect from a diner. The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) are tender. The crunchy texture of the cartilage part also remains.

Looking over the menu, there's also a curious dish called "Okazu," and the name alone made me laugh a little 😂. That kind of playfulness, or Okinawan laid-backness, is part of the charm too. There's taco rice and Okinawa champon too, and I felt this must be a diner the locals use for everyday meals.
"Okinawa champon" is famous, but you don't often see "Okazu" (^0^;) I can't tell the difference from champon (^0^;)

Rating (9/15): It's solidly tasty. All in all, I was convinced this is a shop loved by both tourists and locals. Especially with the special feel of being "open only on Fridays and Saturdays," I felt a little lucky to have come at just the right time 🎶　By all means, how about it when you come to Ichibangai or Park Avenue in Okinawa City 😄

奇跡の手羽先.name: Kiseki no Tebasaki
奇跡の手羽先.desc: The Kumoji 2-chome branch, which also operates as an izakaya. In its playful interior covered with graffiti art, the signature is the mixed soba topped with soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), and chicken wings. The chicken wings soaked in soup give it a personality no other shop has.
t: This article was created with AI (ChatGPT-4o) and partly added to by me 😁
Okinawa soba tour 🚶‍♂️ I ate here in October 2024 😁 I went to "Kiseki no Tebasaki" in Kumoji, Naha! ✨
Kiseki no Tebasaki (Naha Kumoji 2-chome branch)
It's a participating shop in the Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally, and a shop I'd been curious about for a long time. Even the shop name is unique, and I'm excited to see what kind of soba I can eat here! 😄
The exterior is marked by red lanterns, a design where you can tell at a glance, "This is it!"
Outdoor menu sign (it's in English, maybe because there are lots of foreigners 😄)
Inside the shop
Inside the shop
When you go inside, graffiti art covers every wall, creating a playful space that's somehow nostalgic. Since it usually operates as an izakaya too, it has a homey, casual atmosphere. 🍻
Menu

What I had this time was the "Mixed Soba" (large size ¥1,100). It's one of the recommended items on the menu, so my expectations were high! The soba that arrived was loaded with toppings like soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), and chicken wings, and just by looking at it you can tell it's a very generous portion ✨
Mixed soba (large)　¥1,100

First, a sip of the soup. The seasoning has a strong bonito broth flavor, and it's really delicious! 😋 It has a punchy seasoning typical of an izakaya, and I can imagine it would be perfect for finishing off a night of drinking. However, it might be too strong for people who like a light taste.
Mixed soba (large)　¥1,100

Next, the noodles. They're a thin straight type, boiled on the soft side. They go well with the soup, and the way they slurp right down left an impression. However, if you're expecting the thick noodles and firmness characteristic of Okinawa soba, they might be a bit lacking 🤔 Personally, I would have preferred a bit more firmness.

And the toppings! The "chicken wings," which you could call the highlight this time, were a first for me, but they go surprisingly well with Okinawa soba! The soup has soaked in thoroughly, and their fall-apart tenderness is irresistible 😄 The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) were meltingly tender too, with an exquisitely soft texture that you barely need to chew. On the other hand, the braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) had a bit of sinewy texture left, and my impression was that it would be even better if that were improved.

The Okinawa soba at "Kiseki no Tebasaki" was well seasoned overall, as you'd expect from an izakaya menu, and it was filling. The unique topping of chicken wings gives it personality and a special feel you can't get at other shops. It was a memorable bowl among the stamp rally participating shops too! 🎉
Rating (9.5/15): Overall it was solidly tasty Okinawa soba. A bowl where you can enjoy unique chicken wing soba! Next time I'd like to try other menu items and the izakaya dishes too! 🍜✨😊

宮良そば.name: Miyara Soba
宮良そば.desc: A shop along National Route 330 where you can enjoy authentic Yaeyama soba. Yaeyama style with finely cut fish cake (kamaboko) and pork on round thin noodles, in a pork × bonito broth soup. Its bone soup is famous too.
t: I went to eat here in August 2022 😊
Miyara Soba (Urasoe branch)　It's along National Route 330.
Yaeyama soba　¥780

I ordered the "Yaeyama Soba." The toppings are finely cut fish cake (kamaboko) and finely cut pork, on round thin noodles. It's different from the Okinawa soba at other shops 😊　The soup is a blend of pork and bonito broth and is solidly tasty 😋

Rating (9/15): This time I had "Yaeyama soba" from the outlying islands for the first time, and compared with the Okinawa soba of the main island, its toppings and thin round noodles are distinctive. Solidly tasty.
Also, their bone soup seems to be famous, so I'd like to try it someday 😁

宮里そば.name: Miyazato Soba
宮里そば.desc: A famous shop representative of Nago. A bonito-based soup with medium-thin noodles, plus flavor-soaked braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) and kubu (knotted kelp), make it a bowl typical of Nago. Reasonably priced, with braised pork belly soba from ¥400. There's toast and spaghetti too.
t: It was introduced in the "Nago City Soba Map," so I ate here in August 2020 😄
Miyazato Soba
In the "Nago Soba Map," "Miyazato Soba" is featured as shop 6 of 41
I ordered the "Sanmai-niku Soba" that was introduced in the map
Sanmai-niku soba (small?) ¥400　Reasonable, isn't it
The bonito-based soup is delicious 😄, the noodles are medium-thin, and the kubu (knotted kelp) and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) have soaked up the flavor and are tender and tasty.
Rating (9/15): Among Nago soba, Miyazato Soba is famous. You can't go wrong. The map also introduces their "toast" and "spaghetti."

屋台の焼き鳥 トリおじさん.name: Yatai no Yakitori Tori Ojisan
屋台の焼き鳥 トリおじさん.desc: A double act: a yakitori shop at night and Okinawa soba at lunch. Its signature is the "Chicken Bean Sprout Soba with Garlic Chili Oil" (¥650) with a soup rich in chicken broth; dissolve the garlic chili oil and the flavor turns spicy. Its reasonable price is part of the appeal.
t: I ate here in October 2023. This shop is a participant in the "13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (Oct 1, 2023 – Feb 29, 2024)," and I went as my 10th of 34 shops 😊
Yatai no Yakitori Tori Ojisan　At a glance, it doesn't look like an Okinawa soba shop (;^ω^)
When I went inside, there were a few customers. It seems to be a yakitori shop at night, and inside it looked like a yakitori counter lol
The "Chicken Bean Sprout Soba with Garlic Chili Oil" introduced in the stamp rally booklet
I decided to order the "Chicken Bean Sprout Soba with Garlic Chili Oil" introduced in the stamp rally booklet.
Menu
Chicken bean sprout soba with garlic chili oil　¥650

First, a sip of the soup. The stamp rally booklet described it as "Serious Okinawa soba made by a yakitori shop. A broth made from chicken and pork," and since it's a yakitori shop, the chicken broth base comes through strongly. Solidly tasty 😁

After tasting the chicken broth soup a few times, I dissolved the garlic and special chili oil that had been placed on top of the bean sprouts into the soup 😊　Then the light chicken broth soup changed into a spicy base. My body heated up and I started sweating (;^ω^)　A nice accent.

The crunchy bean sprouts are topped with shredded chicken from seasoned drumettes, and when you eat the bean sprouts, shredded chicken, and wavy noodles together, the spicy soup clings to them and it's delicious 🤗

Rating (10/15): Solidly tasty. Since it's Okinawa soba from a yakitori shop, the chicken broth soup comes through nicely. When you mix in the garlic and special chili oil, the flavor turns spicy, and that's nice too. At ¥650 it's reasonable in a way other shops aren't, but I thought the shredded chicken topping was a bit on the small side.

山ちゃん食堂.name: Yamachan Shokudo
山ちゃん食堂.desc: A local diner serving Okinawan cuisine. Homestyle Okinawa soba with a blended pork bone × bonito broth where the pork bone comes through, and medium-thick straight noodles, reasonably priced at ¥600 for a large. The soki soba advertised on the banner being sold out is all part of the charm.
t: I went to eat here in November 2023 😊　It was during the "13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (Oct 1, 2023 – Feb 29, 2024)," so I wanted to eat at a participating shop, but there were no participating shops in the area where I had errands, so I tried eating at this diner I happened to find 😆
Yamachan Shokudo
Menu
Menu
When I went inside, they had only just opened for the day, but several local customers were already seated at tables.

The menu on the wall had "Soki Soba," and the banner outside also said "Soki Soba," so I ordered the "Soki Soba," and the reply was "We don't have it" (^0^;)　"Huh?" I was surprised right off the bat, but this diner isn't an Okinawa soba specialty shop; it's an ordinary diner serving Okinawan cuisine, so I double-checked whether they had no "Okinawa soba"-related items at all, and they said they did have "Okinawa Soba," so I ordered that 😆　Anyway, that was a relief.
Okinawa soba (large)　¥600
The Okinawa soba arrived 😆　First, a sip of the soup. It's a blended broth of pork bone and bonito, a soup where the pork bone comes through. It's ordinary.
Next, the noodles. The medium-thick straight noodles are soft. It's homestyle, very ordinary Okinawa soba. The braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) had a bit of sinewy texture.

Rating (8.5/15): It was homestyle, ordinary Okinawa soba 😄　I ordered the large, but partly because the price was a reasonable ¥600, the portion didn't seem that big. I couldn't help laughing that even though the banner outside advertises "Soki Soba," they don't sell it 😆

山原そば.name: Yanbaru Soba
山原そば.desc: A popular shop with lines, marked by an old house with cement tiles in Izumi on the Soba Highway. The distinctive dark-colored soup reminiscent of Tojin soba and the chewy, characterful pork spare ribs (soki) set it apart from other shops.
t: *This article was created with AI (Claude Sonnet 4) and partly added to by me lol
I ate here in December 2024 😆　This time I made my way to "Yanbaru Soba" in Izumi, Motobu Town! I'd actually been curious about this shop for a while, and I was finally able to visit ✨
Yanbaru Soba
Yanbaru Soba

As you can see, it has a very characterful exterior like an old house. It's a very Okinawan building with cement tiles, with an appearance that truly lets you feel the atmosphere of "Yanbaru" 🏠　The surroundings are peaceful country roads, which also add to its feel as a famous shop.
The sign in front of the shop says "Yanbaru Soba," and you get the sense that it's a soba shop rooted in the local community. There's a parking lot too, so access by car is easy 🚗
Menu posted inside the shop
Inside, lots of handwritten menus are posted on the walls, and it has a very homey atmosphere.
This time I ordered the "Soki Soba," which you could call the signature item. Lots of tourists were coming in too, and the shop was quite busy 😄
Soki soba　¥1,000
After waiting a while, a steaming soki soba was brought out. It looks simple, but big pork spare ribs (soki) sit on top with a thud, and it's very voluminous!
First, as usual, the soup 🍜　Taking a sip... this is interesting! The soup's color is quite dark, and I feel it resembles "Tojin soba," the roots of Okinawa soba.

In terms of flavor, it has a distinctive taste a little different from the usual pork bone or bonito broth. You can taste some sweetness too, and my impression was that maybe it's soy sauce-based? It's quite a unique soup that I've never tasted at other shops. Opinions might be divided on this, but I found it interesting 😋
Soki soba　¥1,000
Next, I try the noodles. Medium-thick straight noodles with a softish texture.

And the pork spare ribs (soki) I was curious about... these were distinctive too! When I ate them, they were quite chewy, with a solid sinewy texture remaining. The texture was clearly different from the pork spare ribs (soki) at other shops; it was a type of pork spare ribs (soki) I'd never eaten before. Maybe the cooking method or cut is different 🤔

Honestly, the texture of these pork spare ribs (soki) was a first-time experience for me. It might be a bit surprising for people used to tenderly stewed pork spare ribs (soki), but I think this is interesting in its own way as part of "Yanbaru Soba's" personality.

Looking around the shop, lots of tourists were coming in, which shows how popular it is. Since it's in the tourist area of Motobu Town, I imagine many people stop by after sightseeing at places like the Churaumi Aquarium or the Bise Fukugi Tree Road 🐠
Also, JUNGLIA OKINAWA, which opened on July 25, 2025, is close by too 😄
It seems to be loved by the locals too, and I spotted a few customers who looked like regulars. You can really tell it's cherished as a shop rooted in the community.

My overall impression is that this shop serves a distinctive style of Okinawa soba that sets it apart from other shops. Both the soup and the pork spare ribs (soki) were characterful creations that defied expectations in a good way. If you love Okinawa soba, I think it's worth experiencing at least once 👍

Rating (9/15): Solidly tasty. If you have the chance to visit Motobu Town, be sure to drop by. It's not that far from the Churaumi Aquarium or JUNGLIA, so it's an easy location to stop by while sightseeing. However, it's a popular shop and can get crowded, so I recommend visiting with plenty of time to spare ⏰　I'm satisfied to have come across delicious Okinawa soba again this time! Next time I'll explore yet another shop, so stay tuned〜😊

我流そば.name: Garyu Soba
我流そば.desc: An Okinawa soba shop attached to the pachinko and slot parlor "LUXOR Nago" in Miyazato, Nago City. Reasonably priced at ¥550, it's a homestyle bowl with a pork bone-based soup topped with luncheon pork.
t: I ate here in April 2023😄　It was my first time at an Okinawa soba shop attached to a pachinko parlor lol
Garyu Soba　Looks like a place for pachinko and slot players to eat lol
I ordered the "Garyu Soba," which has the same name as the shop.
Garyu Soba　¥550

At ¥550 it's reasonably priced. As for the taste, the soup is pork bone-based, and the noodles are a softish flat type. The braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) is tender too and perfectly tasty. With luncheon pork on top, it has a homestyle look and taste.
Rating (9/15): A very, very ordinary Okinawa soba. Perfectly tasty😄

我部祖河食堂本店.name: Gabusoka Shokudo Main Branch
我部祖河食堂本店.desc: A famous Okinawa soba shop (the main branch along Prefectural Route 71) that bills itself as the "original soki soba." Plenty of tender pork spare ribs (soki) simmered for hours in a secret sweet sauce, a rich pork bone blend soup and medium-thin noodles. It has branches in many areas.
t: It was introduced in the "Nago City Soba Map," so I ate here in October 2020😄
Gabusoka Shokudo Main Branch (along Prefectural Route 71)
"Gabusoka Shokudo Main Branch" is introduced as shop 31 of 41 in the "Nago Soba Map"
I ordered the "soki soba" introduced on the map😄　According to the map, this shop calls itself the "original soki soba." It's another famous shop.
Soki soba　¥800

I'm happy there's plenty of tender pork spare ribs (soki) simmered for hours in a secret sweet sauce😄　The original rich soup, blended from lots of pork bones, goes well with the medium-thin noodles and is delicious😋
Rating (9/15): A famous Okinawa soba shop. I think it's perfectly tasty. There are "Gabusoka Shokudo" shops in other areas too, so why not give one a try?

新山そば.name: Arayama Soba
新山そば.desc: A renowned long-established shop founded in 1925 (Taisho 14), said to be the birthplace of Nago-style soba (flat noodles and knotted kombu). A light bonito-based soup with flat noodles, and its specialty is the jiggly, collagen-packed pig's feet (tebichi) soba.
t: It was introduced in the "Nago City Soba Map," so I ate here in July 2020😄
Arayama Soba　This one's famous too. A long-established shop.
"Arayama Soba" is introduced as shop 15 of 41 in the "Nago Soba Map"
I ordered the "tebichi soba" introduced on the map
Pig's feet (tebichi) soba　¥700

The pig's feet (tebichi) are jiggly and packed with collagen, melt-in-your-mouth and delicious😋　True to the Nago style, there's knotted kombu in it too. The noodles are flat, a characteristic of Nago soba, and the soup is bonito-based, light and tasty😄
Rating (9/15): Arayama Soba is also famous among Nago's soba shops. You can't go wrong. The cups look like "One Cup Ozeki?" sake cups, so it feels like you're drinking lol

月桃華（サンニンばな）.name: Sannin-bana
月桃華（サンニンばな）.desc: A homey one-person-run shop tucked away quietly in a residential area. A reassuring soup with a strong bonito broth, and you can choose between fresh noodles and pre-boiled noodles. The complimentary fuchiba (mugwort) and the kōrēgūsu (chili-infused awamori) let you enjoy three different flavors.
t: *This article was created with the AI Claude 4 Sonnet, with some additions of my own.
I ate here in December 2024😄 I went to "Sannin-bana" in Nishizaki, Itoman City😊
Sannin-bana

At first glance the exterior looks like an ordinary diner, and the words "Okinawa soba" on the red sign catch the eye. The building stands quietly in a residential area, with an atmosphere that suggests it's loved by the locals✨

There's parking for only two cars in front of the shop, so at lunchtime you'll probably have to wait a bit. In fact, when I visited there were customers ahead of me, and I waited a little for a parking space to open up😅
The menu posted inside the shop

Inside, there's a warm atmosphere with the warmth of wood. There are counter seats and table seats, and the kitchen is close by, giving it a homey feel. The owner seems to run the place single-handedly, and you can tell each bowl is made with care👨‍🍳
Menu
Menu
Looking at the menu, there's a simple lineup of basic Okinawa soba. The prices are reasonable too, and I like that it's a place local people can casually drop in to💰
This time I ordered the "Soki Soba (Large)" for ¥980. At this shop you can choose your noodles, either fresh noodles or pre-boiled noodles. Since I was there, I asked for the fresh noodles🍜
The "soki soba" arrived. It looks really simple, giving the impression of an old-fashioned Okinawa soba. The bowl is rustic too, and you can feel a homey warmth🍲
Soki soba large　¥980 (*fuchiba free)
First, as is my custom, a sip of the soup. A soup with a strong bonito broth, giving you that reassuring feeling of "Ah, this is Okinawa soba"😌
Soki soba large　¥980
After the soup, I dig into the noodles. The fresh noodles I chose are a thin straight type, with a softish texture🍝
The pork spare ribs (soki) topping is seasoned on the sweet side, but unfortunately there were some parts with small bones left in. That made it a little hard to eat😅

Partway through I tried adding the fuchiba (mugwort) they gave me for free. Its distinctive bitterness and aroma are added to the soup, letting you enjoy a healthy-feeling change of flavor. It's a traditional Okinawan way of eating, and this bitterness makes a nice accent🌿

In the latter half I also added a little of the kōrēgūsu (chili-infused awamori) on the table and enjoyed a spicy change of flavor too. That way I got to enjoy three different flavors and ate it all the way to the end without getting bored🌶️
Looking around the shop, there are many local customers, and you can clearly see it's a shop loved by the community.
From the outside it gave the impression of an ordinary diner, but when I actually ate, it was a pretty authentic Okinawa soba✨
However, since there's parking for only two cars and the owner runs the shop single-handedly, you'll probably have to wait a bit when it's busy. I recommend visiting with some time to spare⏰

Rating (9/15): Overall, my impression is of a warm, community-based Okinawa soba shop, and it's surprisingly authentic. It doesn't have any especially standout features, but you can enjoy a carefully made Okinawa soba with a reassuring taste. When you're in the Nishizaki area of Itoman City, why not stop by once?😊

月黒木（つきくるち）.name: Tsukikuruchi
月黒木（つきくるち）.desc: An Okinawa soba specialty shop in Enobi, Uruma City, opened in 2022. The cloudy, rich pork bone soup, slowly simmered from Okinawa-raised pork bones, is smooth with no gamey smell. Melt-in-your-mouth soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) and thinnish straight noodles. A hideaway-like shop with a low-key sign, so be careful not to drive past it.
t: I went to eat here in November 2023😊　Since it was during the "13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (2023.10.1 to 2024.2.29)," I wanted to eat at a participating shop, but I had already eaten at and cleared the participating shops around Uruma City, where I had errands, so even though it's not part of the stamp rally, I decided to eat at this shop since I'd been curious about it for a while.
Tsukikuruchi　There's no sign (;^ω^)

Tsukikuruchi is about one door down from "Shima Soba," where I ate before, but the road in front of the shop isn't very congested, so cars tend to go fairly fast and it's easy to drive past it (;^ω^)　It's not so much that there's no sign as that it doesn't stand out; Shima Soba is easier to spot.
Besides the parking lot in front of the shop, there's a second parking lot beside the shop that you go down a steep slope to reach. There's a small sign there, but it doesn't stand out (;^ω^)
Inside, a meal ticket machine was installed near the entrance. This shop is cash only too lol　I wish all Okinawa soba shops would hurry up and go cashless; I think it would help with efficiency (lol)
This time I ordered the "Soki Soba (Medium? Regular?)".
Soki soba (Medium? Regular?)　¥890
According to what I'd googled beforehand, the soup is a "rich pork bone broth." The color is a bit cloudy too, and it certainly looks pork bone-based.

First, as is my custom, a sip of the soup. It's definitely a pork bone broth. What's more, there's no gamey smell, and it's finished quite smooth. I thought it was tastier than the soup at "Kame Soba" with its agu pork broth, which I ate before, but I felt it didn't have the rich creaminess of "796 (Nankuru)," which I've introduced as my provisional #4 recommendation.
Soki soba (Medium? Regular?)　¥890

Next, the noodles. They're a thinnish straight type. On the soft side. The topping is soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki). They're very tender, practically melting, and perfectly tasty, but the flavor is on the light side and wasn't quite enough for me.

In the latter half I added kōrēgūsu (chili-infused awamori) to the soup to change up the flavor. I enjoyed it that way too, but the richness of the pork bone disappears and it becomes spicy, so if you want to savor the smoothness, it might be better not to add it.
Rating (9/15): Perfectly tasty. The pork bone soup is reasonably smooth and delicious. It opened in 2022, and the inside is clean too. Why not give this shop a try once?

本家亀そば わかさ店.name: Honke Kame Soba　Wakasa Branch
本家亀そば わかさ店.desc: A Kame Soba directly managed shop near Naminoue Shrine. A light, gentle agu pork broth with thin noodles from Kamehama Noodle Factory. Its signature is the meat and vegetable soba introduced in the stamp rally, and it also accepts cashless QR payments.
t: I ate here in December 2023. This shop is a participant in the "13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (2023.10.1 to 2024.2.29)," and I went as my 26th of 34 shops😊
Honke Kame Soba　Wakasa Branch
The meal ticket machine at the shop entrance
Inside there's a meal ticket machine, and this time I decided to order the "Meat and Vegetable Soba" introduced in the stamp rally booklet.
I thought, "Cash only again?", but in the upper right there were several kinds of QR codes😆
When I tried to scan the QR code with my phone to pay with PayPay, the manager asked, "PayPay?" I answered "Yes," and he asked, "What would you like to order?"
I told him, "Meat and vegetable soba, please," and was instructed, "Please enter ¥850" lol　I scanned the QR code, entered ¥850, and payment was complete.
It's great that they can handle cashless payments👍
The menu posted inside the shop
A sign explaining their commitment to the soba
It's a different shop, but I've eaten Kame Soba at "Kame Soba (Kitanaka branch)" in Kitanakagusuku Village, so I could more or less imagine the taste.
Meat and vegetable soba　¥850

First, a sip of the soup. Since it's vegetable soba this time, the flavor of the vegetables blends into the soup, making it somehow hard to tell (^0^;)　After drinking just the soup a few times, it's the same as what I had at the Kitanaka branch before: the agu pork broth is light and gentle. The sign posted in the shop said the soup is "full-bodied," but I thought it was more on the light side. Still, it's perfectly tasty.
Meat and vegetable soba　¥850

Next, the noodles. They're a thin straight type. The sign in the shop said "We use firm thin noodles from Kamehama Noodle Factory made from three blended flours," but I thought the texture was, if anything, on the soft side.
The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) are jiggly and perfectly tasty. However, the braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) had a bit of a sinewy texture.

Rating (9/15): Perfectly tasty. It tasted better to me than the Kame Soba Kitanaka branch I ate at before. It's near Naminoue Shrine and Naminoue Beach, so when you come sightseeing, why not try this shop too?😁

東江そば.name: Agarie Soba
東江そば.desc: The renowned long-established Urasoe main branch, on the second floor along the national highway. The signature Agarie Soba comes with braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), pork spare ribs (soki) and soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) all in one, with a clear soup with a strong bonito broth and homemade medium-thick wavy noodles; there are many celebrity autographs too.
t: *This article was created with the AI Claude Sonnet 4, with some additions of my own.
I went to eat here in January 2025😄 This time I visited the renowned long-established shop "Agarie Soba Urasoe Main Branch" in Jitchaku, Urasoe City 😊
Agarie Soba Urasoe Main Branch
Agarie Soba Urasoe Main Branch
Agarie Soba Urasoe Main Branch

The shop is on the second floor of a building along the national highway, and the words "Agarie Soba" on the big white sign really stand out 🏪 There are pink banners on the road too, so even first-timers shouldn't get lost. You go up the stairs to the second floor, and the well-worn building has the dignity of a long-established shop. It was lunchtime on a weekday, but there's plenty of parking, so access by car is good 🚗
The meal ticket machine near the shop entrance

When you go in, the first thing you see is the meal ticket machine 🎫 Looking at the menu, there's a wide variety, including Agarie soba, sanmai-niku soba, nankotsu soki soba, vegetable soba and hon-soki soba. Prices are fair, around ¥850 to ¥1,000 for a medium, and even a large is reasonable at ¥950 to ¥1,100. This time I ordered the signature "Agarie Soba (Medium)" for ¥1,000 💰

The seating is a tatami-floored raised area, with a very relaxed atmosphere 🏮 Lots of celebrity autographs hang on the walls, which makes it clear that this really is a popular shop. There's a TV too, making it a space where you can enjoy your meal at a leisurely pace. You can see the scenery outside through the windows, so it feels open too 🪟 The windows showed that it opens at 10:30 and closes at 16:00 on weekdays and 17:00 on weekends 🕐
Inside the shop
Inside the shop
Inside the shop
Agarie soba medium　¥1,000

The Agarie soba that was brought out after a while had an amazing volume of toppings just from the look of it!😋 It's a luxurious bowl with all of Agarie soba's signature toppings: braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), pork spare ribs (soki) and soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki). First I tasted the soup. It's a delicious, clear soup with a strong bonito broth 🐟
Agarie soba medium　¥1,000

The noodles are homemade fresh noodles, a medium-thick wavy type 🍝 The firmness is so-so, cooked to an exquisite doneness that's neither too soft nor too hard. The waves cling well to the soup, creating a delicious sense of unity.

As for toppings, there were three kinds of pork: braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), pork spare ribs (soki) and soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) 🥩 All were simmered to a moderate tenderness, and the flavor had soaked in well. However, the soki and sanmai-niku had some parts with a slight sinewy texture remaining. They weren't completely melt-in-your-mouth, but they were at a level you can enjoy well enough. The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) were especially tender, simmered to the point where the meat comes right off the bone, which was wonderful 👏

Agarie Soba was certainly a delicious Okinawa soba with the dignity of a long-established shop 🌟 The bonito broth in the soup was especially wonderful, and I can well understand why so many celebrities love it. The noodles are carefully made, as you'd expect from homemade noodles, and the volume of toppings is impeccable. However, if you ask whether it's perfect, the parts with a slight sinewy texture bother me a little, but even so, it's an Okinawa soba well within the "pretty tasty" level 😊

Rating (10.5/15): It's perfectly tasty. Access from the national highway in Jitchaku, Urasoe City is good. Agarie Soba Urasoe Main Branch was a shop where I could clearly see why it continues to be loved by so many people as a long-established name in the Okinawa soba world 🏆 It serves a highly satisfying bowl with a refined soup with a strong bonito broth and a hearty volume of toppings. It's a shop I'd like both Okinawa soba beginners and veterans to try at least once. When you're looking for Okinawa soba in the Urasoe area, please do pay a visit to Agarie Soba 👍

根夢.name: Gon
根夢.desc: Gon Isa branch, one street toward the sea from the Route 58 Ginowan Bypass. Its signature is soki soba with medium-thin straight noodles in a soup with a strong bonito broth. A shop loved by local customers.
t: I went to eat here in June 2022😄
Gon　　On the street one block toward the sea from the Route 58 Ginowan Bypass
I ordered the "soki soba" from the menu
Menu
Soki soba　¥730
The bonito broth is strong and delicious😄　The noodles are a medium-thin straight type, and the pork spare ribs (soki) were perfectly tasty too.
Rating (9/15): Perfectly tasty. It's loved by local customers, which is nice😄

民芸食堂.name: Mingei Shokudo
民芸食堂.desc: A long-established diner introduced in the booklet as a shop serving "Tojin Soba," the roots of Okinawa soba. The tatami-floored seating area has an old-fashioned atmosphere. Soki soba with homemade Nago-style flat noodles in a gentle blended broth of bonito and pork bone.
t: *This article was created with the AI Claude 3.5 Sonnet, with some additions of my own.
I ate here in November 2024😄 With the goal of visiting every Okinawa soba shop on the main island of Okinawa, I've been eating my way around little by little.
Mingei Shokudo
Mingei Shokudo

This time I'd like to introduce "Mingei Shokudo" in Yonabaru, Yonabaru Town. This shop isn't a participant in the "14th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally," but it was introduced as selling "Tojin Soba," the roots of Okinawa soba, so I got curious and visited😄
The list of shops selling "Tojin Soba" introduced in the 14th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally booklet
Inside the shop
There's also a counter inside
The view outside from the counter

Inside, there's a tatami-floored seating area with the atmosphere of an old-fashioned diner. I visited right at opening time on a Saturday, but several local customers were already waiting, and I could tell it's a popular shop😊
Prices have been revised due to the recent rise in prices, but I think some shops are still quite reasonable.
Menu
Menu
Looking at the menu, it has all the classic Okinawa soba dishes, like "soki soba" and "tebichi soba." This time I decided to order the classic "soki soba"🍜
Soki soba　¥950

First, a sip of the soup. At first, from the clear soup, I thought it was bonito broth, but it's actually a blended broth of bonito and pork bone, a gentle flavor with a subtle touch of pork bone. It's perfectly tasty😋
Soki soba　¥950
Next, the noodles. They use homemade noodles, the flat type often seen in the Nago area. The texture is on the soft side, and they go well with the soup.
The pork spare ribs (soki) topping is lightly seasoned and tender, but there were some spots with a bit of sinewy texture left. Overall, my impression is of an Okinawa soba with gentle seasoning.

Rating (9/15): I got the impression it's a shop loved by local customers. Many customers come in right from opening, and I think many of them are regulars. The taste is perfectly good, but the sinewy texture of the soki bothered me. When you're in Yonabaru Town, why not stop by once to soak up the atmosphere of a diner loved by the locals?😊

沖縄すばゃ垣花そば.name: Okinawa Subaya Kakinohana Soba
沖縄すばゃ垣花そば.desc: A stamp rally participant near Costco Nanjo. A well-balanced blended broth of bonito and pork bone with round thin noodles, and the self-service free fuchiba (mugwort) topping is a welcome touch.
t: *This article was created with AI (ChatGPT 4o), with some additions of my own😁
I ate here in October 2024😆
I visited "Okinawa Subayaa Kakinohana Soba," a participant in the 14th Stamp Rally (2024.10.1 to 2025.2.28)🌟.
Okinawa Subaya Kakinohana Soba
It's taking part in the 14th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally😄
A shop with a relaxed atmosphere standing along the road🏠.
Inside, the self-service corner has fuchiba (mugwort) set out, and a welcome point is that you can add it as a topping for free✨.
Inside the shop (the free fuchiba service😆)

I actually wanted to order the "Kakinohana Soba" introduced in the stamp rally booklet, but since I went in right at opening time (11:00), I was told "It's still being prepared" and gave up (^0^;). So what I had this time was the "nankotsu soki soba"🍜.
Soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) soba　¥850 (*free fuchiba topping)
The soup is a blended broth of bonito and pork bone, a well-balanced flavor in which you can clearly taste both🎣🐷.
Soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) soba　¥850 (*free fuchiba topping)
Next, the noodles. The straight round thin noodles were soft and easy to eat.

The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) were well-seasoned all the way through, and while tender, they still had a bit of sinewy texture🍖. This may be a point where opinions differ, but personally I'd have liked them better with a more melt-in-your-mouth texture💭.
Also, adding the fuchiba as a topping gives it a refreshing aroma and a healthy touch🌿. A free topping service like this really broadens the enjoyment of Okinawa soba😊.

Rating (9/15): All in all, Okinawa Subayaa Kakinohana Soba's nankotsu soki soba was a solid, consistent bowl with a hearty flavor👌. However, I didn't feel any special surprise or personality; my impression is that it's perfectly tasty🤔. This shop is near the Costco that opened on 2024.8.24, so why not try it once for a meal on your way back from Costco?😄
It's plenty satisfying to visit as one of the stamp rally shops, but next time I'd like to try other items on the menu too🎶.

沖縄そばと郷土料理の店 なび家.name: Okinawa Soba and Local Cuisine　Nabiya
沖縄そばと郷土料理の店 なび家.desc: A local cuisine chain inside Urasoe Shopping Center. Its signature is the Yokubari Soba with three toppings: bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki), pig's feet (tebichi) and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku). It also has a good selection of Okinawan snacks to take out, such as sata andagi and popo.
t: *This article was created with AI (Claude Sonnet 4.6), with some additions of my own😁
I went to eat here in March 2025😁😊　This time I went to "Nabiya Urasoe Shopping Center branch" in Gusukuma, Urasoe City😄
Nabiya Urasoe Shopping Center branch
The cover of the menu says "Okinawa soba　Local cuisine"

Speaking of "Nabiya," it's a chain that features Okinawa soba and local cuisine, and besides the Urasoe Shopping Center branch, it has several locations, including the Barclays Court branch and the AEON Haebaru branch.
The menu also has information on the other Nabiya shops

True to its concept of "freshly made local flavors," Okinawan home-style treats such as sata andagi, jushi, chinbin and popo are also sold for takeout, lined up all around the entrance🌺　Even though it's inside a shopping center, it's packed with so much Okinawan character that my mood lifted as soon as I approached the shop.
They also sell Okinawan snacks like sata andagi and popo😄

When I went in, it being lunchtime on a weekday, the place was bustling with local customers. You can gradually feel that it's a shop rooted in the community. The menu has not only Okinawa soba but a wide range of Okinawan home cooking, such as the bitter melon (goya) champuru set meal, the fu champuru set meal, simmered pig's feet (tebichi) and the tuna and marlin set meal, so it seems you can't go wrong with whatever you order😁
