What I ordered this time was the "Yokubari Soba (¥950)," marked "Recommended" on the menu. It's a truly greedy bowl that lets you enjoy three toppings at once: bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki), pig's feet (tebichi) and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku)🍜
Yokubari soba　¥950

Looking at the bowl as soon as it arrived, it's heaped with leafy greens and green onions, so it looks lively. First, as is my custom, a sip of the soup. It seems to be a blended broth of pork bone and bonito, but none of the broths really asserts itself. There are no sharp edges; it's an "ordinary taste."
Yokubari soba　¥950
The noodles are medium-thick and slightly wavy, with a pretty soft texture. Personally I'd be happier if they had a bit more chewiness.

As for toppings, having the three kinds, bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki), pig's feet (tebichi) and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), is the real appeal of the "Yokubari Soba"✨　However, to be honest, all three still had a somewhat sinewy texture, and I got the impression they fell a little short in terms of tenderness and how well the flavor had soaked in😅　There's plenty of knotted kombu and leafy greens too, so the volume of toppings itself is ample.

What I feel throughout the shop is that it's established itself as "a place for everyday local meals." It's a shop that plays the role of somewhere people in the area can quickly drop in for lunch. Seeing the wide range of local cuisine on the menu and the abundance of takeout sweets, that feeling comes across well🌺

Rating (9/15): As you'd expect from a chain, "Nabiya" is consistent, but it doesn't really have an outstanding personality, so I thought it was an ordinary bowl. That said, it's an easy-to-eat, easy-to-visit shop, and it's no wonder it's bustling with locals😊　When you come to the Urasoe area and suddenly feel like eating Okinawa soba, why not stop by?

沖縄そばゆい.name: Okinawa Soba Yui
沖縄そばゆい.desc: A calm, modern-Japanese-style shop one street off Route 58. Its signature is the Yui Soba, loaded with braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) and bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki) in a well-balanced blended broth of bonito and pork bone. At lunch, jushi is a good deal.
t: *This article was created with the AI Claude 3.5 Sonnet, with some additions of my own.
I ate here in September 2024😄　This time I'd like to introduce "Okinawa Soba Yui" in Uchidomari, Ginowan City.
Yui
Yui (the sign seems to have disappeared (^0^;))

This shop is in a quiet spot one street in from Route 58. The "Okinawan cuisine" sign at the entrance serves as a landmark. Inside, it has a calm, modern Japanese atmosphere, with an impressive interior based on wood grain. The bamboo on the ceiling and the lighting are atmospheric and lovely too😊
Inside the shop
The meal ticket machine near the shop entrance
Menu
Menu
The menu centers on Okinawa soba, with a wide selection including yushi-dofu (soft Okinawan tofu) soba. This time I decided to order the "Yui Soba" (¥1,000), which bears the shop's name.
Yui soba　¥1,000

After waiting a while, the Yui soba arrives along with the fragrant aroma of broth🍜　First, the soup. It's a well-balanced blended broth of bonito and pork bone, with the pork bone flavor coming through slightly more.
Yui soba　¥1,000
Next, the noodles. They're medium-thick straight noodles, boiled on the soft side😌

The toppings are plentiful: braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) and bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki). All are simmered tender, but it bothered me that some slightly sinewy parts remained. The chopped green onion topping adds an accent and nice color too.
Local customers and tourists were visiting, and the shop seemed lively. Apparently jushi is cheaper at lunchtime, so it's a good deal too😄

Rating (9/15): My impression is of a perfectly tasty Okinawa soba. The calm interior has a nice atmosphere where you can enjoy your meal at a leisurely pace. When you're in Ginowan City, why not stop by once?😊

沖縄そば食堂よねはま.name: Okinawa Soba Shokudo Yonehama
沖縄そば食堂よねはま.desc: Although it's a diner attached to a pachinko parlor, the menu is incredibly extensive (the ticket machine is packed with buttons!). A distinctive feature is that you can choose your soup from bonito broth or pork bone broth, and the No.1 most popular item is the salt nankotsu soki soba topped with big soft-bone pork ribs.
t: *This article was created with AI (ChatGPT 5.2 Thinking), with some additions of my own😆
I ate here in February 2025😄　I went on my Okinawa soba tour in Oyama, Ginowan City🍜　This time I visited "Okinawa Soba Shokudo Yonehama."
Okinawa Soba Shokudo Yonehama
Okinawa Soba Shokudo Yonehama
From the outside it has a real "diner" feel, and it's located next to a pachinko parlor, which reminds me a little of "Garyu Soba" in Nago~😊
This is Garyu Soba in Nago City😆

The yellow sign at the entrance stands out, so it's easy to find even on your first visit, which is great. When you enter, it's ticket machine style first, and there are so many buttons that you go "Whoa, that's a lot of menu items!"😂　There are all kinds of soba alone, plus yakisoba, curry dishes, and even rice bowls and set meal-type dishes, so it's very extensive.

From the many menu items, I pressed the button for the "Salt Nankotsu Soki Soba," which was billed as the No.1 most popular.
What's interesting here is that you can choose your soup from "bonito broth" or "pork bone broth." As usual, I chose the bonito broth.
Salt nankotsu soki soba large (bonito broth)　¥950

First, a sip of the soup. The moment I drank it, imagining my usual bonito broth, I went, "Oh, this isn't the 100% bonito I expected." There's definitely bonito flavor, but the "blended broth" aspect was stronger than I expected, and I thought it was a soup where you can taste pork bone broth too.
Salt nankotsu soki soba large (bonito broth)　¥950
The noodles are thin and straight, with a pretty soft texture.
And then the star, the soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki). Big chunky ones on top got me excited, but the seasoning is on the light side.

The atmosphere inside is that of an unpretentious diner, so it's easy to walk into. Customers come and go at a decent pace, and when I happened to look around, everyone was ordering the pork bone broth...! That bothered me a little😂　I honestly found myself thinking, maybe the real star is the pork bone broth? Even choosing bonito I could sense pork bone, so if you choose pork bone, maybe what they're "pushing" is easier to understand. Next time I go, I'll want to go with pork bone and try a different menu item.

Rating (9/15): My honest opinion is that this time's bonito broth salt nankotsu soki soba was less "totally hits the spot!" and more "a perfectly tasty Okinawa soba"😊　Some people might be wary when they hear it's attached to a pachinko parlor, but it's easy to pop into~. Next time I want to try the pork bone broth everyone was ordering🍜✨

沖縄そば鶴亀.name: Okinawa Soba Tsurukame
沖縄そば鶴亀.desc: A shop with an old-fashioned storefront in Makiminato, Urasoe City. The rare "order tags" hanging on the wall give it the feel of a long-established shop. A classic soki soba soup with a strong bonito broth, and with complimentary jushi it's hearty and filling.
t: *This article was created with the AI Claude 3.5 Sonnet, with some additions of my own.
I keep eating my way around every day to conquer all the Okinawa soba shops on the main island of Okinawa😄 I went to eat here in September 2024😄
This time I visited "Tsurukame" in Makiminato, Urasoe City.
Okinawa Soba Tsurukame
The "order tags" hanging on the wall are unusual😄

The storefront has an old-fashioned look, and the characters "中縄 soba" on the white wall are striking😊 Inside, order tags hang on the wall, and you can tell they still cherish the old-fashioned way of doing business.

From the menu, I decided to order the classic "soki soba." When I took an order tag and tried to order, the manager said, "That's okay." In the end, the order tag wasn't needed, and I could order verbally (^0^;)
The menu posted on the wall
Soki soba large　¥900
The soki soba is here😆　Tasting the soup first, it has a strong bonito broth, a perfectly tasty soup typical of Okinawa soba😋
Soki soba large　¥900

The noodles are a medium-thick straight type with a softish texture. The pork spare ribs (soki) topping is seasoned on the sweet side, also a classic flavor. However, some parts had a bit of sinewy texture left.

Since I ordered the "large" this time, there's plenty of volume. On top of that, jushi came complimentary, lightly seasoned, and I enjoyed it as perfectly tasty too. I finished everything including the jushi and was stuffed😆
The complimentary jushi

Rating (9/15): It's perfectly tasty. It's a shop where you can enjoy Okinawa soba at a leisurely pace while feeling the atmosphere of a long-established shop. When you come to Urasoe City, why not stop by once?😊

沖縄ポークそば.name: Okinawa Pork Soba
沖縄ポークそば.desc: A shop that was in the fiercely competitive Tsuboya area of Naha, near EIBUN. Its pork bone-based rich soki soba features exquisite charcoal-seared soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), with high-level toppings and noodles. *There are reports that it closed around May 2024.
t: *Please note that as of May 2024 there are reports that it has closed. It's a shame, since it was one of the Okinawa soba shops I really thought was delicious (;｡;)
I ate here in October 2023. This shop is a participant in the "13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (2023.10.1 to 2024.2.29)," and I went as my 6th of 34 shops😊
Okinawa Pork Soba. It's near EIBUN, my provisional #1 recommendation. Tsuboya in Naha City is a fiercely competitive area for Okinawa soba🤗
It seems it only just opened in April 2023 (R5.4). It also seems to have been introduced on the YouTube channel of Okinawa-born Gori of Garage Sale
It was lunchtime, and EIBUN, my provisional #1 recommendation, had its usual line of customers, but this place was empty. I felt that word about the shop hadn't spread yet.
I decided to order the "Rich Soki Soba" introduced in the stamp rally booklet😁
A meal ticket machine is installed at the shop entrance. I'd decided to order the soba introduced in the stamp rally booklet, so I selected the "Rich Soki Soba."

This ticket machine supports smartphone payment, so I paid with "Rakuten Pay." I earn Rakuten points while paying, which effectively gives me cashback, so cashless payment really is great✌　I hope all Okinawa soba shops go cashless soon🙏
Rich soki soba (no extra toppings)　¥1,200
Apparently the thick fresh noodles take a little while to boil, so even though there were few customers, it seemed to take a bit of time.
They said they could give me a small bowl of jushi for free, so I asked for jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice) too😊
After waiting a while, the rich soki soba arrived lol　Imagining something very rich from the dish name and the color of the soup, I took my customary sip of the soup.

However, it wasn't the rich taste I expected, but a light pork bone-based soup (;^ω^)　I'd been imagining a rich soup like that of "796 (Nankuru)," my provisional #4 recommendation, whose agu broth soup I personally consider the provisional No.1, so I felt a bit let down (;^ω^)

But the toppings, spinach and a seasoned soft-boiled egg (runny yolk), are delicious😋　It feels like they were inspired by ramen toppings. Also, the soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) that came on a separate plate were seared over charcoal, and you could taste the charcoal in both aroma and flavor, which was the best. The toppings are of a higher level than at the other shops I've eaten at so far😊
The thick fresh noodles are nicely chewy and delicious too. I thought they were high-level, just like the toppings.

The topping menu. I didn't add any extra toppings this time, but they look like ramen toppings. The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) were seared over charcoal and very delicious. The spinach is tasty too
That's 6 stamp rally stamps collected~ lol　I'll keep plugging away

Rating (12/15): I thought the toppings and noodles were high-level. Along with EIBUN, the delicious Okinawa soba shops in the Tsuboya area of Naha City are really pushing each other to improve. The soup is lighter than it looks, but adding the green chili condiment changed the flavor and boosted the umami of the soup, making it even more delicious. Please do try this shop too.

結バル.name: Yui Baru
結バル.desc: Under the Route 58 Aja overpass, a shop that serves Okinawa soba by day and is an izakaya by night. The standalone soki soba is ¥580 and comes with a small side dish, salad and even a drink, amazing value for money. A shop run as part of an employment support program that makes you want to support it.
t: I ate here in January 2024. This shop is a participant in the "13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (2023.10.1 to 2024.2.29)," and I went as my 34th of 34 shops😊　At last I've cleared every shop in the stamp rally🎉㊗🎊
The stamps from all 34 stamp rally shops😁　Finally a full clear.
However, my goal is to visit every Okinawa soba shop on the main island of Okinawa, so I'll keep eating my way around steadily and quietly from here on😆
Yui Baru (under the Route 58 Aja overpass)
Inside the shop
This shop seems to operate as an izakaya at night too, and the inside is fairly spacious.
Menu (every item is reasonably priced. What's more, for the daily special?, rice and miso soup come with one free refill😄)

As for my order, I decided to order the "soki soba" introduced in the stamp rally. The menu in the photo above shows ¥680 for the soki soba set meal, but as a standalone item it was even cheaper at ¥580 (^0^;)
I only wanted to eat soba, so I decided to order the standalone "soki soba"😆

Soki soba (standalone) ¥580 (it came with a small dish of komatsuna greens and, hidden behind the soba so you can't see it, a shredded cabbage salad, and even a drink. Even as a reasonably priced standalone item, it's hearty. What would have come with it if I'd ordered the set meal?😁)
First, a sip of the soup. It has a strong bonito broth and is perfectly tasty😁
Soki soba (standalone) ¥580
The noodles are medium-thick with a slight wave. They're soft and also perfectly tasty. The pork spare ribs (soki) topping is large for the price and hearty too.

Rating (9/15): Perfectly tasty, and on top of the reasonable price it comes with a small side dish and salad, so it's a good deal😁　Also, this shop apparently operates as part of an employment support program, and the staff, people in the employment support program, take orders earnestly and serve customers politely. There was also a donation box for the employment support program in the shop, so why not visit once to show your support?

貝出汁沖縄そばキセキ.name: Kaidashi Okinawa Soba Kiseki
貝出汁沖縄そばキセキ.desc: A stylish, popular shop that uses a LINE queuing system. A new-style bowl of creamy pork-bone white broth combined with shellfish broth, topped with fried burdock and black wood-ear mushrooms. There is also a Chatan branch in American Village that serves a rich shrimp broth.
t: ― Urasoe Branch (November 2023) ―
I ate here in November 2023. This shop is a participant in the "13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (Oct 1, 2023 – Feb 29, 2024)," and I went as the 15th shop out of 34 😊
"Kaidashi Okinawa Soba Kiseki." It was lunchtime, and even though it was a weekday, a lot of customers were lined up.

This shop has its own parking lot, and there are also several parking spaces right across from it (in the photo), but lots of customers were lined up near the entrance. It was lunchtime, but it was a weekday, so you can tell it's a hugely popular shop.
However, since people were sitting on the benches outside, I couldn't tell whether they were customers resting after eating or people waiting, so I went inside and asked a staff member.
I was told to add the shop as a friend on LINE using the QR code near the entrance and wait for my turn that way.
The QR code for queuing, set up at the entrance

Registering your place in line through LINE feels really cutting-edge, which is nice 🤗 I've been to about 100 Okinawa soba shops so far (as of November 2023), but this is the first time I've seen a system like this. Making good use of technology, nice.
I registered by following the LINE steps. I was set as the 5th customer in line lol

When my turn came, I got a notification on LINE. After receiving it and going inside, a staff member explained the various menu items in front of the ticket machine. It seems they do this because it's a new shop.
The interior is new and stylish too, and there was even a young woman dining alone. I noticed a mix of customers, such as office workers from the area and young women.
In the middle of the staff member's explanation, I said, "I'll order the Okinawa soba introduced in the stamp rally booklet," and decided to order the "Kaidashi Okinawa Soba (single item)."

However, while the queue registration uses LINE and all that technology, the ticket machine is, amazingly, cash only (;^ω^) Since they've gone this far, I wish they'd add cashless payment here too. It's a new shop, so I found this part disappointing.
I decided to order the "Kaidashi Okinawa Soba" introduced in the stamp rally booklet.

In the stamp rally booklet you can apparently choose from "shellfish broth, shrimp broth, and niboshi (dried sardine) broth," but I went with the "shellfish broth," which matches the shop's name and seems to be their pick lol
Explanation panel for the Kaidashi Okinawa Soba
It seems they also offer nationwide shipping 😁

You earn points by registering in the LINE queue. With this visit I got one free topping for my next visit (you can apparently choose from extra green onions, extra noodles, extra shrimp, or extra burdock) 😊 For the maximum of 50 visits, there's a "special gift made with all our heart" — I wonder what that is? 😁
Kaidashi Okinawa Soba (single item)  ¥950
After a little wait, the "Kaidashi Okinawa Soba" I ordered arrived. It looks Instagram-worthy, and it should definitely appeal to female customers.

First, as always, I tasted the soup 😊 I had assumed the white color of this soup came from the shellfish broth, but since the explanation panel says "a perfect balance of creamy pork-bone white broth and shellfish broth...," I think the cloudy white comes from the pork-bone white broth. It reminded me of the cloudy white soup at "Nakaza-ya" in Naha that I ate at before.

When I drank the soup, I had imagined a soup with a strongly pronounced shellfish broth, but the shellfish broth wasn't that noticeable, and the pork-bone white broth base was strong. Since the dish is named "shellfish broth," I felt the shellfish broth could stand out more.
There was quite a bit of shellfish broth aroma coming from inside the shop, so it's a little disappointing (;^ω^)
Kaidashi Okinawa Soba (single item)  ¥950

Next, the noodles. The medium-thick noodles are slightly wavy, and the explanation says "fresh noodles are used, not boiled noodles." However, I didn't really feel the slipperiness and chewy springiness I've experienced from fresh noodles at other shops; they had a rather soft texture.

The toppings feel new and different too 😁 First, the long, thin topping that had caught my eye from the stamp rally booklet photo (lol). I had assumed it was "shellfish?", but according to the explanation panel it's "fried burdock" (;^ω^) When I ate it, it was indeed burdock lol

The black wood-ear mushrooms are also a topping you don't find at other shops. The braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) was tender and tasty in the ordinary way, but although the explanation says it's "seared after the order comes in," I couldn't really detect much of that aroma here either.

The flavor of the seared soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) I had at "Okinawa Pork Soba," which I ate at during the stamp rally the other day and introduced in my "Holds Its Own Against the Recommendations" corner, is still vivid in my memory, so I'm sorry to say this one felt like it lacked impact 🙇

After finishing, I also received a "one-topping service coupon" via LINE notification, and since this shop is apparently a sister shop of the nationwide Hokkaido/Sapporo soup curry specialty restaurant "Rojiura Curry SAMURAI.," they gave me a discount coupon for soup curry.
The "topping service coupon" and the discount coupon for the sister shop (Hokkaido/Sapporo soup curry specialty restaurant "Rojiura Curry SAMURAI.") I received after the meal

Rating (9/15): Well, it's perfectly tasty, but since the shop name says "shellfish broth," I couldn't help thinking the soup would be better with more shellfish broth than pork bone. The atmosphere inside is very stylish and it's a popular shop, but since I came with high expectations, it was a bit disappointing. It was also a pity that the ticket machine doesn't support cashless payment. Also, the expiration date is the end of November 2023, but you can still get the discount coupon for the Hokkaido/Sapporo soup curry specialty restaurant "Rojiura Curry SAMURAI." right now, so why not give it a try? 😊
― Chatan Branch (October 2024) ―
This article was created with AI (ChatGPT 4o) and partly supplemented by me 😁
I ate here in October 2024. This shop is a participant in the "14th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (Oct 1, 2024 – Feb 28, 2025)," and I went as the 1st shop out of 33 😊

It's my first time at "Kaidashi Okinawa Soba Kiseki." since I ate at the Urasoe branch during last year's stamp rally 😆 I didn't know they had opened a second shop in American Village in Mihama, Chatan Town.

"Kaidashi Okinawa Soba Kiseki. Urasoe Branch" was the most popular shop in last year's stamp rally. This Chatan branch is just as attractive, with an equally refined atmosphere ✨ With its stylish exterior that suits a tourist destination, it seems likely to be loved by tourists as well as locals.
Kaidashi Okinawa Soba Kiseki. Chatan Branch (just as stylish as the Urasoe branch)
Menu
Explanation panel
The condiments are stylish too, and look delicious 😄

What I ordered this time was the "Rich Shrimp Broth Okinawa Soba" introduced in the stamp rally booklet, with extra shrimp topping as the staff member recommended, plus an egg and seared braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) (^0^;).
Rich Shrimp Broth Okinawa Soba (extra shrimp topping, added egg, seared braised pork belly)  ¥1,250?
It looks vivid and luxurious right from the start. The colorful toppings and the rich-looking soup blend beautifully in the bowl. I can't help but get my hopes up.

First, a sip of the soup. True to its name, the rich shrimp flavor spreads through my whole mouth 🦐 This fragrant umami is a type you can't easily find in conventional Okinawa soba. I think it's an irresistible bowl for shrimp lovers. However, if you're expecting the flavors typical of Okinawa soba, such as pork bone and bonito flakes, you may be a little surprised. This soup specializes in shrimp, so it comes across as a completely creative-style Okinawa soba.
Rich Shrimp Broth Okinawa Soba (extra shrimp topping, added egg, seared braised pork belly)  ¥1,250?
The noodles were medium-thin, gently wavy fresh noodles, and their softness was distinctive 😊 In some parts I felt they were a little low on chew to stand up to the richness of the soup.

The toppings were impressive too ✨ The presence of the fried burdock is unique again. Its texture and fragrant flavor served as an accent and gave a slightly healthy impression. It's quite an interesting idea.

Also, adding extra shrimp topping further heightened the unity with the soup. Besides its luxurious look, you can enjoy an indulgent feeling that shrimp lovers will love. Overall the balance of toppings was good, and I got the impression that they are proposing a new form of Okinawa soba 🌈
The interior was very stylish, with an atmosphere that seems popular with women and couples 💕 The Urasoe branch was refined too, but the space here at the Chatan branch is just as lovely.

Rating (9/15): So, my overall impression is that it was ordinarily tasty, and the "Rich Shrimp Broth Okinawa Soba" was a very unique and delicious bowl, but for me it settled into an "average" impression 😌 The rich shrimp flavor is distinctive and offers a fresh experience, but it may feel slightly lacking for those seeking the charm of traditional Okinawa soba. Even so, I think this creative soba is worth trying at least once. I'd especially recommend it to shrimp lovers.

赤犬子.name: Akainuko
赤犬子.desc: A late-night Okinawa soba shop in the center of Nago, perfect for a finishing bowl after drinking. The menu is extensive, with plain soba, goat soba, offal soba and more, plus a soup-curry-style curry soba featured on the soba map.
t: ― 2nd Visit (April 2023) ―
In April 2023 I tried again as a finishing meal after drinking ^^;
Akainuko (trying again while drunk ^^;)
This time I ordered the curry soba for ¥800, which was introduced in the soba map
Curry soba  ¥800

After last month, this time I took on the challenge while keeping my drunkenness in check 😄 The soup is a runny soup-curry-style broth and is ordinarily delicious 😋 The noodles are of ordinary thickness, the straight type, and the curry ingredients cling to them nicely.

Rating (9/15): This is a review from a drunk person's palate, but it's ordinarily tasty. How about it as a finishing meal after drinking in the center of Nago lol Be careful not to drink too much (｡>﹏<｡)
― 1st Visit (March 2023) ―
(1st visit) It was introduced in the "Nago City Soba Map," so I ate here in March 2023 😄
Akainuko: The Nago city center where the shop stands is a bar district. This shop is an Okinawa soba shop for a finishing meal after drinking, so it also operates late at night
I went into this shop after getting thoroughly drunk lol My memory is hazy, but when I consulted the owner, he recommended the plain soba, so I ordered the plain soba.
Menu. This shop is featured as 5th out of 41 shops in the "Nago City Soba Map"
Plain soba  ¥800
Sorry, I went into the shop drunk, so I have no memory of the taste lol m(_ _)m
I can't comment, but when I looked at the soba map, a "curry soba" was introduced with a photo, so next time I'll research it again without drinking too much ^^;
Rating (－/15): I'm sorry, I drank too much and have no memory of the taste, so it's unrated. I think it was ordinarily tasty.

赤瓦そば まる屋.name: Akagawara Soba Maruya
赤瓦そば まる屋.desc: The northernmost of the shops participating in the 13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally. A new building with a red-tile roof, serving a pork-bone-based soup with thin straight noodles. Its signature dish is the tsukemen-style "Kawara Soba."
t: I went to eat here in October 2023 😊 How did I find out about this shop? A few days earlier I learned from a local newspaper that the "13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally, 'The Road to Soba Mastery'" was being held from October 1, 2023 to February 29, 2024, and that this shop was a participant, so I came to eat here lol
Akagawara Soba Maruya
Akagawara Soba Maruya: It's apparently only in its 4th year, and the building is new

I wanted to visit every Okinawa soba shop on the main island of Okinawa, and I've been going for about three years now, but I didn't know there was a stamp rally like this (;^ω^) As usual, my antenna is lacking (;^ω^)

I'm told this stamp rally has a record 34 shops entered. Anyway, aiming to complete all the shops within the period, I first came to this "Akagawara Soba Maruya." Among the shops entered this time, it's the northernmost Okinawa soba shop 😁
The stamp rally booklet (front cover)
The stamp rally booklet (back). It has stamp spaces for all 34 shops entered this time. In this age of digitization, an analog format has its charm 👍

From the Okinawa soba section of the menu, I decided to order the "Maruya Soba, Large," which was at the very top. The thing at the top of the menu, called "Kawara Soba," which you eat like tsukemen, seems to be the main selling point. But since I'm aiming to eat ordinary Okinawa soba, I chose from the Okinawa soba section 😁
Menu
Maruya Soba, Large  ¥900
First, my usual sip of the soup. As introduced in the stamp rally, it's definitely pork-bone based 😋 The soup is ordinarily delicious. Next, the noodles.
Maruya Soba, Large  ¥900. The noodles are the thin, straight type
The noodles are fairly soft, thin straight noodles. These are ordinarily delicious too.
Next, the toppings. Pickled red ginger, green onions, fish cake (kamaboko), bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki), braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), and soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki). Quite a lot.
However, the toppings are generous and the meat is tender, but there's a lot of meat with a somewhat sinewy texture.
The introduction of each shop in the stamp rally booklet. This is the 1st shop of the stamp rally lol
Stamp rally shop 1 of 34. There's still a long way to go, but I want to somehow complete them all. I'm looking forward to it
Rating (10/15): The pork-bone-based soup and straight thin noodles were ordinarily delicious 😄 However, the meat has a sinewy texture. Why not join the stamp rally yourselves?

金月そば.name: Kinchichi Soba
金月そば.desc: The Onna branch along Route 58. The in-house fresh noodles boiled after you order are medium-thin straight noodles that are smooth and chewy, and pair superbly with a soup made from 8 kinds of fish flakes. The 2nd shop following the original in Yomitan Village.
t: "Kinchichi Soba (Onna Branch)" along Route 58. Following the original shop in Yomitan Village, this appears to be the 2nd shop. I tried it in August 2022 lol
Kinchichi Soba (Onna Branch) along Route 58
I ordered the Okinawa soba, large (¥800)
Before eating at Kinchichi Soba, from my impression of in-house noodles at other shops, I had the idea that "in-house fresh noodles = strong springiness = firm texture," but I was wrong ^^;

Here, the in-house fresh noodles apparently get boiled once the order comes in. They are medium-thin straight noodles, smooth and chewy, with a texture unlike any shop I've been to so far, and were very delicious 😀
Also, the soup uses 8 kinds of fish flakes, so the seafood flavor and taste are strong, and it pairs superbly with the noodles.
Explanation of Kinchichi Soba's noodles

Rating (12/15): Both the noodles and the soup are distinctive, and it's very tasty. If "Nakamura Soba," also in Onna Village, is crowded and you can't get in, this place is recommended too 😀 Kinchichi Soba also has a shop along Route 58 in Yomitan Village.

首里そば.name: Shuri Soba
首里そば.desc: An extremely popular shop with a line every time. It competes with just one menu item, Shuri Soba in large, medium, and small, and the large is a reasonable ¥600. A light bonito-based soup with thin straight noodles.
t: A friend recommended it, and I ate here in December 2022. Every time I see the shop there's a line, and I think it must be really popular.
Shuri Soba (there's a line every time I see it ^^;)
As Okinawa soba, it competes with just one menu item: "Shuri Soba in large, medium, and small." This time I ordered the large. ¥600 for a large is quite reasonable 😁
Menu
Shuri Soba, large  ¥600
The noodles are the thin straight type. The soup is bonito-based and light. To me, overall the flavor seemed weak.

Rating (8.5/15): Every time I passed the shop there was a line and I couldn't eat there, so given my reasoning up to now that "popular shop = delicious," I went in for the first time with high expectations, but to me it tasted weak overall, which was unexpected ^^; However, the price is more reasonable than other shops.

馬天そば.name: Batten Soba
馬天そば.desc: A hideaway soba shop quietly tucked into a riverside building, with a distinctive entrance. The No. 1 favorite is the mix soba, loaded with chunks of braised pork belly and soft-bone pork ribs. Meltingly tender, sweetish meat and a pork-bone-forward blended broth give it a homey feel.
t: * This article was created by Claude Sonnet 4 AI and partly supplemented by me.
I ate here in December 2024 😄 On the way home from our usual weekend post-surf trip, wanting New Year's Eve soba, I went to "Batten Soba" in Sashiki Shinkai, Nanjo City!
Batten Soba
Batten Soba (the entrance is distinctive (^0^;))

Actually, when I ate at Tebichi no Tesuke last time, I spotted this shop's sign and had been curious ever since. This time I went to eat the "Mix Soba," recommended as the No. 1 favorite at "Batten Soba" in Sashiki Shinkai, Nanjo City, which I found when I ate at Tebichi no Tesuke the other day 😆

First, the location of this shop is quite interesting. It quietly sits on the first floor of a white building along a river, but the entrance is a bit unusual, and it's hard to find unless you're a local 😅

From the outside you'd think "Huh, is this a shop?" It gave the impression of a true hidden-gem Okinawa soba shop known only to those in the know. If the red flag hadn't been fluttering, I'd definitely have driven right past it. But shops like this, rooted in the local community, are surprisingly often delicious ✨ Still, the entrance inside the shop is so distinctive that you can't find it unless you're a local customer 😆
The entrance inside the shop
Inside the shop
Once inside, a more substantial menu than I expected was ready, and it has a great variety too 😋
Menu
Menu

Starting with the "Mix Soba" labeled as the No. 1 favorite, the lineup is quite varied, with soft-bone pork rib soba (nankotsu soki soba), braised pork belly soba (sanmai-niku soba), mazesoba, fu-suba with sea lettuce (āsa), black soba, and more. Prices are reasonable at ¥750 to ¥950, and the fact that you can also take out jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice) is a nice point! This time I decided to order the No. 1 favorite "Mix Soba" (¥900) recommended by the staff member. Being able to enjoy both braised pork belly and soft-bone pork ribs is a real luxury, isn't it? 🤤

The shop isn't very large, but the homey, warm atmosphere is really nice 😊 Wooden tables and chairs are arranged, giving a nostalgic feeling like an old Okinawan diner. Various decorations and masks are displayed on the walls, so it's fun just to look around. The paper lanterns hanging from the ceiling add a nice touch too, and there was an atmosphere that reminded me of a festival stall. An electric fan spins round and round, a scene that's so very Okinawan, isn't it?
Mix Soba  ¥900

After ordering and waiting a while, the "Mix Soba" finally appeared! 😆 First, the visual impact is amazing. Chunks of braised pork belly and soft-bone pork ribs are piled in, and the fish cake and green onions are generously topped as well. The pink fish cake adds color, and it looks delicious just to look at ✨ The soup has a gentle, translucent color, and the lovely aroma of the blended broth rises up. My expectations are rising!
Let's start with a sip of the soup 😋 Yes yes, this is a blended broth with a solid pork-bone flavor! It's ordinarily tasty. It gently soaked into my body, tired from the end of the year 😌
Mix Soba  ¥900

Next, I try the noodles. These are medium-thick straight noodles, boiled to a soft texture 👍 People who like firmer noodles might find them a little lacking. The flavor of the noodles themselves is simple and doesn't get in the way of the soup's taste.

And now, the long-awaited toppings! First, the braised pork belly. Wow, this has been simmered until it's meltingly tender 😍 The seasoning is fairly sweet, with a gentle soy-sauce-based flavor. The soft-bone pork ribs are meltingly tender in the same way. These are also sweetly seasoned, finished with a gentle, Okinawan-style flavor.

Overall, my impression is of an ordinarily delicious Okinawa soba 😊 It doesn't have any particularly memorable features, but its steady deliciousness makes it easy to see why it continues to be loved by locals. As New Year's Eve soba, this gentle flavor may have been just right. It was a soba that gave me a warm, cozy feeling, as if healing a year's worth of fatigue ✨ My impression was that it was just ordinarily good.

Still, the distinctiveness of the entrance was memorable 😅 I'm sure first-time visitors will definitely get lost. But maybe that's part of Batten Soba's charm too. It feels like a hidden-gem shop that only locals know, which somehow makes you feel special. If you drive out toward Nanjo City, please stop by once. You can enjoy the ocean view too, and I think you can spend a relaxing time 🌊

Rating (9/15): Batten Soba was a shop that serves homey Okinawa soba that isn't flashy but that you can eat with peace of mind. The soup, noodles, and toppings were all of an ordinarily delicious quality, and it's understandable why it continues to be loved by locals 😊 The entrance is hard to find, but I think it's a shop you can enjoy including that. When you want to eat Okinawa soba in Sashiki Shinkai, Nanjo City, please remember Batten Soba!

高江洲そば.name: Takaesu Soba
高江洲そば.desc: An extremely popular shop that's sure to have a line, and the home of the "original yushi-dofu soba." A light, salty soup of pork bone, bonito, and kelp loaded with yushi-dofu (soft Okinawan tofu). You write your name on the whiteboard at the entrance and wait.
t: I ate here in September 2023, at this shop near the Pipeline Road 😁
The other day, on my way home from eating at "Suke Soba" along the same Pipeline Road (in Ginowan City), I found Takaesu Soba, so I decided "I'll go here next," and here I am lol
Takaesu Soba
Go a little way in from Pipeline Road and there's the shop, with a parking lot, but although it was lunchtime, it was amazingly full and I couldn't park (;^ω^)
And there are lots of customers lined up near the entrance!! I could tell it's a popular shop.
"This might be high-level Okinawa soba!" My expectations went up 🤗
I waited in the parking lot with my hazard lights on for a parking space to open up. After a while, customers who had finished eating left, and I finally got parked 😊
But now, waiting in line (;^ω^)
There was a bench outside with a few seats, and elderly people were sitting there, and I couldn't tell whether they were people resting outside after eating or people waiting their turn, so I asked.
It turned out there was a whiteboard at the entrance where you write your name. So I went to the entrance and wrote my name.
The whiteboard at the entrance. You write your name here and then wait to be called 😊
After waiting in line for quite a while, my turn finally came to go inside. You buy a ticket at the ticket machine set up near the entrance.
I came here without any research again, but the entrance said "original yushi-dofu soba," so I decided to order the yushi-dofu soba.
I decided on my order after seeing the "original yushi-dofu soba" at the entrance 😁
Yushi-dofu soba, large  ¥800
The toppings are green onions, egg, shredded pork spare ribs (soki), kūbu (knotted kelp), and yushi-dofu
The kelp reminded me of "Miyazato Soba" in Nago City lol
I ordered the "large," but the bowl seemed on the small side (medium size?)
On the ticket machine, the yushi-dofu soba came in "extra large," "large," and "medium," so even though it says "large," it might be the "medium" size at other shops.

First I tasted the soup 😊 It was like "Hm? What's the base?" and I couldn't really tell the flavor (;^ω^) Sorry for my dull palate (;^ω^) I thought it was very gentle and light. When I googled it, it's said to be a "light, salty soup using pork bone, bonito, and kelp," but since it also contains yushi-dofu, I could taste the flavor of the yushi-dofu liquid too.
The noodles are medium-thick, wavy, and on the soft side. Like the light soup, the other toppings were also lightly seasoned.

Rating (9/15): It's ordinarily tasty, but seeing the line of customers raised my expectations and I set the bar too high ^^; It seems to be a hugely popular shop, so why not try the original yushi-dofu soba?

鶏そば屋いしぐふー.name: Tori Soba-ya Ishigufu
鶏そば屋いしぐふー.desc: Provisional #4 (13.5/15). A popular shop in a renovated foreign-style house in Minatogawa. A clear salty soup of Yanbaru herb young chicken with in-house flat noodles, and two kinds of chicken chashu (salt chicken and seared chicken). A new style of Okinawa soba that's like salt ramen.
t: I ate here in December 2024 😄 This time I'm introducing "Tori Soba-ya Ishigufu," tucked into a corner of a residential area in Minatogawa, Urasoe City. It's a shop renovated from a building that was originally a foreign-style house, with an atmosphere that mixes nostalgia and stylishness. Even though it was a weekday, it was full of tourists and locals, and the wait was about the longest I've had, which shows how popular it is.
Tori Soba-ya Ishigufu (a shop renovated from a foreign-style house)
Tori Soba-ya Ishigufu. It's in a corner of Kansas Street
The menu is packed in all over the shop. From the standard chicken soba to creative, unusual variations, there's plenty to choose from 👇 (I'm introducing just part of the menu)

The No. 1 favorite, the "Special Chicken Soba." Two kinds of chicken, seared chicken and salt chicken, with in-house flat noodles and a broth made with Yanbaru herb young chicken, all with careful attention to detail
Chicken soba lineup (Special Chicken Soba, Chicken Salt Soba, Chicken Seared Soba, Green Onion-only Soba)
Vegetable soba  ¥1,000
Magic Special Black Mayu Oil Soba
Passionate Special Red Spicy Soba
Drink menu (including handmade ginger ale and floats too)
A view of the counter table

Now, what I ordered this time was the shop's top pick, the "Special Chicken Soba (medium)"! 🥢 In the bowl that was brought to me, in a clear chicken soup, shining in-house noodles, two kinds of chicken chashu (salt chicken and seared chicken), and vivid green onions were topped. Just from the look of it, it already feels like a winner ✨
Special Chicken Soba (medium)  ¥1,100

First, a sip of the soup... Mmm, it's delicious! 😋 This tastes more like a high-quality salt ramen than Okinawa soba. The broth made from Yanbaru herb young chicken has a perfectly balanced saltiness, and while it's refreshing, the umami of the chicken comes rushing in. I can't stop with my soup spoon with this soup 😆
Special Chicken Soba (medium)  ¥1,100

Next, the noodles. The in-house flat, wavy noodles are chewy and supple and pair superbly with the soup. Among the Ishigufu group, some shops finish the noodles a bit firm, but the noodles at the Minatogawa shop were just the right doneness. They have springiness while also being gentle on the palate, the type I'd recommend to anyone.

The salt chicken chashu topping is gently seasoned with a salty touch, moist and tender. A faint herb aroma gives it an elegant impression. The other one, the seared chicken, is fragrantly soaked in a sweet-and-salty soy sauce glaze, with a slightly punchy taste. Both had different personalities and were enjoyable, but personally I preferred the salt chicken 😊
Autographs of famous people displayed in the shop (could this be Robert's Baba-san, the gourmet who runs restaurants on Miyakojima?)
Autographs of famous people displayed in the shop
Autographs of famous people displayed in the shop (personal chopsticks are displayed too)

The interior has rows of autograph cards lined up, and you can tell many famous people visit. Anime and game pixel-art-style characters are also displayed on the walls, giving the shop a bit of a playful feel. The service was polite, and the atmosphere of the staff was warm.

However... the only drawback is "it gets so crowded!" The board inside the shop said "40+ minute wait," but I waited even longer 💦 Also, parking is limited, so if possible I recommend visiting on a weekday morning or at a time outside the peak.

Rating (13.5/15): Overall, I felt the Minatogawa shop is especially well-polished even among the Ishigufu shops. The balance of broth, noodles, and toppings was wonderful, and it was a bowl that proposes a new style of Okinawa soba. It's a shop I'd like to keep coming back to, and it's officially registered as a "Recommended Shop" ✨

そば処 琉風.name: Soba-dokoro Ryufu
そば処 琉風.desc: The airport shop on the first floor of the Naha Airport Domestic Terminal. A shop also featured in Horiemon's gourmet app, famous for its "Mozuku Soba" generously topped with locally grown mozuku seaweed. Pork-bone broth soup with medium-thick straight noodles. You can enjoy it quickly after arriving or before boarding.
t: On this Okinawa soba journey, I'm introducing "Soba-dokoro Ryufu" inside the Naha Airport Domestic Terminal 🍜
I ate here in May 2025 😆
Soba-dokoro Ryufu (look for the conspicuous sign inside the terminal)
I had been curious about this shop for a long time after seeing it introduced in Horiemon's gourmet app 😄 It seems to be such a staple that it's the place to go for a meal at the airport.
The shop is at the end of the passage lined with luggage carts, inside the domestic terminal

Looking at the menu, the basic lineup is four items: soft-bone pork rib soba (nankotsu soki soba), mix soba, mozuku soba, and Okinawa soba. Some can be made into a jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice) set, and the mozuku soba and mix soba sets apparently even come with sea grapes 😋 There's even a bowl typical of an airport shop, the "Mozuku Soba," generously topped with locally grown mozuku. It had been a while since I'd had mozuku, so this time I tried ordering this one.
Menu (soft-bone pork rib soba, mix soba, mozuku soba, Okinawa soba)

I bought a meal ticket at the ticket machine and went to my seat. Inside, table seats are spaciously arranged, and it feels like a place where you can sit down and eat quickly before boarding or after arrival.
Buying a meal ticket at the ticket machine (Mozuku Soba ¥1,150)
Table seats inside the shop

After a while, the "Mozuku Soba" appeared! Piled high with black mozuku, plus braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), white fish cake, pickled red ginger, and green onions, it's appetizing just to look at 😆
Mozuku Soba  ¥1,150
First, the soup. It's a pork-bone broth soup with no off-putting quirks, an easy-to-eat flavor.
Next, the noodles. They're medium-thick straight noodles, finished on the soft side.
Medium-thick straight noodles
When I scooped up and ate the mozuku, I didn't feel much of a sea flavor. If the mozuku aroma were a bit more pronounced, it might have had more character.
The braised pork belly topping had a really strong sinewy texture ^^;

Rating (9/15): It was a shop I had been checking out for a long time since it was introduced in Horiemon's gourmet app, but when I actually ate there, it was an ordinary bowl. That said, being able to eat Okinawa soba right at the airport is welcome. I recommend it for those who want to quickly enjoy Okinawa soba after arrival or before boarding 👋

美里そば.name: Misato Soba
美里そば.desc: A locally beloved shop in Higashi, Okinawa City. Its signature "Misato Soba" is a pork-bone-based soup with soft, medium-thin wavy noodles, topped with all of yushi-dofu, braised pork belly, soft-bone pork ribs, and fish cake. Fūchībā (mugwort) is a nice accent. A popular shop with a constant stream of local customers.
t: On this Okinawa soba journey, I went to "Misato Soba" in Higashi, Okinawa City 🍜 I ate here in May 2025 😆
Misato Soba (it's behind the Ryugin Juji-ro branch)
It's a shop in a corner of a residential area behind the "Ryugin Juji-ro" branch in Higashi, Okinawa City 😊
The shop was bustling with local customers
I ordered the "Misato Soba," the same as the shop's name. A pork-bone-based soup, with medium-thin, loosely wavy noodles finished on the soft side.
Misato Soba  ¥950
The toppings are all of yushi-dofu, braised pork belly, soft-bone pork ribs, and fish cake. The braised pork belly and soft-bone pork ribs were well flavor-soaked, but they also had a sinewy texture.
Misato Soba  ¥950 (the most popular signature menu item)
Explanation board (describes their commitment to the soup and noodles)
Looking at the explanation board, it says they simmer pork soup bones slowly and carefully, frequently removing scum and fat. The soft bones are apparently simmered until meltingly tender 😋
Fūchībā (mugwort) is a nice accent, tightening up the overall flavor.
The explanation board also said, "The fact that fūchībā comes with the bowl shows care for health" 😊
Local customers were visiting the shop without a break, and I felt this is a shop loved by the community.

Rating (9/15): The flavor is just ordinarily tasty, but with all of yushi-dofu, braised pork belly, soft-bone pork ribs, and fish cake on top and the fūchībā accent working well, it was a bowl rooted in the local community 😄

根夢（沖縄市）.name: Gon (Okinawa City)
根夢（沖縄市）.desc: Gon (根夢) in Ageda, Okinawa City. A community-rooted shop with two signs: Okinawa soba by day and an izakaya by night. A light soup with bonito broth and soft, medium-thick straight noodles, and the "Mix Soba" with all of bone-in pork ribs, soft-bone pork ribs, and braised pork belly is plenty satisfying.
t: On this Okinawa soba journey, I went to "Gon" in Ageda, Okinawa City 🍜
Exterior. The "Gon (根夢)" sign is the landmark

This is a shop with two signs: Okinawa soba by day and an izakaya by night. Perhaps because of that, the interior has the feeling of eating soba in a corner of an izakaya rather than at a so-called Okinawa soba specialty shop 😄
Inside. A typical izakaya atmosphere with bottles lined up
When I visited, it was quite bustling with local customers. It feels like a shop rooted in the community rather than aimed at tourists, and getting into a shop like this makes me a little happy 😊
Handwritten menus covering the whole wall
Menu notices posted all over the wall too

Looking at the menu, this time I ordered the loaded "Mix Soba." It's a greedy bowl with all of bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki), soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) on top 🤤
Menu
There was also an English menu (GON MENU)
Here's the Mix Soba that appeared. With three kinds of meat piled on, it has quite an impact ✨
Mix Soba, large  ¥1,080
First, the soup. It has a flavor with the bonito broth coming through firmly.
The noodles are the medium-thick, loosely straight type. Finished on the soft side 🍜
Mix Soba, large  ¥1,080

And the star, the all-in toppings. The bone-in pork ribs, soft-bone pork ribs, and braised pork belly each have a moderate flavor and are delicious, but all of them had a fair amount of sinewy texture ^^;
The soft-bone pork ribs are not the type simmered until tender but have a firm, crunchy texture, which is satisfying in its own way, though it might divide opinions 😋

Overall, it was an ordinarily delicious, relaxed bowl, just like the Okinawa soba an izakaya would serve. It's understandable why it's bustling with locals 😄 At night, you could probably enjoy it as an izakaya, having a drink and finishing with soba 🍶

Rating (9/15): A light soup with bonito broth and soft, medium-thick straight noodles. With all of bone-in pork ribs, soft-bone pork ribs, and braised pork belly on top, it's plenty satisfying. It was an unpretentious bowl born from an izakaya and loved by the community 😊

アグーそば処 ひかり食堂 与儀店.name: Agu Soba-dokoro Hikari Shokudo Yogi Branch
アグーそば処 ひかり食堂 与儀店.desc: The Yogi branch (opened in 2024) of Agu Soba-dokoro Hikari Shokudo, along Route 329 in Yogi, Okinawa City. You can choose the soup from light / rich / blended, and the noodles from straight / wavy. The limited-quantity rich "Hikari Soba" is a pork-forward bowl with strong agu broth.
t: This time I visited "Agu Soba-dokoro Hikari Shokudo Yogi Branch" in Yogi, Okinawa City 🍜 I ate here in June 2025 😄
Hikari Shokudo (it's along Route 329)

Actually, this is my first time at Hikari Shokudo since visiting the Meido branch in Okinawa City. The agu broth from that visit left an impression, and the Yogi branch is a relatively new shop that opened in 2024 ✨
Hikari Shokudo (it's along Route 329)

Partly because I visited at lunchtime, the shop was quite bustling with local customers. It felt like a community-rooted eatery where neighbors drop in for lunch rather than tourists, and a shop with this kind of atmosphere is reassuring 😊
The menu posted on the wall inside the shop

Now, I decided to order the "Hikari Soba," which is also the shop's signature menu item. The interesting thing about Hikari Shokudo is that you can choose the soup and noodles yourself. You can choose the soup from three types, "light," "rich," and "blended," and the noodles from "straight" and "wavy."
You can choose the soup and noodles
The menu is lined with dishes using Ryukyu black pork agu, and it's fun just to look at 🤤
The menu posted on the wall inside the shop
Autographs of famous people posted on the wall inside the shop

Since I was there, this time I had them combine the "rich" soup, which is said to be limited in quantity, with "straight" noodles. When something is described as limited quantity, you can't help wanting to order it (lol)
Ticket machine / meal ticket
And here's the bowl that arrived. A bowl with agu pork broth that looks absolutely delicious ✨
Hikari Soba ¥950 (rich soup, straight noodles)
First, the soup. As you'd expect from choosing rich, the agu broth is fairly strong and the pork flavor comes through strongly. It had a taste that pushed the pork feel way up front 🐷
The noodles are medium-thick straight noodles. Boiled on the soft side, they had a gentle mouthfeel and slid down easily 🍜 They went well enough with the rich soup too.
Hikari Soba ¥950 (rich soup, straight noodles)

The toppings are braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), and pork shoulder loin, and it's nice that there are three kinds of meat on top. However, the seasoning of the meat itself was light. Honestly, I felt a fair amount of sinewy texture in each, and there were a few so-so parts ^^; It's satisfying to eat, so I thought I'd have liked it better if it were a bit more fall-apart tender.
Condiments and seasonings on the table

Rating (9/15): My honest impression overall is... hmm, the flavor was just average, to be frank 😅 The fun of choosing the soup and noodles is there, and the rich agu broth did come through to a fair degree, but my impression is that it didn't reach the point of an outstanding "wow!" this time. Even so, it's understandable that it's this bustling with locals, and with light or blended soup or wavy noodles the impression might change, so I'd like to try those next time 😄

沖縄そば まんま家.name: Okinawa Soba Manmaya
沖縄そば まんま家.desc: A popular shop near Naha City Hospital in Furujima, Naha. You can choose the soup from three types: rich pork bone / light / light bonito, and the noodles from wavy / straight. The signature "Manmaya Soba" is hearty with pig's feet, braised pork belly, and soft-bone pork ribs, and comes with jushi and two side dishes. A shop bustling with local customers.
t: On this Okinawa soba journey, I visited "Okinawa Soba Manmaya" in Furujima, Naha City 🍜 I ate here in June 2025 😄
Exterior: the red sign of "Okinawa Soba Manmaya"

It's a shop in the Furujima neighborhood with a red sign that catches the eye. The storefront is what you'd call a neighborhood Okinawa soba shop, and its unpretentious atmosphere actually raises my expectations 😄 Partly because I visited at lunchtime, the shop was quite bustling with local customers. Being loved by this many locals seems like proof of deliciousness in itself 😊

Now, for my order I naturally chose the signature menu item named after the shop, "Manmaya Soba." The interesting thing about this shop is that you can choose the soup and the noodles separately. You can choose the soup from three types, "rich pork-bone broth," "light broth," and "light bonito broth," and the noodles from "wavy noodles" and "straight noodles."
Okinawa soba menu with an explanation that you can choose the soup and noodles

I hesitated, but this time I had them combine "light bonito broth" for the soup with the "wavy noodles" that the staff told me "are popular." Being able to ask for recommendations like this is a pleasure unique to a local shop 😋
Incidentally, the menu also had taco rice, a lineup unexpected (lol) for an Okinawa soba shop.
Taco rice menu
And here's the bowl that arrived. A quite hearty bowl with pig's feet (tebichi), braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), and soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) piled on ✨
Manmaya Soba, large  ¥1,050

First, the soup. It's named "light," but when I drank it the bonito broth came through firmly, and it was a bowl with umami rather than just lightness. It's fairly tasty 😋 The rich pork bone is tempting too, but the balance of this bonito broth was pretty good as well.

I chose the wavy noodles. Surprisingly, and I say this with apologies, for a shop with such an unpretentious storefront they're authentic, and the chewy texture is fun 🍜 They clung well to the soup and were fairly tasty.
Manmaya Soba, large  ¥1,050

The toppings are pig's feet, braised pork belly, and soft-bone pork ribs, with volume to spare. However, the soft-bone pork ribs were finished with a firm, crunchy texture, which was a little disappointing for me, someone who likes meltingly tender ^^; Both the soft-bone pork ribs and braised pork belly had a fair amount of sinewy texture. This might be where opinions divide.
And what's nice is that when you order soba, jushi and two small side dishes (mozuku and macaroni salad) come with it.
Jushi and two side dishes: mozuku / macaroni salad

This time I ordered the "large," so the soba alone is plenty hearty, and with the jushi and side dishes added I'm completely full 😆 With this much volume, it's understandable that local customers never stop coming. The only disappointment was perhaps that there's no parking lot. I parked on the road along a nearby park, but if you're going by car you'll probably need to look for a nearby coin parking lot 🚗

Rating (10/15): The light bonito broth is a soup with firm broth and umami, and the wavy noodles are more authentic and chewy than they look. With pig's feet, braised pork belly, and soft-bone pork ribs it's full of volume, and the satisfaction of having jushi and side dishes is plentiful. The crunchy texture of the soft-bone pork ribs and the lack of parking may divide opinions, but it was a bowl for which it's understandable why it's bustling with locals 😊

みーや小.name: Mīya-gwā
みーや小.desc: A popular local shop recognizable by its roadside sign. You can choose white or green (herbal) noodles, with a bonito-based broth and free fuchiba service. You can enjoy it with a healthy feeling.
t: I ate here in January 2023 😊
Mīya-gwā
This sign is the landmark, lol
I ordered the “sanmai-niku soba (braised pork belly soba).” You can choose white or green noodles, and I chose the herbal noodles.
Braised pork belly soba (sanmai-niku soba)　¥800

The broth is bonito-based and delicious 😋 The noodles are green. I couldn't feel any herbal flavor or taste, but fuchiba (mugwort) came as a free service, so along with it I could eat with a good bitterness and a healthy feeling. Delicious. The braised pork belly was tender too 😋
Rating (9/15): It's just plain tasty 😊 It was bustling with local customers. I thought it's a shop loved by the locals.

むかしむかし.name: Mukashi Mukashi
むかしむかし.desc: A shop run by an owner who is a potter. The tables and tableware are all handmade, and its specialties are the house-made mokkai soba (made with wood-ash lye) using wood from the hill behind, and hiija (goat) soba with goats raised on that hill. No gamey smell and easy to eat.
t: Relying on the “Nago City Soba Map,” I ate at “Mukashi Mukashi” (October 2020).
“Mukashi Mukashi” along Prefectural Route 84
On the “Nago Soba Map,” “Mukashi Mukashi” was introduced as shop 26 of 41.
The soba map explains “The house-made mokkai soba (made with wood-ash lye) by the potter owner can't be tasted anywhere else!” and has a photo of the “hiija (goat) soba” ^^;

Although I am an Uchinanchu (Okinawan), I have avoided goat since the last time I had hiija soup in junior high school, out of a picky refusal to even try it, but this time I thought it would be a good experience and took on the challenge 💪
Menu (there is no photo, but they say the tables, chairs, and even the tableware inside the shop are all handmade by the owner himself)
Hiija (goat) soba, small　¥1,050

The toppings as they look are indeed beastly, lol But when I ate it, there was absolutely no gamey smell, the meat was tender, and it was just plain tasty ☺ The topping of fuchiba (mugwort) also plays a role in masking odors.

The noodles were mokkai soba made from wood from the hill behind, and the flavor was different from noodles at other shops. The goats are also raised on the hill behind, and you can hear them bleating, which gives a nice peaceful countryside atmosphere.
Rating (9.5/15): Its looks are a shock, lol, but it's just plain tasty ☺ If you're tired of ordinary Okinawa soba, why not give it a try?
PS: While eating I could enjoy it with no gamey smell, but for a while after finishing, my own breath seemed to smell beastly lol Be careful, haha
Also, home-grown shikuwasa and limes were being sold at the counter, so I bought some as souvenirs to put in awamori back home (200 yen total), lol

伊芸サービスエリア（下り）レストラン.name: Igei Service Area (Northbound) Restaurant
伊芸サービスエリア（下り）レストラン.desc: A restaurant in the Igei Service Area (northbound) on the Okinawa Expressway. With its red tile roof and shisa, it has an Okinawan exterior, and serves a classic old-fashioned Okinawa soba topped with green onions, shredded egg, fish cake, and braised pork belly. A reassuring bowl for a break in your travels.
t: I ate here in March 2025 😊
This time, while driving on the Okinawa Expressway, I stopped at the Igei Service Area (northbound) and had “Okinawa soba” 🍜
Igei Service Area (Northbound) Restaurant

When going around eating Okinawa soba, your eyes tend to go to famous shops aimed at tourists or traditional neighborhood diners, but Okinawa soba at service areas like this also catches my interest, since you get to see the “everyday bowl” of Okinawa. The exterior's red tiles catch the eye, giving the feel of “oh, this is Okinawan” at first glance 😆 The shisa on the roof add good flavor too, and it was just the right atmosphere for taking a little break during a trip.
Ticket machine near the entrance

Inside is a spacious area typical of a service area, with a simple diner-like quality, and the lack of pretension was oddly calming. In front of the ticket machine I hesitated a little over what to eat, but this time I chose the basic “Okinawa soba” after all.
Inside the shop
Inside the shop
Okinawa soba　¥850

The moment I saw the actual bowl, I thought it was truly a traditional, standard style. In a dark-colored bowl sat green onions, shredded egg, fish cake (kamaboko), and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) — a classic style without gimmicks just by looking at it. With this kind of bowl you can somehow imagine the direction of the flavor before eating, but that “reassurance of it being just as you imagined” is also the good thing about Okinawa soba 😊 First, I took a sip of the broth and it was the type with a pork-bone-based richness. However, rather than being too thick or punchy, my impression was that it was clearly put together as a bowl to eat at a service area. It's not bad, but it didn't make me excited with an “Oh, this is delicious!” — it was a pretty ordinary broth.
Okinawa soba　¥850

The noodles were medium-thick, loose straight noodles with a definite Okinawa soba feel. Lifted up, they also looked just like diner Okinawa soba. But when I ate them they were a bit on the soft side. Personally I would have liked a bit more springiness and bite.

Among the toppings, what left the strongest impression was the braised pork belly, as expected. It was clearly well seasoned just from looking at it. However, there was also a little sinewy texture, and if you expect a softness that gently unravels in your mouth, it's a bit different. It's properly simmered, but not the melt-in-your-mouth type. So for people seeking strong satisfaction from the braised pork belly, it might need one more step. The fish cake, green onions, and shredded egg were the reliable supporting players, tidying up the overall look while properly supporting the old-fashioned Okinawa soba feel.

What I thought while eating this time was that this bowl works as a “reassuring Okinawa soba to eat along the way on a trip,” but if you ask whether I'd stop in just for this, it doesn't quite get there. Comparing within the Okinawa Expressway, I thought the Okinawa soba I ate earlier at “Ajisen Ramen” in the Nakagusuku Service Area was more delicious. The Okinawa soba at this Igei Service Area (northbound) was “ordinary,” in both the good and bad senses. Since I always look for each shop's individuality and a memorable point, in that sense I felt a bit of dissatisfaction.

Still, being able to casually eat this classic-style Okinawa soba at a service area diner is very Okinawan and nice. During sightseeing, between travel legs, when you're a little hungry and don't want to take any adventure but want Okinawa soba, I think it's perfectly fine. It's not flashy, but it felt like they serve a traditional standard Okinawa soba just as it is.
Rating (9/15): My honest take is “ordinary, not exceeding expectations; not so good that I actively want to repeat it” 🙂 But why not try it once when sightseeing in the north? 😆

伊覇そば.name: Iha Soba
伊覇そば.desc: A chicken-broth shop along Route 507. The “Iha Soba,” topped with chicken instead of pig's feet, has a chicken-bone-based flavor not found at other shops. A fresh combination of chicken × Okinawa soba.
t: In January 2023, on the way back from surfing (Itoman City, Suicide Cliff Point), I stopped in since I'd been curious about it for a while ☺
Along Route 507　“Iha Soba”

I went in with no prior information, so for now I ordered the “Iha Soba,” which shares the shop's name. Since the menu said “everything on top,” I thought it would be the usual “braised pork belly (sanmai-niku; the belly part of the pig's torso), pork spare ribs (soki; bone-in pork ribs), and pig's feet (tebichi),” but...
Menu (Iha Soba ¥870)
Iha Soba ¥870　There are soki and braised pork belly, but chicken instead of pig's feet. I hadn't looked at the menu in detail, so I only noticed the difference when it came out ^^;
While thinking “Oh, the toppings are somehow different,” I first took a sip of the broth. “Huh, the broth's taste is different too,” I thought, and took another sip. Yep, different.

Normally, Okinawa soba broth is a blend of pork bone stock, bonito stock, dried small sardines, kelp, and so on, with pork bone emphasized or, for bonito-based ones, bonito emphasized, but this was a taste I'd never experienced at other shops.
So I googled it, and it turns out Iha Soba is “chicken-bone-based.”
I see, so that's why they use chicken in the toppings too ☺
I thought chicken and chicken-stock broth go well with Okinawa soba. It was delicious.
Rating (9.5/15): It's just plain tasty. The chicken and chicken-stock broth are delicious. If you're tired of ordinary soba, why not give it a try? It feels fresh.

伊豆味そば.name: Izumi Soba
伊豆味そば.desc: A queue-guaranteed old-house soba shop standing alone in the mountains of Izumi on the soba road. The No. 1 popular “Izumi Soba” comes with bone-in pork ribs, braised pork belly, and 2 small side dishes. They also have the limited-quantity “Tojin Soba,” a recreation of soba from about 120 years ago.
t: * This article was created by AI (Claude Opus 4.5) with some additions and updates by me 😆
I went to eat here in February 2025 😁😊
For this Okinawa soba outing, I went to “Izumi Soba” in Izumi, Motobu Town 😄
Izumi Soba
Sign-in sheet
Izumi Soba
Signboard along the way to the shop

This shop is near “Mori no Ie,” where I ate the other day, and is also in the mountains 🌿 Following the navigation down a narrow road, an old house suddenly appears alone, surrounded by trees. A big sign with the words “house-made noodles” stands out, greeting you with a red tile roof and a shisa perched on it ✨

When I arrived, there was a “Full” sign at the entrance...! As expected, it's a popular shop. A waiting tent was set up outside, and the system was to wait your turn there. On the sign-in stand were paper and a pen, and you write your name and wait to be called 📝
I waited quite a while that day~ When there's a line, expectations rise too 😆
Menu set up outdoors
Menu set up outdoors
Ticket machine

After waiting a while I finally got inside. There's a ticket machine right at the entrance, so it's a style where you buy a ticket here. You take off your shoes and step up, and the wooden warmth inside is new and clean 🏠 It has the feel of a renovated old house, with exposed ceiling beams giving an open feeling. There was also a sign on the wall reading “Sold out for today,” so it seems it sometimes sells out early.
Inside the shop
Inside the shop
When I sat down, the view out the window was a green landscape with luxuriant hego tree ferns, truly giving the feeling of “eating in the Yanbaru forest” 🌴 The atmosphere is outstanding.
Outside is forest (^0^;)
Menu (again)

Looking at the menu, the “Izumi Soba,” which shares the shop's name, was written as the shop's popular No. 1. It has two kinds of meat, bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki) and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), plus 2 small side dishes, so it's a good-value menu. They also had “soki soba,” “braised pork belly soba,” and a rare limited-quantity item called “Tojin Soba.” Tojin Soba recreates the origin of Okinawa soba from about 120 years ago, and is apparently a black soy-sauce-based broth 🍜
Naturally this time I decided to order the “Izumi Soba” (¥950), which shares the shop's name.
After waiting a few minutes, the Izumi Soba was brought out on a tray! Beside the soba come pickled bitter melon (goya) and 2 small bowls of tofu. It's full of Okinawan flavor just by looking at it 😊
Izumi soba　¥950
First, as always, I start with the broth. When I took a sip, it was a gentle seasoning with the bonito stock coming through firmly.
Izumi soba　¥950

Next, the noodles. I had been expecting them since they're house-made, and they're medium-thick wavy noodles with a chewy quality 🍜 When you bite, there's a firm springiness, and they cling nicely to the broth. These noodles are quite delicious.

I tried the toppings of bone-in pork ribs and braised pork belly. The seasoning is moderate and not bad, but there's quite a lot of sinewy texture. My impression was that I'd have been happier if they had been simmered a bit more tenderly. The fish cake and green onions were also properly included.
The small side dish of pickled bitter melon has a firm bitterness, and it's surprisingly delicious 😋 It's perfect as a palate cleanser and went well with the soba.

Rating (9.5/15): As an overall impression, because there was a line and I waited quite a while, my expectations had risen, but honestly it felt like it was one step short~ The atmosphere of an old house in the mountains is outstanding. The chewiness of the house-made noodles was good, but the sinewy texture of the toppings bothered me a little. It's a just plain tasty Okinawa soba 😊 Being an old house, the interior is new and clean, the green view from the window is superb, and I'm sure it's a popular shop ✨ I recommend it to those who want to enjoy the atmosphere and savor Okinawa soba slowly.
It might be good to stop by on the way toward Motobu Town, especially to the Churaumi Aquarium or Jungle-ia Okinawa. However, I recommend going at an early time of day, prepared for a line 😄

山田水車屋.name: Yamada Suisha-ya
山田水車屋.desc: An ultra-unique Okinawa soba shop that used to be in Yamada, Onna Village (* closed in December 2021). Famous for its handmade bungee jump and the goats it kept, its bonito-broth Suisha Soba was a reasonable ¥500. I'm keeping this article as a record.
t: I ate here in April 2021 😄
Note: Unfortunately this shop is now closed. I'm writing it down as a record.

Near the entrance of the now-gone “Yamada Suisha-ya.” The exterior was impactful too, so I wish I had taken a photo showing the whole exterior ^^; It closed, maybe due to the effects of COVID, which is a pity.
There was a bungee jump too. They also kept goats. Unique, lol
The stairs leading to the bungee jump 😁 Full of a handmade feel, lol
Suisha soba　¥500
I ordered the “Suisha Soba” recommended by the owner. A bonito-broth-forward soup with thin wavy noodles. It was just plain tasty, and the price was reasonable too.

Rating (9/15): It was just plain tasty, but it's a pity it has closed. What stuck with me is that when I ate there, the owner was happily chatting with other tourists. I also vaguely remember there was something handmade inside like a “COVID sterilization device?”, but it was a very unique shop 😁

島そば.name: Shima Soba
島そば.desc: A long-established shop along Prefectural Route 255 in Enohi, Uruma City. A popular local shop with a hand-lettered-looking sign full of character, whose charm is the double-stock broth that is bonito-based but with a strong pork-bone presence, and melt-in-your-mouth braised pork belly. Shima soba, large, is a reasonable ¥650. Next door is Tsuki Kuroki.
t: I went to eat here in February 2023 😊
Shima Soba (the sign seems hand-lettered? and has great character, lol)
Menu
I ordered the “shima soba,” which shares the shop's name
Shima soba, large　¥650

The braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) is melt-in-your-mouth and delicious. The noodles are medium-thick, and the broth is bonito-based but I also feel a strong pork-bone flavor 😊 They seem to have raised prices recently due to rising raw material costs, but even so I think ¥650 for large is cheap 😁
Rating (9/15): It's just plain tasty. Why not stop by when you come near Enohi in Uruma City? There seems to be another Okinawa soba shop right next door, so I'd like to take that on next time.

島そば一番地.name: Shima Soba Ichibanchi
島そば一番地.desc: The Naha branch of a Yaeyama soba specialty shop whose main store is on Ishigaki Island. Shima soba with thinly sliced fish cake and braised pork belly, round thin noodles, and a faintly pork-bone broth, served with a mini miso rice ball. Changing the flavor with pipaz spice is the Yaeyama way too.
t: I ate here in February 2024 😄
It's on the 2nd floor of Nōren Plaza
Shima Soba Ichibanchi
Shima Soba Ichibanchi
This soba shop is a Yaeyama soba specialty shop, and it seems to run two shops: the main store on Ishigaki Island, and this Naha branch (Hikawa, Naha City) on the Okinawa main island.
Menu
Menu
Menu
Menu
A comment from an island-song singer written on the menu. I wonder if he's famous (^0^;)
From the menu I decided to order the “shima soba,” which shares the shop's name.
Explanation of the effects of pipaz spice
Perhaps as a feature of Yaeyama soba, there's a spice called “pipaz,” and it seems to have various effects 😄 I'd like to try it partway through to change the flavor 😆
Shima soba, medium　¥700 (in the back there is also pipaz spice)
The shima soba has arrived 😄 Not only pickles but also a mini rice ball (miso) comes with it, which is a good deal 😆
I previously had Yaeyama soba for the first time at “Miyara Soba (Urasoe branch)” in Urasoe City, and the feature is that the fish cake and braised pork belly are thinly sliced.
First, a sip of the broth. A broth with a faint pork-bone base, just plain tasty.
Shima soba, medium　¥700
Next, the noodles. They are thin straight noodles, on the soft side. The braised pork belly and fish cake are just plain tasty too.
Partway through I added “pipaz” to change the flavor 😆 But it tasted like ordinary pepper? and wasn't the spice I'd imagined (^0^;)

Rating (9/15): It's just plain tasty. If you want to try Yaeyama soba, why not give this shop a try once? I used a paid coin parking lot nearby without knowing, but apparently the Nōren Plaza parking lot is free for one hour 😄

島人そば.name: Shimanchu Soba
島人そば.desc: A sister shop of the tacos-famous “Gate One.” Its signature is the Shimanchu Soba, with a broth of Agu pork stock scented with bonito, and it was also selected as one of the “Tabearuki Kyushu-Okinawa 100 Taste Shops.” Its longer hours, until 20:30, are convenient too.
t: * This article was created with “Chat gpt4o” and partly supplemented by me, lol
I went to eat here in August 2024 😆
Shimanchu Soba
Shimanchu Soba
The menu says it is a sister shop of Gate One, a taco and taco rice shop.
Even the tissue packs advertise Gate One 😆

Incidentally, I'm told this is a sister shop of the shop called “Gate One,” famous for taco rice and tacos. As usual I went in with no research, so I learned this for the first time (^0^;) The tacos looked famous and delicious too, but this time, since I aim to conquer every Okinawa soba shop, I ordered the “Shimanchu Soba” 😆
Furthermore, the menu says it was selected as one of the “Tabearuki Kyushu-Okinawa 100 Taste Shops.” I don't really know what that is, but maybe I can expect something 😄
Menu (my smartphone was overheating and the photo is out of focus. Sorry 🙏)
Menu
Menu
Inside the shop
Inside the shop (I don't know who, but there are many autographs of celebrities too)

When you enter the shop, a calm, Okinawan atmosphere spreads out first. Autograph boards of celebrities are lined up along the wall, giving the impression of a shop loved by locals and tourists alike. It's also nice that you can get water and tea self-service, so casual. Wrapped in a relaxed atmosphere, I looked at the menu right away, and what caught my eye was, as expected, the “Shimanchu Soba.” A soba with the same name as the shop — I have to order it!
Shimanchu soba　¥800

After ordering and waiting a while, the “Shimanchu Soba” finally arrived. In a big bowl, the generous broth and medium-thick noodles whet the appetite. The broth, said to use “Agu stock,” gives a distinct pork flavor on the first sip, but at the same time the aroma of bonito comes through too.
Shimanchu soba　¥800

The noodles are medium-thin, with a characteristically soft texture. I felt they were slightly lacking in firmness and thought a bit more bite would be good~ But they cling easily to the broth and were perfect for the light, easy-to-drink broth.

The toppings include braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) and soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki). The braised pork belly is lightly seasoned. The soft-bone pork ribs are also lightly seasoned, a bit firm, with some sinewy texture remaining. This may divide opinions, but for those who want to enjoy a solid texture, it might be a plus. I prefer them a bit softer, but those who like this meat's chew might like it.

Rating (9/15): Overall, the “Shimanchu Soba” didn't have strong surprise or individuality, and my impression was of a so-called “just plain tasty” soba. The shop's hours are 11:00 to 20:30, which I think is longer than the hours of other Okinawa soba shops. If you get a chance to come to Yogi in Okinawa City, please do stop by “Shimanchu Soba.” Next time I'd like to try the tacos too 😆

縁そば.name: En Soba
縁そば.desc: Moved from Gakuen-dori in Iso to inside Makeman Urasoe. The signature En Soba has a broth with the umami of pork bone, kelp, and bonito flakes and chewy whole-wheat noodles. A noodle shop with mazesoba, ramen, and even a fried chicken set.
t: ― 2nd Visit (March 2025) ―
I went to “Mendokoro En Soba” inside Makeman in Gusukuma, Urasoe City 😊 I went to eat in March 2025 😄
En Soba is inside Makeman
En Soba

What I had this time was the “En Soba, large,” which has the same name as the shop. I had eaten here before, when it was on Gakuen-dori in Iso, Urasoe City, so this is my first visit since then. This was my first time since it moved here, so I headed over looking forward to how it would be 🚗✨ Since it's inside Makeman, there's almost no worry about parking, which is really helpful. It's easy to stop by while shopping, and the location seems easy for families and locals to use.
