In front of the shop is a big yellow “En Soba” noren, which was quite eye-catching 🌼 As it's a restaurant inside a home improvement store, at first I imagined something closer to a food court, but it was actually a proper standalone shop, with a calm interior. The wood-grain floor and tables give warmth, and the seating seemed relatively roomy. It looks easy to use at lunchtime or after shopping, and I like the atmosphere of casually eating Okinawa soba 🍜
Menu
Menu
Menu
Menu

Looking at the menu, there was quite a variety just in Okinawa soba. En soba, tebichi soba, braised pork belly soba, soft-bone pork ribs soba, meat and bean sprouts soba, small soba, and more were lined up, and there are also seafood mazesoba, Taiwan mazesoba, ramen dishes, and even a fried chicken set 😳 Rather than an Okinawa soba shop, it's more of a noodle place where you can eat a wide range. The fried chicken set also looks good value, and seems good for those who want to eat heartily. This time I ordered the signature-looking “En Soba, large” without hesitation.
En soba, large　¥950

The bowl that arrived after a while looks like a classic Okinawa soba just from appearance ✨ On a brownish broth sit medium-thin noodles, braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), fish cake (kamaboko), shredded egg, and green onions, a look that is not too flashy but well put together. The bowl is also subdued, matching the broth's color, and looked delicious.

Starting with the broth, it seems to be made from pork bone, kelp, and bonito flakes, with firm umami. I can feel the mellowness of the pork bone, but overall the bonito flavor comes slightly to the front 🐟 I thought it's still a delicious broth as ever 😋
En soba, large　¥950

The noodles are medium-thin, slightly wavy noodles kneaded with whole-wheat flour. When lifted with chopsticks they look smooth, and when eaten they're chewy 🍜✨ They're slurpy, easy-to-eat noodles. Since they contain whole wheat, they have a slightly different presence from ordinary noodles 😊

Since the toppings include braised pork belly and soft-bone pork ribs, it looks satisfying as well. The braised pork belly and soft-bone pork ribs are tender too 🥩 My honest impression is that both are tender but the sinewy texture bothered me a little. Because the impressions of the broth and noodles are so good, if the meat toppings had been finished a bit more meltingly, the overall satisfaction would have risen further. The flavor isn't bad, so it was truly just a little short, I felt 🤔

The fish cake, shredded egg, and green onions are included too, giving the proper reassurance of Okinawa soba. Especially the shredded egg gives a touch of brightness to the look 🌿 The aroma of the green onions suits the broth, balancing the whole. Rather than a flashy impact, it's a bowl that lets you take a breather in the middle of shopping. Including its location inside Makeman, I think it's an Okinawa soba shop easy to use in daily life. Even with a family, there are many menu choices, so those who want Okinawa soba, those who want mazesoba, and those who want to add fried chicken could each be satisfied 👍

Rating (10/15): This time's “En Soba, large” was an easy-to-eat bowl with a well-balanced broth and slurpy, chewy noodles 🍜 While both pork bone and bonito umami can be felt, the broth with a slight bonito lean has stability. The noodles with whole wheat have character and went well with the broth. However, it was a pity that the braised pork belly and soft-bone pork ribs toppings had a little sinewy texture. If that were improved, it would become a highly satisfying bowl. Even so, I'm glad I can eat Okinawa soba of this level while shopping at Makeman 😊 It's easy to enter, the menu is extensive, and it was a shop where I want to try other menu items again.
― 1st Visit (October 2023) ―
I ate here in October 2023. This shop is a participating shop in the “13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (2023.10.1–2024.2.29),” and I went as the 4th of 34 shops 😊
En Soba is along Gakuen-dori near Pipeline-dori.
It seems this shop's lease expires at the end of December 2023, but the relocation site hasn't been decided. Because of that, and the stamp rally running until December, I decided to go early 😁
The stamp rally booklet featured the “En Soba,” which has the same name as the shop, so I had planned to order the “En Soba,” and the menu also introduces it as the owner's recommendation.
Menu

This shop has not only Okinawa soba but also mazesoba and ramen. Previously I thought the Okinawa soba at the ramen shop “Ajisen Ramen” on the Okinawa Expressway (Nakagusuku SA) was of quite a high level, so I can expect this shop's Okinawa soba too 🤗
En soba, medium　¥800

First the broth. The moment I drank it: “Delicious” 😊 The menu says “Our proud broth, carefully simmered with selected pork bone, kelp, and bonito flakes,” and it's a gentle, delicious broth with a bonito stock lean.

Next, the noodles. The explanation said “Please enjoy the chewy, slurpy texture of the noodles kneaded with whole-wheat flour,” and indeed, they were chewy thin straight noodles, and these were delicious too 🤤
En soba, medium　¥800　Slurpy, chewy noodles, delicious.

Rating (10/15): There might be a rule that “Okinawa soba shops that also serve ramen are high level” 🤗 The bonito-based broth and chewy whole-wheat noodles were high level and delicious. However, the braised pork belly was a little sinewy, which was a pity~. The relocation site after the end of December 2023 hasn't been decided, but I think it's delicious Okinawa soba, so I hope they somehow find a new location and keep operating.

美ら花 別邸.name: Churahana Bettei
美ら花 別邸.desc: A shop I met through the “Nago City Soba Map,” the starting point of my Okinawa soba journey (13.5/15). A creative style with ramen-like house-made extra-thin noodles × a golden broth simmered for 5 hours. The signature is the ingredient-packed “vegetable soba.” It also appeared on Bananaman's Sekkaku Gourmet.
t: I ate at a shop I found through the “Nago City Soba Map,” which started my Okinawa soba journey, in September 2020 ☺
The “Nago City Soba Map” was what got me into going around Okinawa soba shops. At first I relied on this map to visit Okinawa soba shops in Nago City, lol
“Churahana” is along Route 58, so it's easy to find.
When I checked Twitter, it seems this was the 10th shop since I started going around Okinawa soba shops. Nostalgic 😁

Nago City soba tour, No. 10〜 Vegetable soba at “Churahana.” House-made? ramen-like extra-thin noodles with a rich broth. Lots of vegetables on top of an egg omelet, packed with toppings and delicious. An original Okinawa soba that's new to me. I recommend this one at least once ^_^ Finally reached double digits in my eating tour. I'll do my best to conquer them all 💪— Anji (@UisDnbFwbMz5xjm), from a tweet on September 29, 2020
Actually, this shop was introduced on “Bananaman's Sekkaku Gourmet (Nago City edition)” broadcast on August 28, 2022, but it appeared not for Okinawa soba but for “chicken wings & fu champuru” ^^;
On the show, “Kou-chan Soba” appeared as the Okinawa soba, but personally I think Churahana's “vegetable soba” is more delicious than that, so I recommend it.
It was a creative-style Okinawa soba like ramen. The “vegetable soba” that was introduced with a photo on the soba map

The house-made noodles are extra-thin like ramen. They apparently use an original blend of wheat flour and mineral-rich Okinawan salt. The smooth, firm taste unique to fresh noodles struck me as a new creative-style Okinawa soba unlike any before.

The toppings were generous vegetables on top of an egg omelet and delicious. The soba broth is said to be a golden broth made by slowly simmering aromatic vegetables, pork, and chicken for over 5 hours, and the broth was delicious too.

Rating (13.5/15): It's a creative-style Okinawa soba, and tastes may vary, but I recommend this one at least once too. Next I'd like to try a different kind too, but since I also want to go around all the soba shops on the Okinawa main island, who knows when, lol

花はな商店.name: Hanahana Shoten
花はな商店.desc: A shop particular even about its water, with special fresh noodles kneaded with fish powder and aged 48 hours for a firm texture. The signature Mixed Soba, with low-temperature-cooked whitish meat and 2 quail eggs, has a character found at no other shop.
t: I ate here in November 2023. This shop is a participating shop in the “13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (2023.10.1–2024.2.29),” and I went as the 16th of 34 shops 😊
Hanahana Shoten (there is no parking lot, so you need to use a nearby coin parking lot.)
On the wall inside the shop was an explanation of their commitment to soba 😊

Inside the shop, a note explaining their commitment to the soba was posted. Also, when I googled it, there was an explanation saying “Specially made fresh noodles with an original blend of wheat flour and fish powder kneaded in and aged for 48 hours. Firm and smooth going down,” which sounds delicious 😁

There was also an explanation about the water: “With a water purifier using 2 types of antibacterial activated carbon, free residual chlorine is removed while leaving the mineral content in the raw water. Furthermore, with a water softener with high filtration capacity, advanced chlorine is removed. Safe and secure ‘delicious water’ is used and served for the broth, boiling the noodles, and drinking water, all.” They're particular about water too, which sounds delicious.
The broth is said to be extracted over 5 hours from domestic pork bones, Hidaka kelp, and domestic bonito flakes with aromatic vegetables. That sounds delicious too 😊
The meat is also cooked at low temperature for a gentle flavor, they say. This too is different from other shops, so I'm looking forward to it, lol
The ticket machine at the entrance. Cash only is a pity; I'd like them to support cashless.
At the ticket machine, I decided to order the “Mixed Soba” introduced in the stamp rally booklet.
Mixed soba　¥900 (topping of fuchiba (mugwort) is a free service)

First, a sip of the blended broth of pork, kelp, and bonito, for which they're even particular about the water. A gentle flavor with the bonito stock of the blended broth coming through strongly. Just plain tasty 🙂
Mixed soba　¥900
Next I tried the medium-thin straight special fresh noodles with fish powder. The noodles feel a little firm and hard.
They reminded me of the fresh noodles at “Ishigufu” and “Chodegwa.” They're similarly firm and hard, so preferences may divide depending on the person.

The braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) and pork spare ribs (soki) toppings are a whitish color not found at other shops, perhaps because of low-temperature cooking. They were tender and lightly seasoned. Only a little shows in the photo, but there were 2 quail eggs, and this topping isn't found at other shops.
Rating (9/15): It's just plain tasty. The noodles are firm and hard, so preferences may differ depending on the person.
* The shop has no parking lot, so you will need to park at a nearby coin parking lot.

茶話乃屋.name: Chawanoya
茶話乃屋.desc: A hideaway mokkai soba (wood-ash lye) shop set back from Route 58, surrounded by fields in the mountain valleys of Nago (with an attached folk museum). The house-made wood-ash noodles are medium-thin noodles with a faint wood-ash flavor. Mugwort soba too. You can eat in a quiet atmosphere.
t: It was introduced on the “Nago City Soba Map” and I ate here in January 2021 😄
Chawanoya (go in off Route 58)
On the “Nago Soba Map,” “Chawanoya” was introduced as shop 34 of 41
Braised pork belly soba (sanmai-niku soba)　¥700

I ordered the “braised pork belly soba” introduced on the map. A bonito-broth soup with particular medium-thin noodles made with house-made wood ash, and the wood-ash flavor faintly wafted, so I enjoyed it 😀 The braised pork belly was also well-seasoned, tender, and delicious 😋
Rating (9/15): The shop is set back from Route 58, surrounded by fields, and you can eat in a very quiet atmosphere 😄 It's just plain tasty, so why not give it a try?

薫風.name: Kunpu
薫風.desc: A noodle shop in Onan, Nago City, particular about house-made noodles. The ¥600 “mugwort soba,” with impressive green flat noodles kneaded with mugwort, has a light pork-bone × bonito broth and the aroma of extra fuchiba. Its affordability is a charm too.
t: It was introduced on the “Nago City Soba Map” and I ate here in September 2020 😄
Kunpu
Kunpu
On the “Nago Soba Map,” “Kunpu” was introduced as shop 8 of 41
The map touted mugwort, so I ordered the “mugwort soba”
Mugwort soba　¥600

The green flat noodles kneaded with mugwort are impactful, lol The broth, a blend of pork bone and bonito stock?, is the light kind. The toppings include extra fuchiba (mugwort) and braised pork belly 😄 When you eat it, the aroma of fuchiba rises, and the quirkiness is irresistible. Delicious.

Rating (9/15): The mugwort soba I had this time is a reasonable ¥600, and when I googled it, the other menu items also seem cheap; they're particular about house-made noodles, yet I think it's relatively cheaper than other shops.
PS: There is no parking lot, so this time I parked at the nearby gymnasium parking lot, lol m(_ _)m

謝苅そば.name: Jagaru Soba
謝苅そば.desc: A popular shop on the heights of Chatan where you can see the sea in the distance from the counter. A light bonito-broth soup with a choice of boiled or fresh noodles, and large, tender soki. Lots of autographs from Kings players too.
t: I ate here in August 2022 😊
Jagaru Soba
Since I went at lunchtime, there was a line of customers. The parking lot in front of the shop was full, so I parked at the “Jagaru Park” parking lot across the street and walked a little to enter 😊
This time I ordered the “Jagaru Soba,” which shares the shop's name.
Jagaru soba (fresh noodles), medium　¥650

A light bonito-broth soup, with noodles you can choose between “boiled noodles” and “fresh noodles,” and I chose fresh noodles. The soki is tender and large. Because the shop is on the heights of Chatan Town, from the counter seats you get a view of the sea far away (around Mihama) 😊
From the counter seats you can see the sea in the distance, lol
Also, inside the shop it's full of autographs of players of the B.League (basketball) Ryukyu Golden Kings and of entertainers 😁 It was a line again today, so it's a popular shop.

Rating (10/15): Both the fresh noodles and the broth are just plain tasty, but unfortunately the time from ordering to serving was by far the slowest of all the shops I've eaten at so far (T_T) Other shops also had lines, but food came out relatively quickly after ordering, so Jagaru Soba's slowness stood out, which I thought was a pity.

うちなぁそば青雲.name: Uchinaa Soba Seiun
うちなぁそば青雲.desc: A community-rooted shop in Takushi, Urasoe. Its biggest distinguishing feature is soki soba piled so high with green onions that you can't see the noodles, with the onion flavor spreading through a light bonito soup. The menu is admirably minimal: braised pork belly soba, soki soba, and jushi only. The model airplanes inside the shop are fun too.
t: I ate here in April 2025 😄 This time I visited "Uchinaa Soba Seiun" in Takushi, Urasoe City 🍜
Uchinaa Soba Seiun (Takushi, Urasoe City)

A yellow "soba" banner stands at the entrance. A tasteful wooden sign reads "Uchinaa Soba Seiun," giving the place a charming look 😊 The exterior has an open feel, letting you see inside through the glass.
There's also the word "soba" beside the entrance. You can really feel the community-rooted atmosphere 🌺
The word "soba" beside the entrance too

Inside is a compact space, mainly counter seats. You can feel that it's a shop that has long been loved by locals 😄 Through the big windows you can see the street outside, and it has a bright, open atmosphere.
A bright interior with big windows
Over the counter you can see the kitchen, and the owner working hard making soba. Photos and models of airplanes are displayed on the walls, making it a slightly fun space ✈️
The kitchen seen over the counter

The menu is very simple, with an admirably minimal lineup: "Braised pork belly soba ¥750," "Soki soba ¥850," and "Jushi ¥150" 😄 Not having to hesitate is actually welcome. This time I decided to order the "soki soba" 🍖
Menu
The tabletop is stocked with condiments such as ichimi chili pepper, yuzu kosho, and pipāchi (island pepper) 😋
Condiments on the table

After a short wait, the "soki soba" appeared ✨ Wow, this is a surprise 😳 It's so loaded with green onions that you can't see the noodles! I've never seen another shop with this many green onions on top 😆 The green of the chopped onions spreads across the whole bowl, vivid to look at 🌿
Soki soba  ¥850 (so loaded with green onions you can't see the noodles!)
First, the soup. It's a light, bonito-based soup with a gentle flavor 😊 With the onion flavor added, it's a refreshing, easy-to-drink bowl.

Pushing aside the onions and pulling up the noodles, out came medium-thin straight noodles. The texture is on the soft side and they pair well with the light soup 🍜 Since it's loaded with onions, every time you slurp the noodles you enjoy the onion texture and flavor together, which is this shop's special charm.
Lifting up the medium-thin straight noodles
The soki topping has a moderately soaked-in flavor and is ordinarily tasty 😄 However, some parts had a bit of sinewy texture.
Overall, being able to feel the texture and flavor of the onions at all times is distinctive, and it was an ordinarily tasty bowl 😊

Rating (9/15): A light bonito-based soup, soft medium-thin straight noodles, and moderately flavor-soaked soki made for an ordinarily tasty Okinawa soba 😄 Above all, the onion-loaded bowl where you can't see the noodles is a distinctiveness you won't find at other shops 🌿 The atmosphere of being loved by the community is nice too, so when you come to Takushi, Urasoe City, why not stop by once? 🍜

沖縄そばcafe 崎門.name: Okinawa Soba Cafe Sachijo
沖縄そばcafe 崎門.desc: Opened in February 2025. An Okinawa soba cafe in a stylishly renovated old house with a cement-tile roof. Its signature is the "Sachijo Soba," with a classic pork-bone broth soup and medium-thick round noodles, topped with fish cake, pig's feet (tebichi), bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki), and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku). The cafe-like interior is popular with locals.
t: This time I visited "Okinawa Soba Cafe Sachijo (Sachijō)" in Moromisato, Okinawa City 😊 I went to eat here in May 2025 😄
Okinawa Soba Cafe Sachijo (it looks like an old house with a cement-tile roof)
Okinawa Soba Cafe Sachijo
Okinawa Soba Cafe Sachijo

The exterior alone has a great atmosphere. It's a building like an old house with a cement-tile roof, with a solid presence. At first glance it looks like a traditional Okinawan home, but the sign says "Okinawa Soba Cafe," giving it a curious charm where tradition and stylishness coexist ✨ I'm told it's a new shop that only opened in February 2025, so my expectations are rising.
Inside the shop (stylish like a cafe)

Once inside, in contrast to the old-house atmosphere of the exterior, the interior has been newly and cleanly renovated, and a calm, cafe-like space opens up 😌 I visited at lunchtime, and it was bustling with local customers, so I felt this is a popular shop.
Menu (Sachijo set)
Menu
Menu
Menu (they have shaved ice too 😄)
Menu (drinks and desserts)
Looking at the menu, this time I decided to order the large "Sachijo Soba," named after the shop 😋
Sachijo Soba, large  ¥1,050
Here comes the "Sachijo Soba, large"! First, my usual sip of the soup 😊 It's a soup with a classic pork-bone broth, with a reassuring flavor of the quintessential Okinawa soba.
Sachijo Soba, large  ¥1,050

Next, the noodles. The noodles are medium-thick round noodles with a soft texture. They cling well to the soup and are easy to eat 🍜 The toppings are plentiful: fish cake, pig's feet (tebichi), bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki), and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) 😆 The meat has a moderately soaked-in flavor, which is quite nice. However, the braised pork belly and bone-in pork ribs had some parts that still had a bit of sinewy texture.

Rating (9/15): The flavor was "ordinary," a bowl where you can comfortably enjoy classic Okinawa soba 😊 Above all, the atmosphere of the stylishly renovated old house with a cement-tile roof is lovely, and it's understandable why it's bustling with locals. When you come to the Moromisato area of Okinawa City, why not give it a try? 🍜

農産物直売所 畑人市場.name: Nosanbutsu Chokubaijo Hatabito Ichiba
農産物直売所 畑人市場.desc: A bowl you can enjoy inside a farm produce market in Zanami, Itoman. The only menu item is Okinawa soba, at a one-coin ¥500. A pork-bone broth with a salty touch and soft, thin straight noodles. It has a warm atmosphere like a gathering place for the local grandmas.
t: On this Okinawa soba journey, I visited the "Farm Produce Market Hatabito Ichiba" in Zanami, Itoman City 🍜
I ate here in May 2025 😄
Farm Produce Market Hatabito Ichiba (look for the yellow building)

A vivid yellow building is the landmark, and inside the shop, local fresh vegetables and specialty products are lined up. It has a wonderfully warm atmosphere, like a gathering place for the local grandmas 😊
Seeing people chatting (yuntaku) while shopping, I feel this is a place loved by the community.
Local fresh vegetables lined up inside the shop
The direct-sales corner where specialty products are also displayed
Now, the only Okinawa soba on the menu you can eat here is "Okinawa soba"! No need to hesitate, an admirably minimal competition 😄
The price is, amazingly, ¥500. Okinawa soba prices have been rising recently, so being able to eat it for one coin is nice.
The "Okinawa soba ¥500" sign at the entrance
The "Hatabito Ichiba Shokudo" corner inside the shop
Okinawa soba  ¥500
First, the soup. It's a pork-bone broth soup, the type where the saltiness comes through firmly.
The noodles are the thin straight type, finished on the soft side. It has a gentle, old-fashioned texture.
Thin straight noodles

The toppings are a simple composition of braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), fish cake, and pickled red ginger. The braised pork belly has a moderately soaked-in flavor, which is nice, but the sinewy texture was really strong ^^;

The portion is average, so it may be unsatisfying for people who want to eat heartily. It has just the right volume for a light snack while shopping. Considering the ¥500 price, I think the value is good 😄

Rating (9/15): The bowl was very, very ordinary in taste, but the good thing about a produce-market eatery like this is that you can taste the local atmosphere along with it. When driving toward Itoman, why not try a one-coin bowl while shopping for fresh vegetables? 👋

本家亀そば うん玉店.name: Honke Kame Soba Untama-ten
本家亀そば うん玉店.desc: A Kame Soba group shop in Ikeda, Nishihara, bustling with local customers. Its feature is a fairly robust soup in which agu pork broth combines with the umami of stir-fried meat and vegetables, and the signature dish is the Agu Soba at ¥930. The menu is also extensive, with set meals, rice bowls, and more.
t: On this Okinawa soba journey, I went to "Honke Kame Soba Untama-ten" in Ikeda, Nishihara Town 😄 I ate here in May 2025 😆
Exterior of Honke Kame Soba Untama-ten
The exterior is striking, with a well-worn sign standing under the blue sky and an entrance made of wood. A big sign along the road also had parking directions.
The sign along the road and the parking directions

A one-item service coupon I received when I ate Okinawa soba before at "Isagawa Shokudo" in Nago City. When I looked at the back, it said it could also be used at "Honke Kame Soba Untama-ten," so this time I visited with that service coupon 😁
The shop bustling with local customers

When I entered the shop, it was bustling with local customers. Inside there are table seats and tatami raised seating, and the atmosphere of being rooted in the community is nice. As expected of Kame Soba, it's bustling with local customers 😆
Table seats and tatami raised seating
A ticket machine with an extensive menu

Looking at the ticket machine at the entrance, the menu is quite extensive, with not only Okinawa soba but also set meals, rice bowls, curry, and more. What I ordered this time was the "Agu Soba" for ¥930. And I used the service coupon to get jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice) as well. The combination of Okinawa soba and jushi is always welcome 👍
Agu Soba ¥930, service jushi, and the service coupon
It was a little different from the bowl I imagined from the name "Agu Soba." What came out was a bowl like vegetable soba, topped with stir-fried bean sprouts, onions, and pork 😄
First, my usual sip of the soup.

The agu pork broth soup combines with the umami from the stir-fried meat and vegetables for a fairly robust flavor. The agu broth and the broth from the stir-fried pork and vegetables blend well. It's ordinarily delicious 👍
Next, the noodles. The noodles are the thin straight type with a slightly soft texture. They're easy to eat together with the stir-fried meat and vegetables and blend well with the robust soup.
Thin straight noodles

The toppings are stir-fried bean sprouts, onions, and pork. You can eat the vegetables together, and the umami of the pork and vegetables adds to the soup. It wasn't what I pictured from the name "Agu Soba," but as a vegetable soba it's an ordinarily delicious bowl 😋
I also enjoyed the jushi that I got with the service coupon. A service coupon that links the earlier Isagawa Shokudo to this Untama-ten is fun and very much in the spirit of an Okinawa soba journey 😁

Rating (9/15): The robust soup, combining agu pork broth with the umami of stir-fried meat and vegetables, was memorable. The noodles are thin, straight, and slightly soft. It wasn't the "Agu Soba" I'd imagined and was more like a vegetable soba, but it had the steady reliability typical of Kame Soba and was ordinarily delicious. It's understandable why it's bustling with local customers 😄

ながどう家.name: Nagadoya
ながどう家.desc: "Kominka Iyashidokoro," a traditional Ryukyuan old house. Enjoy it in a tatami room that feels like visiting grandma's house: a soup with strong bonito broth and wonderful chewy medium-thick wavy noodles. The signature "Nagadoya Soba" at ¥1,000 comes with all of braised pork belly, soki, and nankotsu, and you can choose the meat seasoning from sweet soy sauce or light salt. Try it as a set with Navy Underground Headquarters Park.
t: On this Okinawa soba journey, while visiting Navy Underground Headquarters Park, I went to "Nagadoya" in Nagado, Tomigusuku City 🍜 I ate here in May 2025 😄
Nagadoya (look for the red gate)
A garden spreads out once you pass through the gate

A traditional Ryukyuan old house is used as the shop just as it is 😊 With a red-tile roof, a well-tended garden, and an approach lined with stepping stones, it feels less like coming to an Okinawa soba shop and more like visiting a relative's house in the countryside.
The old-house main building with its red tiles and beautiful garden
On the wall is a handwritten notice. It says they're open 10:30 to 15:00 and closed on Tuesdays and Wednesdays. The parking lot is behind the building 🚗
Closed Tuesdays and Wednesdays, open 10:30 to 15:00. Parking is at the back

Inside, low tables are lined up in a tatami room, and a relaxing air flows as if I'd come to visit grandma's house 😆 Old furnishings such as old family photos and a dressing table are displayed, making it a deeply atmospheric space.
You can relax and eat in the tatami room
A nostalgic interior lined with old furnishings

Now looking at the menu, the one labeled as the shop's recommendation is the signature "Nagadoya Soba" at ¥1,000. It's a luxurious bowl with all three kinds of meat on top: braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), soki, and nankotsu (soft bone) 😆 I ordered this without hesitation.
Menu (the shop's recommendation, "Nagadoya Soba" ¥1,000)

There are also quite a lot of other menu items, such as Uchinaa-don, taco rice, curry soba, yushi-dofu soba, and limited-quantity bean sprout and beef soba. For an additional ¥350 on any soba, it seems you can also make it a "soba set meal" that comes with jushi and a small side dish 😋
A menu rich in rice bowls and unusual soba
Drink menu
There's also a "Kids' Soba" for ¥300 (for elementary school sixth grade and under), a shop that's friendly to families too 👨‍👩‍👧
The "Kids' Soba" ¥300 sign

And what I found interesting was the line written on the menu: "Meat flavor... you can choose from sweet soy sauce or light salt." Shops where you can choose the meat seasoning are hard to find elsewhere 😄 I couldn't decide, so I asked the staff member, and they recommended the sweet soy sauce, so I obediently asked for that.
After a while, the "Nagadoya Soba" appeared! In a black bowl, braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), soki, and nankotsu are piled up, and the green of the green onions stands out ✨
Nagadoya Soba  ¥1,000 (with three kinds of meat: braised pork belly, soki, and nankotsu)
First, the soup. Mm, the bonito broth is strong and delicious 👍 This is high-level.
Next, the noodles. They're medium-thick wavy noodles, and their chewy texture is delicious 😋 It's a bowl that's highly satisfying even with just the noodles.
Chewy medium-thick wavy noodles

And the three kinds of meat. The sweet soy sauce seasoning is more robust than I'd imagined, with the flavor soaked in deeply. I could also taste the sweetness of brown sugar, which is distinctive in its own way.
However, the braised pork belly, soki, and nankotsu all had a fair amount of sinewy texture ^^; It's a signature menu where you can taste three kinds of meat, so I thought this was a bit of a waste.

That said, the level of the soup and noodles is truly high. A bowl enjoyed in an old house with the atmosphere of coming to grandma's house is special in itself 😄 When you visit Navy Underground Headquarters Park, why not stop by as a set? 👋

Rating (10/15): The soup with strong bonito broth and the chewy medium-thick wavy noodles are of unquestionable level. Being able to choose the meat seasoning from sweet soy sauce or light salt is interesting too. As long as the sinewy texture of the meat doesn't bother you, I think it's a bowl that would rank quite high 😊

てびちのてーすけ.name: Tebichi no Tesuke
てびちのてーすけ.desc: A pig's feet (tebichi) specialty shop recognizable by its laid-back pig sign. Its signature is the “Tesuke Special,” topped with pig's feet, braised pork belly, soft-bone pork ribs, yushi-dofu, and sea lettuce — everything. A light tebichi soba to enjoy with vinegar and shikuwasa pepper. They also sell seasoned frozen pig's feet and horse sashimi.
t: * This article was created with AI (Chat GPT 5 Thinking) and partly supplemented by me 😁
I ate here in December 2024 😆 This time I went to “Tebichi no Tesuke” in Sashiki Shinkai, Nanjo City.
Tebichi no Tesuke
Tebichi no Tesuke

In a corner of a well-worn building, a handwritten “Open” sign and a laid-back pig sign greet you boldly. As in the photo, “Tebichi specialty shop” is written in big letters, and artificial turf is laid in front of the shop, giving it a nice hideaway feel 🐷
Inside the shop
As for condiments, there is no kōrēgūsu (chili-infused awamori) — instead there is vinegar and shikuwasa pepper.
There is also a panel on how to eat tebichi
Inside, the counter and tables are compactly arranged, with figurines casually displayed, giving it a relaxed, homey feel.
Menu
Menu
Menu
Tesuke Special　¥1,300

From the menu I ordered the “Tesuke Special” without hesitation. With the dignity of an “everything on top” bowl, pig's feet (tebichi), braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), yushi-dofu, and sea lettuce (āsa) — the tastiest parts of Okinawa — are all packed into one bowl. The blended broth has a somewhat strong bonito stock and a noticeable saltiness.
Tesuke Special　¥1,300
The noodles are medium-thin fresh noodles, slightly wavy. They're chewy 🍜

The star, the pig's feet, is wobbly-soft. The skin melts, and sweetness spreads each time the layers of collagen unravel. The seasoning is quite restrained, and as the notice on the table says “we recommend adding vinegar,” a single drizzle brings out a sharp crispness all at once. The braised pork belly leans light. It has a little sinewy texture. The soft-bone pork ribs are soft right through to the bone.

The yushi-dofu topping is soft and gentle, and its sweetness swells further once it absorbs the broth. The green of the sea lettuce brings the scent of the sea, adding Okinawan flavor to the scene in the bowl, which is nice too. The condiments of shirogaki-negi (shredded green onion) and julienned ginger sharpen the outline, and it felt designed to run from start to finish as a “light tebichi soba.” There's no kōrēgūsu on the table; instead there is shikuwasa pepper, which pairs wonderfully. The citrus freshness lifts the broth's saltiness and the bonito aroma, and neatly pulls together the aftertaste. Toward the end, I dissolved a little chili paste, and the slow-building heat of the spice made my forehead sweat. Yet the outline of the broth doesn't collapse, and it let me drink it down happily to the end. By the time I finished eating, I was warmed from the core of my body 🔥

On the wall there is also a poster titled “How to eat tebichi deliciously,” and it's interesting that it carefully guides you through using vinegar, Tabasco, and even turning it into a broth-over-rice dish.
I'd like to try the bone soup soba too 😄

By the register there's also a notice for the “bone soup soba.” I thought I'd like to go for that next time. In the merchandise corner, in addition to seasoned frozen pig's feet, they even sell horse sashimi. It's an enticing lineup that makes you want to take it home as a snack for drinking at home, and my purse strings almost loosened. I felt that the reason for its popularity lies not only in the bowl but also in how it creates this kind of “room for enjoyment” 😊

Rating (9/15): All in all, it was a reassuring bowl for which the words “just plain tasty” fit perfectly, without any gimmicks. It pleasantly betrays the image that tebichi means rich and heavy, with a lightness that leaves no heaviness after the meal, which I like ✌️
When you come to Nanjo City, why not give it a try once?

そば処 じゅりあん.name: Soba-dokoro Jurian
そば処 じゅりあん.desc: A shop with an additive-free (no chemical seasoning) broth of bonito, kelp, and Agu pork bone. The soft-bone pork ribs soba (regular) is a reasonable ¥640, and there is a ¥100 discount service when you show your Itomaru parking lot ticket.
t: I ate here in November 2023. This shop is a participating shop in the “13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (2023.10.1–2024.2.29),” and I went as the 21st of 34 shops 😊
Soba-dokoro Jurian

This shop has no parking lot, but a few dozen meters away on foot there is a large paid parking lot at “Itoman Market Itomaru,” and according to the stamp rally booklet, “show your parking ticket for a one-hour fee cashback,” so the parking problem seems fine 😁
The paid parking lot of “Itoman Market Itomaru”
The paid parking lot of “Itoman Market Itomaru”
Inside the shop (it's fairly large)
Inside the shop (it's fairly large)
For my order I chose the “soft-bone pork ribs soba (regular) with soft-boiled egg topping” introduced in the stamp rally booklet.
Menu (with toppings)
Menu (without toppings)

The “soft-bone pork ribs soba (regular) with soft-boiled egg topping” I ordered is ¥640, but when I showed my parking ticket they said “we'll take ¥100 off,” making it ¥540 😊 You don't see this price range much at other shops; I think it's reasonable.
“Soft-bone pork ribs soba (regular) with soft-boiled egg topping” ¥640 → ¥540 (with parking cashback)
First, a sip of the broth. This shop's broth is made with bonito, kelp, and Agu pork bone with no chemical seasoning, so they are particular about ingredients. The flavor is gentle too.
“Soft-bone pork ribs soba (regular) with soft-boiled egg topping” ¥640 → ¥540 (with parking cashback)

Next, the noodles 🤗 They are medium-thick straight noodles and on the soft side. The soft-bone pork ribs also seem to be seasoned with preservative-free soy sauce; there was a little sinewy texture, but they were tender and gently flavored.
After finishing, when leaving the paid parking lot, I inserted my parking ticket to put in the cashback ¥100, and to my surprise the display said “¥0” (;^ω^)
I think it's because I finished eating in a short 10 to 20 minutes and took my car out. In the end, the soba came to a quite reasonable ¥540, lol

Rating (9/15): It's just plain tasty 😊 Moreover, if you leave the parking lot early, the parking fee is free and you also get the ¥100 cashback with the parking ticket at the shop, so effectively you can have Okinawa soba at a reasonable price 😁

沖縄そば 金太郎.name: Okinawa Soba Kintaro
沖縄そば 金太郎.desc: A hugely popular shop famous for “Minami Jiro,” the Okinawa soba version of Ramen Jiro. A soy-sauce-based ramen using fresh Okinawa soba noodles, authentic Jiro style where you're asked about the amount of vegetables and garlic. Hearty portions, recommended for those who want to eat their fill.
t: I went to eat here in February 2024 😄 I learned about this shop from a newspaper, and I was curious because it apparently has an Okinawa soba version of “Ramen Jiro,” which I had experienced for the first time in Tokyo in October 2023, so I came to eat 😄
Okinawa Soba Kintaro
Incidentally, the image below is my X post from when I first ate “Ramen Jiro” in Tokyo (^0^;)

I went without doing detailed research, and since the customer in front of me ordered “small,” I thought “small” literally means less and ordered “small,” but I was shocked when it arrived, lol I ate and ate but the amount never went down, it got painful, and I gave up with half left (^0^;)
Tweet from my first Ramen Jiro experience 😆 I gave up with half left (^0^;)

How about this “Okinawa Soba Kintaro”? I came several dozen minutes before opening, and right before it opened there were lots of customers. The parking lot filled up immediately too. I thought it's definitely a popular shop.
Menu posted at the shop entrance (the item called “Minami Jiro” seems to be the Jiro-style Okinawa soba 😆)
Menu posted at the shop entrance (besides the soba menu there are rice bowl dishes too 😄)
Inside the shop there is a ticket machine, and I ordered the “Minami Jiro.” The sizes are large and medium, but just in case I ordered “medium” (^0^;)
This ticket machine supports cashless payment, and I was able to pay with PayPay. Cashless is great 👍
When I ordered “Minami Jiro, medium,” the staff asked “How would you like the amount of vegetables and garlic?” so I ordered “extra, please.”
Will I be okay? Will I repeat the mistake of Tokyo's Ramen Jiro? My heart is pounding (^0^;)
Inside the shop (it's quite spacious)
Minami Jiro (medium)　¥900
Here it comes. Like the original “Ramen Jiro,” you can't see the noodles (^0^;)
First I taste the broth. As the menu says “This is ramen using fresh Okinawa soba noodles,” the broth is soy-sauce-based and it's already ramen (^0^;)
But it's just plain tasty. Next I want to taste the noodles, but I can't see them and don't seem able to reach them, so I eat the vegetables, chashu, and garlic bit by bit (^0^;)
The broth has a strong flavor and contains garlic, so at any rate it has punch.
Minami Jiro (medium)　¥900

I reached the noodles and tasted them. Chewy fresh noodles, just plain tasty. I asked for extra vegetables and garlic with the medium size; naturally the amount is smaller than a small at the original “Ramen Jiro,” but it's still full of volume, and I think it is more than the large size at other shops. I managed to finish it all 😄

Rating (9/15): It was ramen, practically 😄 The flavor is strong and punchy, and the portion is large too, so I recommend it to those who want to eat their fill. Incidentally, the amount of garlic is also extreme, so your mouth will smell of garlic all day, lol

みらい食堂.name: Mirai Shokudo
みらい食堂.desc: A diner that used to be inside Michi-no-Eki Ginoza (* now closed). Its Okinawa soba featured the signature “jagamen,” noodles kneaded with potatoes from Ginoza Village, and the Ginoza soba topped with pig's feet, braised pork belly, pork spare ribs, and egg omelet was hearty. I'm keeping this article as a record.
t: I ate here in January 2021.
Note: Unfortunately this shop is now closed. I'm writing it down as a record.
Mirai Shokudo (inside the Ginoza Village roadside station) “In the photo it says ‘Taiyotei,’ but I'm not sure why ^^;”
Menu (at Mirai Shokudo, the noodles are “jagamen,” made with potatoes from Ginoza Village)
Ginoza soba, large　¥750

I ordered the “Ginoza soba, large.” The noodles are medium-thin, made from potatoes. The broth is bonito stock and delicious 😋 There seemed to be no difference from ordinary noodles ^^; The toppings were hearty too, with pig's feet (tebichi), braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), pork spare ribs (soki), and egg omelet.

Rating (9/15): It was just plain tasty, but it's a pity it has closed. Ginoza Village promotes itself as a potato village, and the road lighting fixtures in the area are designed as “potatoes,” so please take a look when you pass nearby 😁 It seems to be a shop called “Shokudo Manjiro?” now, so maybe they have Okinawa soba using “jagamen.”

みーなみ.name: Mīnami
みーなみ.desc: A local diner that pushes its goat (yagi) dishes (there is even a goat sashimi vending machine!). The classic Okinawa soba comes with free fuchiba on a separate plate, so you can change the flavor partway and enjoy it to the end. Its unpretentious atmosphere with table and tatami seating is charming.
t: For this Okinawa soba outing, I went to “Mīnami” in Minami-Uehara, Nakagusuku Village 🌞 I ate here in March 2025 😄
Mīnami
Outdoor vending machine (it's all goat (^0^;))

The exterior has a bright sign like a blue sky, giving it a somewhat laid-back feel. At first glance it's simple and approachable, but when you look at the vending machine and banners beside the entrance, the presence of goat dishes such as goat soup and goat sashimi is quite strong, and you immediately think “oh, this shop pushes goat,” which makes a strong impression 🐐
Inside the shop
Inside the shop

Inside, the wood-grain walls give a calm atmosphere, with table seats and tatami seating, and it definitely has an old-fashioned diner feel 😊 I personally like this unpretentious feel quite a bit. It didn't feel designed for tourists, but like a place that is an extension of everyday life where local people just come to eat.
Menu
Looking at the menu boards, goat soba, goat soup set meal, soki soba, and more were lined up, showing this shop's character. Among them I chose the “Okinawa soba (braised pork belly), large” 👀
Okinawa soba (braised pork belly), large　¥800

The Okinawa soba that arrived was quite classic just from looking at it. With a slightly clear broth, medium-thin straight noodles, braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), fish cake (kamaboko), and green onions, it has a comforting quality that makes you want to say “this is diner Okinawa soba” 🍥 Also, free fuchiba comes on a separate plate, which was a nice touch 🌿 A service like this is quietly appreciated. At first you eat it as is, and then you can change the flavor partway, so it's easy to eat without getting bored until the end.

First the broth. My impression after one sip was that it's probably a blended broth, but neither pork bone nor bonito pushed to the front. There was also a faint gentle sweetness, making it easy to drink ☺️ But for better or worse the individuality was faint, without an obvious punch like “the bonito is strong!” or “the pork-bone richness is strong!” It's not that the balance is off at all, but honestly, as for whether it's a broth that leaves a strong impression, it doesn't quite reach that.
Okinawa soba (braised pork belly), large　¥800

The noodles were medium-thin straight noodles, finished on the soft side. The noodles themselves didn't have a strong presence, and neither in texture nor aroma did they make me think “these noodles are great.” Not bad, but my impression is that it's an overall mild bowl.

The braised pork belly was moderately well-seasoned, neither too strong nor too weak, and the balance there was not bad 🥢 It wasn't sweet-and-salty to the point of pushing itself forward, so it didn't spoil the broth's character. However, when I ate it, the sinewy texture was rather strong, and it wasn't the type that falls apart. It has a chew, but if it had a bit more fat tenderness and melt-in-the-mouth quality, the satisfaction would go up another notch. Including the fish cake and green onions, the toppings overall are quite basic, giving the impression of an old-fashioned bowl without gimmicks.

And when I added the fuchiba partway through, it made quite a nice accent 🌿✨ To a broth that was a little mild as is, the fuchiba's characteristic aroma and faint bitterness were added, and the flavor tightened up. Rather than putting it all in from the start, adding it a bit at a time as I watched was more enjoyable. Thanks to this free topping, I could eat without it getting too monotonous until the end. Honestly, where it would have ended with “it's ordinary” with the plain state alone, the fuchiba lifted it a little 😌

Rating (9/15): My overall impression settles at “this is really just ordinary Okinawa soba.” Of course that's not only in a bad sense; it means it has no odd quirks and is a standard bowl you can eat with confidence at a diner 🍜 But if you ask whether I'd go all the way from afar for this Okinawa soba, I didn't feel it was decisive enough. Precisely because it's a shop with prominent goat dishes, I thought it would be interesting if the standard Okinawa soba had a bit more character too. Still, as a bowl you can eat casually in a calm interior while changing the flavor with the free fuchiba, it wasn't bad 🙂 It was the kind of Okinawa soba shop you'd drop into on a whim if you were nearby.

裕次郎そば.name: Yujiro Soba
裕次郎そば.desc: A long-established shop that has been going since 1989 in Kitamae, Chatan. The owner is a fan of Ishihara Yujiro, and the interior is lined with Yujiro posters and autograph cards. The signature "Yujiro Soba" (large ¥800) combines a bonito and pork-bone blended broth with translucent in-house medium-thin flat noodles, topped with braised pork belly, fish cake, and soft bone. Ramen menu items are available too.
t: On this Okinawa soba journey, I visited "Yujiro Soba" in Kitamae, Chatan Town 🍜 I ate here in June 2025 😄
Yujiro Soba
It's a solidly built shop with a red-tile roof that catches the eye. The parking lot was fairly large and it felt easy to enter.
Inside the shop
Inside, wooden tables and round stools are lined up, with the air of a nostalgic Showa-era diner. It's a calming space, and you can't help wanting to linger in a shop like this 😊

And looking around the shop, what I noticed was the posters of Ishihara Yujiro lined up all over the wall. The shop name "Yujiro Soba" seems to come from that, and I could tell the owner is quite a Yujiro fan 😄
Ishihara Yujiro movie posters on the wall
A wooden sign reading "in-house noodles" and a Yujiro poster
A wooden sign reading "in-house noodles" is also hung on the wall, showing their confidence in the noodles. A line like this raises my expectations 🤤
A "Senkyaku Banrai" plaque and autograph cards

A splendid "Senkyaku Banrai" (a thousand customers, ten thousand visits) plaque, with countless autograph cards filling the space around it. You can tell this is a shop that has been loved for a long time.
Inside the shop, the raised tatami seating
In the back there's also a raised tatami seating area, built so that even families could relax 😊

Now looking at the menu, the Okinawa soba lineup runs Yujiro Soba, soft-bone pork rib soba, bone-in pork rib soba, bean sprout soba, pork-and-chicken soba, and plain soba. What's interesting is that, even though it's an Okinawa soba shop, there's a full ramen menu too. Soy sauce, salt, tonkotsu, mountain vegetable, miso, tanmen, and extra spicy are all there, quite a range 🍜
Menu: Okinawa soba and ramen
Menu: set meals and side dishes
Set meals and set menus are plentiful too, and sides like inari and tempura are available. I hesitated, but this time I decided to have the signature menu item named after the shop, "Yujiro Soba."
Yujiro Soba (large)  ¥800
This is what was brought out. A classic bowl with plenty of soup, topped with braised pork belly, soft-bone pork ribs, fish cake, and green onions ✨
First, the soup. A blended bonito and pork-bone broth, and the umami of both came through firmly. It's a balanced soup that doesn't lean only toward bonito or only toward pork bone 😋
Yujiro Soba (large)  ¥800
And the in-house noodles they're proud of are medium-thin flat noodles. Beautiful, translucent noodles, boiled on the soft side 🍜
The toppings are braised pork belly and soft-bone pork ribs. Both are fairly firmly seasoned. However, I did notice a fair amount of sinewy texture, which bothered me a bit ^^;

Rating (9/15): A soup where the bonito and pork-bone blended broth is nicely balanced, with translucent in-house medium-thin flat noodles. The braised pork belly and soft-bone pork ribs are firmly seasoned. Overall, the flavor was honestly average, but the interior brimming with love for Yujiro is something you can only experience here 😊

Barシーサー亭.name: Bar Shisa-tei
Barシーサー亭.desc: Authentic Okinawa soba served by a bar in Goya, Okinawa City, in the heart of Koza. A light pork-bone broth soup, with a choice of wavy noodles or locally milled flour noodles. The signature "Shisa Soba" (¥950) is a loaded bowl topped with smooth yushi-dofu from the long-established Kawakami Tofu, braised pork belly, soft-bone pork ribs, and even a soft-fried egg.
t: On this Okinawa soba journey, I visited "Bar Shisa-tei" in Goya, Okinawa City 🍜 I ate here in June 2025 😄
Exterior of the shop
When I was passing by I noticed an "Okinawa soba" banner standing out, and I couldn't help but drop in. The combination of a bar and Okinawa soba is so intriguing, isn't it? 😆
The shop entrance
A wooden "Bar" sign hangs at the entrance, and it really does look completely like a bar. I doubt many people go in thinking it's an Okinawa soba shop (lol)
The "Shisa-tei" sign
Beside it is a splendid yellow "Shisa-tei" sign adorned with a shisa lion-dog. Seeing it makes me feel it's an Okinawan shop and warms me up to it 😊
Inside, shelves lined with bottles
Inside, bottles of liquor line the entire wall, truly the interior of a bar. Honestly, I was a little on guard thinking, "What kind of soba will come out of here?" ^^;
Menu
But when they showed me the menu, it was surprisingly authentic. And you can choose the noodles from "wavy noodles" and "locally milled flour noodles (+¥50)" 🤤
Soba toppings and drink menu
The toppings are well stocked too: soft-bone pork ribs, braised pork belly, and yushi-dofu are each +¥200, and extra noodles are +¥150.
Notes on their commitment

There's also the line "All the meat uses prefectural pork! Choose your prefectural noodles!" The soup is based on a light broth, and they say to let them know if you prefer rich. Such solid commitment, you wouldn't think it's a bar ✨
MENU: soba price list

Shisa Soba ¥950, soft-bone pork rib soba ¥880, braised pork belly soba ¥880, yushi-dofu soba ¥800, vegetable soba ¥900. I hesitated, but naturally I decided to have the "Shisa Soba" named after the shop.
Inside the shop
After placing my order and looking around the shop, there's even a billiards table so you can play while drinking at the bar 😄
Shisa Soba  ¥950

And here's what was brought out. Loaded with yushi-dofu, braised pork belly, soft-bone pork ribs, and even a soft-fried egg. It's a more authentic bowl than you'd expect from Okinawa soba made by a bar ✨
First, the soup. A light pork-bone broth flavor, a gentle bowl that goes down easily 😋

What stood out among the toppings was the yushi-dofu. It's apparently from the long-established "Kawakami Tofu" in Okinawa City, and its smooth texture is irresistible 😊 The braised pork belly and soft-bone pork ribs were both tender, and their seasoning is light as well. However, I did feel a bit of sinewy texture ^^;
And something you rarely see at other shops is the soft-fried egg. This is a welcome touch.
Shisa Soba  ¥950
The noodles are medium-thick wavy noodles, boiled on the soft side. They went well with the light soup 🍜

Rating (9/15): A light pork-bone broth soup with soft medium-thick wavy noodles. It's a loaded bowl topped with smooth yushi-dofu from Kawakami Tofu, tender braised pork belly and soft-bone pork ribs, and even a soft-fried egg. It was an ordinarily delicious bowl, hard to believe it came from a bar 😊

みの家 天久りうぼう楽市店.name: Minoya Ameku Ryubo Rakuichi Branch
みの家 天久りうぼう楽市店.desc: A long-established Okinawan cuisine restaurant inside the "Ameku Ryubo Rakuichi" commercial complex in Naha Shintoshin. An overwhelming selection from soba to champuru, simmered dishes, soups, set meals, and side dishes. The "Soki Soba" (¥950) has a light pork-bone-based soup with soft, medium-thick straight noodles.
t: On this Okinawa soba journey, I visited "Minoya Ameku Ryubo Rakuichi Branch" in Ameku, Naha City 🍜 I ate here in June 2025 😄
Exterior of the shop

It's a shop inside "Ameku Ryubo Rakuichi," a commercial complex in Naha Shintoshin. The sign lined with "Okinawa soba" and "goya champuru" is the landmark, and it's nice how casually you can drop by while shopping 😊
Soba menu

Opening the menu, the first thing that catches my eye is "40 years of commitment to flavor." It's apparently a long-established Okinawan cuisine restaurant ✨ The soba lineup is Okinawa soba ¥800, soki soba ¥950, braised pork belly soba ¥900, tebichi soba ¥900, offal (nakami) soba ¥900, and sea lettuce (āsa) soba ¥950 (all tax included).
Set menu
Champuru and miso-simmered menu

And with every turn of the page, I'm overwhelmed by the sheer size of the menu. There are soba sets, takana fried rice sets, yakisoba sets, even island Napolitan, and Okinawan dishes are lined up: goya champuru, tofu champuru, fu champuru, liver and chives, and miso-simmered eggplant and loofah sets 😆
Set meals and simmered dishes menu
Minoya set meal and āsa soup set meal
Soups and jushi menu

Soki simmered sets, tebichi simmered sets, Minoya Special, Minoya set meal, āsa soup set meal, nakami soup and tebichi soup sets, jushi, yushi-dofu, even inamuruchi. It feels like nearly all of Okinawan home cooking is covered, and I don't think you'd ever tire of it no matter how often you come 🤤
Rice bowls and fried food menu
In addition, there are fried foods and rice bowls such as tonkatsu sets, katsudon, karaage sets, and chicken tempura sets.
A la carte menu
Demi-glace hamburger steak set and a la carte
Side dishes such as kūbu irichii, mimigā, and yushi-dofu, a demi-glace hamburger steak set, and drinks — there really is everything 😄
Great-value light drinking set

From 16:00 there's also a "great-value light drinking set," with either a draft beer set or a sour set at ¥1,200. You can reportedly pick one item from fried gyoza, karaage, fried tacos, and more, and I feel the breadth of an Okinawan casual diner rather than a soba shop 🍺
Takeout-only side dish menu
The takeout-only side dish menu is rich too.
Inside the shop
The interior is an unpretentious diner with table seats lined up. It looks like you could relax even by yourself 😊
The side dish showcase at the shop front
At the shop front there's also a showcase lined with bento boxes and side dishes, and looking at just this part it looks like a deli.
Soki Soba  ¥950
Now, what I ordered this time was the "Soki Soba." This is what was brought out ✨ An orthodox bowl, topped with soki, kelp, and green onions.
First, the soup. A gentle pork-bone-based flavor 😋
Soki Soba  ¥950
The noodles are medium-thick straight noodles, boiled on the soft side.
The soki is moderately seasoned, with the flavor soaked in just right. However, I did feel a fair amount of sinewy texture ^^;

Rating (9/15): A light pork-bone-based soup with soft, medium-thick straight noodles. The soki is moderately seasoned but has a sinewy texture. For better or worse, it was an ordinary Okinawa soba 😊 However, the sheer breadth of the menu lined with Okinawan dishes had the dignity of a long-established shop.

潮騒そば.name: Shiosai Soba
潮騒そば.desc: An Okinawa soba shop on the first floor of "Hotel Shiosai," along the seaside in Ishikawa, Uruma, where you can also stay without meals. The signature "Shiosai Soba" (regular ¥1,080 / large ¥1,180) is a hearty bowl that even includes pig's feet, two big pieces of soft-bone pork ribs, offal, knotted kelp, and daikon radish. Bustling with local customers.
t: On this Okinawa soba journey, I visited "Shiosai Soba" in Ishikawa, Uruma City 🍜 I ate here in June 2025 😄
Exterior of the shop / Hotel Shiosai

It's a shop on the first floor of "Hotel Shiosai," standing along the seaside in Ishikawa. The building has a "Hotel Shiosai" sign, and under it a "Shiosai Soba" banner stands, a rather rare arrangement where an Okinawa soba shop and a hotel are one 😆
Reception counter inside
Once inside, first a reception counter that looks like a hotel front desk greets you. Though I came to a soba shop, I get a curious feeling as if I'd stepped into a hotel lobby 😊
Inside the shop
Table seats inside the shop
Table seats inside the shop

The seating area has a spacious layout, as if the hotel lobby had simply been turned into a diner. When I visited, it was quite bustling with local customers. It feels like a shop loved by the community, which is reassuring.
Menu
The menu has a notice: "All menu items available for takeout!!" Bringing your own container is also welcome, and you can tell locals use it casually.
Soba menu

Here's that soba menu. The signature "Shiosai Soba" comes with all of soft-bone pork ribs, offal (nakami), and tebichi, at ¥1,080 regular and ¥1,180 large. The others, offal soba, tebichi soba, soft-bone pork rib soba, and braised pork belly soba, are all ¥880 regular and ¥980 large. And for +¥150 you can apparently switch to fresh noodles (limited quantity) 🤤
Soba menu continued
Beef tendon and bean sprout soba, meatless plain soba, and yushi-dofu soba are available too.
Limited-quantity menu

What also caught my eye was the limited-quantity "bone soup." With a small side dish and rice it's ¥700, and the bone soup soba is a great-value ¥780 regular. It ends when it runs out, so I'd like to aim for it next time.
Set meal, rice bowl, and a la carte menu
Set meals, rice bowls, a la carte items, and drinks are all available, so its range as a diner is wide too.
Shiosai Soba, large  ¥1,180

Now, this time I asked for the "Shiosai Soba," named after the shop, in the large size. This is what was brought out. A bowl with a big piece of tebichi, two large soft-bone pork ribs, offal, knotted kelp, and, unusually, even daikon radish, a bowl with seriously hearty volume ✨

First, the soup. Maybe it's a blended broth; it feels like the pork bone comes through firmly, but the liquid from the offal soup also seems to be mixed in, so honestly it was a complex flavor I couldn't pin down with a single word 😋
Shiosai Soba, large  ¥1,180
The noodles are thin, loosely wavy noodles, boiled on the soft side.

The toppings are really something, though. The tebichi is large, there are two big soft-bone pork ribs, plus offal and knotted kelp. Meeting daikon radish in Okinawa soba is quite rare, and it was a welcome little discovery 😄 Partly because I got the large, I was completely full by the time I finished.
Lodging information for Hotel Shiosai

And as I mentioned at the start, this is a hotel, so you can also stay without meals. A single room is ¥4,500 per night without meals, and a twin room is ¥8,000 (for 2 guests), quite reasonable. Thinking about it, being able to eat Okinawa soba and then stay right there may be a rather luxurious way to use it 🍶

Rating (9/15): A somewhat elusive soup, a blended broth with a strong pork-bone flavor mixed with the flavor of the offal soup. The noodles are thin, loosely wavy, and soft. With tebichi, two soft-bone pork ribs, offal, knotted kelp, and daikon radish, the volume of toppings is beyond complaint. My impression of the flavor itself was average, but its satisfying portions made it understandable why it's bustling with local customers 😊

天妃そば.name: Tenpi Soba
天妃そば.desc: An Okinawa soba specialty shop in Kume, Naha, a short walk from Asahibashi Station. The top-pick bone-in pork rib soba (small ¥650 / regular ¥800 / large ¥950) features soy-sauce-soaked ribs with medium-thick, loosely wavy noodles. It comes with a free jushi or inari, and is bustling with locals and foreign tourists.
t: On this Okinawa soba journey, I visited "Tenpi Soba" in Kume, Naha City 🍜 I ate here in June 2025 😄
Exterior of the shop

The shop's landmarks are the big "Okinawa Soba Specialty Shop" sign and a white noren curtain reading "Tenpi Soba." Greenery and flowers decorate the entrance area, giving off a somewhat nostalgic atmosphere 😊
Sign at the shop front

The big sign at the shop front reads "We're committed to the noodles, committed to the broth, and committed to the meat." Among them, the bone-in pork rib soba is described as "our top-pick bone-in meat. Once you try it, you'll be hooked!" so I had to order it 🤤
Ticket machine

You order at the ticket machine at the entrance. The bone-in pork rib soba comes in three sizes: small ¥650, regular ¥800, and large ¥950. Besides soft-bone pork rib soba, meat soba, and the greedy soba with lots on top, there's also curry rice, taco rice, and even zenzai.
Inside the shop
The interior has wooden floors and hanging lamps for a calm atmosphere. When I visited, in addition to locals, there were many foreign tourists, and it was quite bustling 😄
Bone-in pork rib soba, large  ¥950  * Inari service
This is the bone-in pork rib soba that was brought out. The nice thing is that a free jushi or inari comes with it as a service, and this day I chose the inari ✨
First, the soup. Maybe it's a blended broth; rather than either pork bone or bonito asserting itself strongly, the flavor was restrained overall 😋
Bone-in pork rib soba, large  ¥950
The noodles are medium-thick, loosely wavy noodles, boiled on the soft side.
The bone-in pork ribs are the type with soy sauce soaked in firmly. Some firm soft bone is mixed in and it's satisfying to eat, but I did feel a fair amount of sinewy texture ^^;

Rating (9/15): A blended broth where neither pork bone nor bonito is too assertive, with soft, medium-thick wavy noodles. The bone-in pork ribs are the type with soy sauce soaked in and some firm soft bone mixed in, with a sinewy texture. The free inari was a nice point, but my impression of the flavor itself is that it's average. Even so, it was a shop bustling with locals and foreign tourists, showing its popularity 😊

沖縄そばエッチャン.name: Okinawa Soba Etchan
沖縄そばエッチャン.desc: An Okinawa soba shop up the stairs on the second floor, near the south gate of the University of the Ryukyus in Uebaru, Nishihara. A pork-bone-forward blended broth with soft, thin straight noodles. The "Mix Soba" (¥950) comes with meltingly tender tebichi and soft-bone pork ribs whose texture varies between soy sauce and salt versions. Bustling with locals and construction workers.
t: On this Okinawa soba journey, I visited "Okinawa Soba Etchan" in Uebaru, Nishihara Town 🍜 I ate here in July 2025 😄
Exterior of the shop
Unfortunately it was raining that day. The photo ended up being taken through a window glass, but the landmarks are the "Etchan" sign and the stairs with red handrails ☔
The "Seared Salted Soft-Bone Pork Rib Soba" banner
Along the road there were banners for "Open" and "Seared Salted Soft-Bone Pork Rib Soba." Salted soft-bone pork ribs are intriguing 🤤
Entrance
The entrance is at the top of the stairs.
Ticket machine

You order at the ticket machine at the entrance. The Mix Soba is ¥950, and the set with jushi is ¥1,000. There's a wide variety of soba too: soft-bone pork rib soba, seared salted pork rib soba, braised pork belly soba, tebichi soba, yushi-dofu soba, and green onion soba. They're open from 11:00 to 16:00 and closed on Mondays and Tuesdays.
Notes on the table and self-service
The shop is self-service. Pickled red ginger and kōrēgūsu (chili-infused awamori) are on the table.
Counter seats
Table seats inside the shop
Inside the shop
The interior has counter seats and table seats, and when I visited it was bustling with local customers and construction workers. Shops with a lot of customers like this seem to rarely disappoint 😊
View from the window
Outside the window it was rainy. From the window seat you can see the road and greenery, which gives a relaxed feeling.
Mix Soba  ¥950
What I ordered this time was the "Mix Soba." It's a loaded bowl topped with tebichi, braised pork belly, and soft-bone pork ribs ✨
First, the soup. A blended broth with a pork-bone-forward flavor 😋
Mix Soba  ¥950
The noodles are thin and straight, boiled on the soft side. The noodles and soup go well together, and it's fairly tasty.

The tebichi topping is meltingly tender. What's interesting is the soft-bone pork ribs: the soy-sauce-based ones have firmer cartilage, while the salted soft-bone pork ribs have meltingly tender cartilage, so they vary the textures. It's quite a fun touch 😄 However, I felt a sinewy texture in the braised pork belly and soft-bone pork ribs ^^;

Rating (10/15): A pork-bone-forward blended broth with soft, thin straight noodles. The noodles and soup pair fairly well. There was thoughtfulness in the toppings too, with meltingly tender tebichi and soft-bone pork ribs whose texture changes between soy sauce and salt. The sinewy texture of the braised pork belly and soft-bone pork ribs bothered me, but the level was higher than I expected, and it was a fairly satisfying bowl 👌

そば処くんち.name: Soba-dokoro Kunchi
そば処くんち.desc: An Okinawa soba shop in Shuri Torihori-cho, Naha, near Shuri Station on the monorail. A pork-bone-based soup with soft, thin straight noodles. The "Kunchi Soba" (¥900) comes topped with firmly seasoned bone-in pork ribs and braised pork belly. Sanshin are lined up inside the shop, and you may get to hear the owner sing with the sanshin.
t: On this Okinawa soba journey, I visited "Soba-dokoro Kunchi" in Shuri, Naha City 🍜 I ate here in July 2025 😄
Exterior of the shop
It's a shop in a building along the street, near Shuri Station on the monorail.
Entrance
Sign with a photo of soba
Above the entrance is a "Soba-dokoro Kunchi" sign, and beside it hangs a sign with a photo of soba, so you can tell right away this is an Okinawa soba shop 😊
Ticket machine

You order at the ticket machine at the entrance. The signature Kunchi Soba is ¥900, and the set meal is ¥1,100. Others lined up include Okinawa soba, soki soba, tebichi soba, soft-bone pork rib soba, and jushi set meals.
Inside the shop
The interior has the feel of an old-fashioned diner, with a TV and noren curtains hanging. The only customers that day were a local student and me.
Kunchi Soba  ¥900
What I ordered this time was the "Kunchi Soba," named after the shop. A bowl topped with bone-in pork ribs and braised pork belly ✨
First, the soup. It has a pork-bone-based flavor 😋
Kunchi Soba  ¥900
The noodles are thin and straight, boiled on the soft side.
The bone-in pork ribs and braised pork belly toppings are both firmly seasoned and the type with a solid bite. The sinewy texture was clearly there too ^^;
A corner of the shop with sanshin lined up

And from here is what surprised me most at this shop. I'd been thinking there were quite a few sanshin lined up in one corner of the shop, when suddenly the owner performed singing with the sanshin for me 😅 I got to hear Asadoya Yunta and a few other songs 😅
The owner singing with the sanshin
Here's how it looked 🎶 Live music, unexpectedly, in the middle of a diner.
Bulletin board on the wall

On the wall are posted a "list of famous Ryukyuan sanshin," a newspaper clipping saying "the owner's sanshin performances are popular," and lots of photos of him holding a sanshin, so this is the shop's specialty. Since it's close to Shuri Station, it may be a welcome service for those visiting as tourists 😄

Rating (9/15): A pork-bone-based soup with soft, thin straight noodles. The bone-in pork ribs and braised pork belly were firmly seasoned, with a chewy, sinewy texture. My impression of the flavor itself is that it's average, but it was a shop where you can have an experience you can only get here: the owner's singing with the sanshin 😊

なかむら屋 浦添店.name: Nakamura-ya Urasoe
なかむら屋 浦添店.desc: An Okinawa soba shop in Yafuso, Urasoe, easy to spot by its yellow walls. A gentle blended broth with plenty of bonito, and you can choose between the newly introduced thin noodles or the classic flat noodles. The "Mix Soba (with jushi)" (¥1,100) comes with bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki) the size of giant spare ribs, plus generous pieces of braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) and soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki). Busy with local customers.
t: On my Okinawa soba journey, this time I visited "Nakamura-ya Urasoe" in Yafuso, Urasoe City 🍜 I ate here in July 2025 😄
The shop exterior
The landmark is the building with "Okinawa Soba" written in big letters on its yellow wall.
Signboards out front

In front of the entrance there was a sign saying "Limited to 5 servings a day — we've started yushi-dofu soba!" and a board of recommended dishes listing Mix Soba (with jushi), Mix Soba (with white rice) and hon-soki soba. They're open from 11:30 to 15:00, and closed on Sundays and Wednesdays.
Notice about the shop's parking
Parking is only in the spaces marked with a yellow sign reading "Nakamura-ya" in black letters. A notice asks you not to park anywhere else, so please be careful if you come by car 🚗
Ticket machine

You order at the ticket machine by the entrance. Mix Soba (with jushi) is ¥1,100 and Mix Soba (with rice) is ¥1,000. Other options include hon-soki soba ¥980, sanmai-niku soba ¥850, Okinawa soba ¥850, vegetable soba ¥880, yomogi (mugwort) soba ¥900 and yushi-dofu soba (large) ¥900.
Inside the shop
The kitchen and menu
Inside, tables are lined up in a calm, relaxed atmosphere. When I visited, it was busy with local customers 😊
A corner of the shop
In one corner, there was a board with a drawing of Okinawa soba and an "Okinawa Soba" banner on display.
Table sign about the thin noodles
"New thin noodles" poster

Here they've introduced "NEW thin noodles," so you can choose between the new thin noodles, made for easy eating, and the classic flat noodles, made for a satisfying bite. Asked "Which are you?" I was torn, but this time I went with the flat noodles.
Mix Soba (with jushi)　¥1,100

This time I ordered the "Mix Soba (with jushi)." It's a bowl topped with bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki), braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) and soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), served with jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice) ✨
First, the soup. It's a blended broth with a gentle flavor and plenty of bonito 😋
Mix Soba (with jushi)　¥1,100
The noodles are flat, cooked on the soft side.

What really surprised me was the hon-soki. It was a giant spare rib, and I couldn't help laughing 😅 It reminded me of "Nakama Shokudo" in Onna Village. The sanmai-niku and nankotsu soki were also big pieces, making this a seriously hearty bowl. That said, all of the meat had a sinewy texture ^^;
The jushi was lightly seasoned. Eating it together with the soba left me completely full.

Rating (9/15): A gentle blended broth with plenty of bonito, with soft flat noodles. The hon-soki was a giant spare rib, and the sanmai-niku and nankotsu soki were big too, so the portion was outstanding, but all of the meat had a sinewy texture. The taste itself was just average, I'd say, but it's a shop loved by the neighborhood, busy with local customers 😊
